q: Which element has the chemical symbol 'Fe'?
e: Iron borrowed its Fe name tag from ferrum, an old Latin word for this tough, trusty metal.

q: Which of the following is not one of the groups on the periodic table?
e: Fluorine is just one feisty element in the halogen family, so Fluorines is not a real group name.

q: Which element has the highest melting point?
e: Carbon hugs its tiny atoms so tightly that it can survive inside blazing heat where every other element melts away.

q: Which is the most abundant element in the universe?
e: Hydrogen was the universe's first creation, and it still fills nearly three-quarters of all space with starlight!

q: The element involved in making human blood red is which of the following?
e: Iron catches fresh oxygen in your blood and blushes bright red, painting every heartbeat with vibrant color!

q: Naturally occuring uranium primarily consists of which isotope?
e: Uranium-238 is the heavyweight champ that makes up over ninety-nine percent of all the natural uranium resting in the ground.

q: What is the common name of the chemical compound "dihydrogen monoxide"?
e: Dihydrogen monoxide is just a fancy science name for water, meaning two hydrogens hugging one oxygen!

q: Which gas forms about 78% of the Earth’s atmosphere?
e: Nitrogen quietly fills most of our sky, wrapping the whole world in a giant, invisible blanket.

q: Salt is 100% composed of Sodium.
e: That is false because table salt is a tasty friendship between sodium and chlorine, working as a team.

q: This element, when overcome with extreme heat and pressure, creates diamonds.
e: Deep underground, humble carbon atoms squeeze together in a giant warm hug until they sparkle into brilliant diamonds.

q: What is the elemental symbol for mercury?
e: Mercury borrows its symbol Hg from an ancient name meaning silver water, dancing around like shiny liquid metal.

q: Stars consist mainly of hydrogen and which other gas?
e: Stars cook hydrogen into heaps of helium, fueling their warm, fiery glow across the deep dark night.

q: Which noble gas has the lowest atomic number?
e: Helium floats at the very top of the noble gas family, proudly carrying an atomic number of just two.

q: Dry ice is the solid form of what substance?
e: Dry ice is really frozen carbon dioxide gas, skipping the messy puddle stage to vanish right back into chilly air!

q: What is the atomic mass of Carbon?
e: Carbon balances six protons and six neutrons inside its tiny heart, giving this busy life-builder an atomic mass of twelve.

q: What is the first element on the periodic table?
e: Light and cheerful hydrogen has just one proton, proudly leading the giant parade of elements at spot number one.

q: Which of these Elements is a metalloid?
e: Antimony is a metalloid because it acts like a magical mix, shining like metal but crumbling like rock.

q: Water always boils at 100°C, 212°F, 373.15K, no matter where you are.
e: This is false because high up on chilly mountains, lighter air lets water bubble and boil at lower temperatures.

q: An exothermic reaction is a chemical reaction that releases energy by radiating electricity.
e: This is false because exothermic reactions prefer to give off cozy heat and light, not sparks of electricity.

q: Who is the chemical element Curium named after?
e: Curium honors Marie and Pierre Curie, two brilliant partners who spent their lives unlocking the secrets of radioactivity.

q: What is the chemical symbol for Helium?
e: Helium simply borrows the first two letters of its cheerful name to get its symbol, He.

q: What is the chemical makeup of water?
e: Water is H2O because two eager hydrogen atoms team up with one oxygen atom to make every splashing drop.

q: What is the atomic number of the element Strontium?
e: Deep inside every strontium atom, thirty-eight cheerful protons keep its cozy center glowing bright with personality.

q: As a solid undergoes a phase change to a liquid state, it:
a: Releases heat while remaining at a constant temperature
Absorbs heat while remaining at a constant temperature
Releases heat as the temperature increases
Absorbs heat as the temperature increases
e: The solid drinks in warmth to break free from its icy pose, keeping its temperature perfectly still until it completely melts.

q: Which of the following is NOT true concerning pure liquid water:
a: it is a good solvent for simple sugars
it has a high specific heat
it is a requirement for all known life forms
the colder it gets the denser it gets from 100C to 0C
e: Water plays a funny trick below four degrees, fluffing outward and getting lighter instead of heavier as it freezes.

q: Food provides energy in what form?
e: Every crunchy bite of an apple packs hidden chemical energy, just waiting for your tummy to unlock its secret power!

q: Which of the following is the approximate percentage of the United States' total energy use supplied by oil, coal, and natural gas?
e: Oil, coal, and gas do the heavy lifting, powering about eighty-five percent of our giant, bustling country!

q: Calcium, strontium, and barium are commonly called what kind of elements?
e: Scientists call these friendly metallic cousins alkaline earth elements because ancient thinkers found them tucked inside ordinary rocks and dirt.

q: Which of the following is the function of the carbon rod that runs down the center of a dry cell?
a: To keep the chemical paste moist
To conduct electrons between materials involved in the chemical reaction
To break a circuit if it overheats
e: That tall carbon rod acts like a helpful bridge, guiding tiny electrons between materials to keep the battery running smoothly.

q: Scientists supported by the Department of Energy are studying electron transfer reactions in organic molecules. These molecules are typically used as what?
e: Because they pass electrons along like a friendly game of catch, these clever molecules work as molecular wires.

q: Which of the following types of energy transformation occurs in a lightbulb?
e: Zipping electrical energy journeys into a bulb and magically bursts into glowing, radiant light to chase away shadows.

q: A chemical change occurs when a substance:
e: When atoms trade tiny electrons, they transform from the very inside out, creating a brand-new chemical identity.

q: Stars are composed of a number of elements at their birth. Which of the following elements has the HIGHEST percent composition when a star is born?
e: Baby stars begin their glowing lives mostly made of hydrogen, the simplest fuel ready to light up the galaxy!

q: For a particular chemical reaction, delta H is negative and delta S is positive. Which of the following is true?
a: The reaction is spontaneous at any temperature
The reaction is only spontaneous when the temperature is greater than the heat of the reaction
The reaction is only spontaneous if the absolute value of delta H is greater than delta S
e: When a reaction gives off cozy warmth and creates happy chaos, nature eagerly lets it happen at any temperature!

q: You manufacture a chemical called Bowlinium that is a blue liquid at room temperature. You vigorously mix the Bowlinium with some yellow oil and clear water. Over time, two layers separate out: a green layer on top, and a clear layer on the bottom. Which of the following conclusions about this experiment is MOST correct?
a: Bowlinium is less dense than water
Bowlinium is more dense than water
Bowlinium is less dense than water and as dense as oil
Bowlinium has the same density as oil
e: Blue Bowlinium blended right into the yellow oil, floating together on top because they share the same density and are lighter than water.

q: Electrochemical batteries convert chemical energy directly into electrical energy. Would you expect the efficiency of an electrochemical battery, in general, to be more or less efficient in generating electrical energy than a gas-powered electrical generator?
a: The overall efficiency of a battery would be better than that of a gas-powered electrical generator
The overall efficiency of a battery would be worse than that of a gas-powered electrical generator
The overall efficiency of a battery would be the equal to that of a gas-powered electrical generator
e: Batteries skip the hot, noisy fuss of burning fuel, making them much more efficient than gas generators!

q: Charcoal created by pyrolysis [py-ROL-uh-sis] of biomass is referred to as which of the following?
e: When plants get baked without oxygen, they become rich, black biochar, a magical charcoal that helps garden soil thrive.

q: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of a decaying unstable isotope?
a: It is more chaotic than random
e: Decaying atoms pop off purely at random, following peaceful odds of probability instead of wild, messy chaos.

q: Which of the following is a chemical reaction?
e: Burning lamp oil creates glowing flames that turn the oil into brand-new substances like smoke and gas.

q: During a chemical reaction, which of the following will never occur?
e: Energy loves to change costumes into heat or light, but the universe never allows a single drop of it to disappear.

q: Which of the following is closest to the distance, in meters, between the electron and proton in the neutral hydrogen atom?
e: In tiny hydrogen, the whizzing electron stays about 10^-10 meters away from its proton partner.

q: Which of the following energy transformations occurs in your muscles when you jump into the air?
e: Your leg muscles unlock chemical energy from your food and transform it into bouncy kinetic energy to launch you skyward!

q: Kate sips some juice and notices that it is sour. What can she reasonably hypothesize about the juice?
a: It would likely neutralize with acetic acid
It would likely neutralize with muriatic acid
e: Acids love to tickle our tongues with a sharp, tangy zip, which gives sour juices their puckery punch.

q: Predict which object made of the following metal will sink in a pool of Mercury, which has a density 13.5 grams per cubic centimeter:
a: aluminum, which has a density of 2.6 grams per cubic centimeter
iron, which has a density of 7.9 grams per cubic centimeter
lead, which has a density of 11.34 grams per cubic centimeter
uranium, which has a density of 19.5 grams per cubic centimeter
e: Uranium is even denser than the liquid mercury, so it plunges straight to the very bottom.

q: Which of the following chemical processes combines methane with water to produce hydrogen gas and carbon monoxide?
e: Steam reforming uses a blast of super-hot water vapor to gently break methane apart into useful hydrogen gas and carbon monoxide.

q: A botanist observes pollen grains suspended in water jittering about in a random fashion. Another scientist observes similar random motion of coal dust on the surface of another liquid. These are commonly considered an examples of:
e: Pollen grains do a jittery dance called Brownian motion because invisible water molecules constantly bump them from every side.

q: In order to measure the current passing through an element in the circuit, we want to connect which of the following?
a: An ammeter in parallel with the element
A voltmeter in parallel with the element
An ammeter in series with the element
A voltmeter in series with the element
e: To count the rushing electric parade, the meter must stand right in the single-file line with the circuit.

q: A litmus paper test is used to determine:
a: whether a solution is acidic or basic
e: Litmus paper cleverly shifts color like a chameleon to reveal if a splash is sour acid or slippery base.

q: Which of the following is NOT a naturally occurring polymer?
e: Polymers are giant repeating chains, but sweet sucrose sugar is just a tiny pair of sugar rings.

q: For which of the following reasons is baking soda a good substance for putting out a grease fire?
a: It deprives the fire of oxygen
It removes all the components of a fire
e: When baking soda hits heat, it puffs out a blanket of gas that gently cuts off the fire's oxygen.

q: J. J. Thomson primarily used what instrument to discover electrons:
e: Thomson zapped glowing beams through a glass cathode ray tube to discover tiny zooming electrons!

q: Researchers at SLAC National Accelerator Lab are using an x-ray free-electron laser to study changes molecules undergo when interacting with light. Which of the following biological processes depends most strongly on the interaction of light with molecules?
e: In photosynthesis, hungry little leaves reach out to catch zooming sunbeams, turning pure light into yummy food to grow big and strong!

q: In the periodic table, Potassium's symbol is the letter K.
e: It is true, because potassium borrows the letter K from its historic name, kalium, to keep things fun.

q: An aspiring science student has a quantity of an unknown liquid in an unmarked, irregularly-shaped container. If a hydrometer [high-DRAW-meh-tur] reads 1.0 after being placed in the liquid, what other physical property of the liquid could be used to obtain the volume of liquid in the container?
e: Since the hydrometer gives density, weighing the liquid's mass lets you easily unlock its secret volume.

q: The position of an element in the periodic table is determined by its:
e: Elements line up neatly on their colorful chart by atomic number, counting the cheerful protons tucked inside each one.

q: Which of the following observations would show that soil has a high pH?
a: When mixed with wet baking soda, it forms carbon dioxide
It turns red litmus paper blue
It turns blue litmus paper red
e: Soil with a high pH is a base, and like a cheerful magic trick, bases turn red litmus paper bright blue.

q: What are the percentages of ethanol used in the fuel of a regular vehicle and a flexible fuel vehicle (FFV), respectively?
e: Regular cars sip fuel with just ten percent ethanol, but special flex-fuel cars can happily gulp down blends with eighty-five percent!

q: Which of the following is a characteristic of all strong acids?
e: The moment strong acids dive into water, all their tiny parts joyfully let go and split completely apart.

q: Metals A and B are both used in a circuit. Given that the temperatures of A and B are the same, and that metal A is a better conductor of heat than metal B, which of the following is necessarily true?
a: The current across A is greater than the current across B
The voltage across A is greater than the voltage across B
A has a higher resistivity than B
A has a lower resistivity than B
e: Metals that guide heat easily also let electric current glide smoothly, meaning metal A resists the flow less.

q: Hydrogen bonding is NOT important in the physical and chemical properties of:
e: Methane particles are too shy to make sticky hydrogen bonds, so they just float freely past one another.

q: Why does the pressure exerted by a gas against a sealed container increase as the temperature increases?
a: The gas molecules move faster and strike the container wall more frequently
The gas molecules gain more entropy and hence produce more pressure
The gas molecules generate more collision energy
The increased kinetic energy increases the rate of chemical reactions between gas particles
e: When gas warms up, its tiny particles get super energetic and zoom around, bumping into the walls much more often.

q: Which of the following is a Bronsted base, but not an Arrhenius [ah-REE-nee-us] base?
e: Triethylamine happily scoops up loose protons like a Bronsted base, but lacks any hydroxide to release as an Arrhenius base.

q: How many states in the US mined coal in 2013?
e: In 2013, exactly twenty-five states dug underground, meaning precisely half of America was busy scooping up black coal from the earth.

q: As you walk, which of the following forces is the most directly responsible for propelling you forward?
a: The normal force of the ground on your foot
The force of your foot pushing on the ground
The friction between your foot and the ground
The reaction force of the ground on your foot
e: Every time your shoe nudges backward, the trusty ground gives you an equal push forward to send you marching!

q: Which of the following best describes the following reaction: 2Mg + O2 2MgO
e: When magnesium and oxygen hold hands to become one shiny team, they combine into a single partnership called a combination reaction.

q: Which of the following is NOT part of clean coal technology?
e: While clean coal scrubs out soot and sulfur, nitrogen capture is not part of the plan because nitrogen is harmless air.

q: How would you turn carbon-12 into the isotope carbon-13?
e: To give carbon a tiny bit more heft without changing who it is, just sneak in one extra neutral little neutron!

q: Which of the following four processes is endothermic?
e: An ice cube melts by drinking in warmth from the air, making it an endothermic heat-sponge.

q: Which of the following has the GREATEST kinetic energy for an object moving in a straight path:
a: a mass of 2 kg with a velocity of 10 meters per second
a mass of 4 kg with a velocity of 8 meters per second
a mass of 6 kg with a velocity of 6 meters per second
a mass of 8 kg with a velocity of 4 meters per second
e: Because speed gets multiplied by itself, four kilograms zooming at eight meters per second packs the biggest energetic punch.

q: In general, metals do NOT have which of the following properties?
e: Metals are happy sharers that let electrons wander off, so they do not cling to them with high affinity.

q: What is responsible for the luster, conductivity and ductility [duk-TIL-ih-tee] of metals?
a: The position on the periodic table
The number of protons in the metal
e: In metallic bonds, friendly electrons swim in a shared sea, letting metals bend, shine, and zip electricity along easily.

q: Which of the following has the most inertia:
e: Inertia is just how stubborn an object is against moving, and four kilograms of iron has the most mass to shove.

q: Which of the following defines a pure substance that cannot be broken down by any chemical means?
e: An element is nature's purest building block, so wonderfully simple that no chemical reaction can break it down any further.

q: Chemical bonding between which of the following pairs of atoms would MOST likely be ionic:
e: Copper the metal happily gives an electron to chlorine the nonmetal, creating a strong, magnetic ionic hug.

q: Which of the following functional groups replaces a hydrogen in an alcohol:
e: To make an alcohol, a cheerful hydroxyl group of oxygen and hydrogen steps in to replace a lonely hydrogen.

q: When magnesium and zinc bromide are combined, zinc and magnesium bromide are formed according to the reaction, Mg + ZnBr2 Zn + MgBr2. Which of the following types of reactions has occurred:
e: Magnesium cheerfully cuts in to steal bromide as a partner, leaving lonely zinc to dance all by itself in a single replacement!

q: Which of the following explains the size of a chloride ion compared to that of a chlorine atom?
a: Chloride is smaller because it has fewer electrons
Chloride is smaller because it has more electrons
Chloride is larger because it has fewer electrons
Chloride is larger because it has more electrons
e: Gaining an extra electron makes chlorine puff out its cloud for elbow room, so the chloride ion is noticeably larger.

q: Which of the following is NOT true for a substance:
a: pure substances always contain the same ratio of elements
water and steam are 2 different forms of the same substance
all compounds are substances and all substances are compounds
a pure substance cannot be separated by physical means
e: Pure elements like shiny gold are true substances, but they are not compounds because they have only one ingredient!

q: Which of the following statements is true regarding resonance?
a: A molecule will equilibrate through its resonance structures
The nitrate ion has three valid resonance structures
Sigma bonds are most often involved in resonance
e: Nitrate shares its bonds equally among three oxygen friends, so it gets drawn in three different, equally real ways.

q: The plum pudding model of the atom was based on which of the following observations?
a: When alpha particles are fired at the nucleus, some bounce back
Light given off by elements in a flame test has discrete wavelengths
Alpha particles can knock positive particles from nuclei
e: Scientists discovered tiny negative particles and imagined them scattered like sweet raisins inside a puffy, positive pudding.

q: Bernoulli's equation describes which of the following?
e: Bernoulli figured out the secret dance of fluids, describing how liquids swirl and how air rushes under soaring airplane wings.

q: Which of the following types of biomass energy do we use the most in the United States?
e: Cozy wood has fueled human fires forever, making it the most used biomass energy in America!

q: A space heater converts what forms of energy?
e: A space heater drinks electrical energy from the wall and transforms it into toasty heat to warm chilly toes.

q: Although this is dangerous, if you hypothetically were to breathe in xenon or krypton instead of helium, what would happen to the sound of your voice?
a: It would be lower than when you breathe helium and also lower than your regular voice
It would be lower than when you breathe helium, but higher than your regular voice
It would be the same as when you breathe helium
It would be higher than when you breathe helium
e: Heavy xenon gas slows sound waves down like molasses, turning your voice into a deep, rumbling giant’s growl.

q: An electron is emitted by an atomic nucleus in the process of:
e: During beta decay, an eager neutron transforms and zips a brand-new electron right out of the nucleus like a shooting star.

q: Which of the following engines runs using the Otto, spelled O-T-T-O, cycle?
e: Gasoline engines run on the Otto cycle, playfully sparking fuel and air to give cars their everyday vroom!

q: Which of the following is a transition metal?
e: Iron lives right in the busy center of the periodic table, where all the colorful transition metals hang out.

q: Which of the following is the BEST description of the arrangement of the magnetic domains of an unmagnetized iron bar:
a: all are aligned at 180 to each other
all are aligned at 90 to each other
there are no magnetic domains in this case
e: Without a magnet to guide them, tiny magnetic pockets point in random directions like sleepy puppies.

q: During normal chemical reactions, although the combinations of atoms that form molecules can change, the total number of atoms must remain the same. This is called:
a: the law of conservation of matter
e: Nature never misplaces its building blocks, so the law of conservation of matter ensures every atom is safely kept.

q: Which of the following real gases would behave most like an ideal gas at room temperature and pressure?
e: Tiny hydrogen molecules are so small and light that they zip around without sticking to each other at all.

q: Brookhaven National Lab is researching how to tether catalysts to chromophores for artificial photosynthesis. Which of the following is most similar in function to a chromophore?
e: Just like colorful dye soaks up light to brighten your shirt, a chromophore’s special job is catching sunlight too.

q: The U.S. Energy Information Administration is projecting that primary energy consumption of which of the following energy sources will grow by more than 4% per year between 2007 and 2035?
e: Liquid biofuels made from sunny crops are projected to grow over four percent each year as the world zooms toward cleaner energy!

q: Which of the following molecules contains the largest bond angle?
e: Carbon dioxide stretches out in a perfectly straight line, making a giant, wide-open 180-degree angle between its atoms.

q: When plotting the energy of the components of a slow reaction, such as the conversion of diamond into graphite, versus the reaction progress, which of the following best represents the shape of the curve?
e: Atoms must climb an energetic little mountain called activation energy before rolling downhill, making a peak in the middle.

q: Which country has the largest proven coal reserves?
e: Tucked beneath its rolling hills, the United States holds more proven coal than any other country on Earth.

q: In general terms, an electric generator converts which of the following?
e: A generator catches mechanical motion, like a spinning wheel, and magically transforms all that hustle into sparkling electrical power.

q: Phosphorus pentachloride [penta-KLOOR-ide] gas is in a container in which it is in equilibrium with liquid phosphorous trichloride [try-KLOOR-ide] and chlorine gas. Which of the following statements would be true if the pressure inside the container were doubled by adding argon gas, holding the temperature constant?
a: The amount of chlorine gas would increase
The amount of chlorine gas would decrease
The amount of chlorine gas would remain the same
e: Argon is just a quiet bystander that ignores the other gases. Because it never joins their dance, the amount of chlorine gas stays the same!

q: Analysts at Los Alamos National Laboratory have shown how to minimize environmental impacts by refracturing shale gas wells. Which of the following is not an environmental benefit of refracturing?
a: Fewer wells need to be drilled
Natural gas is more efficiently removed from each well
Carbon dioxide is deposited in a form of carbon sequestration
Natural gas does not release harmful byproducts
e: Even though refracturing saves wells, burning natural gas still puffs out pollution, so it definitely produces harmful byproducts.

q: A permanent magnet has magnetic properties due to which of the following?
a: The magnetic fields of its electrons are balanced
Magnetic monopoles accumulate at the ends
The magnetic domains have parallel magnetizations
Its magnetic dipole moment is zero
e: Inside a permanent magnet, millions of tiny magnetic neighborhoods line up side by side, marching in the exact same direction.

q: Which of the following devices would need a step- up transformer to work properly in your home?
e: Old tube televisions need a huge boost of electric energy to paint glowing pictures on the screen, stepping the voltage way up!

q: Which of the following is closest to the diameter, in meters, of the nucleus of a zinc atom?
e: A zinc nucleus is unimaginably tiny, measuring ten to the minus fourteen meters across. It is like a speck of dust inside a giant stadium!

q: Which of the following metals is often used to transform a sheet of regular glass into a mirror:
e: Shiny silver loves bouncing light so much that a thin coat on glass reflects your smiling face right back!

q: Which of the following is NOT an acid-base conjugate pair?
e: True acid-base partners differ by only one single proton, but these two strangers are not even close family.

q: Which of the following phases of matter has atoms or molecules that assume the shape of their container and are NOT easily compressible?
e: Liquids love sloshing into the shape of any container, but their closely packed molecules stubbornly refuse to be squished smaller.

q: Although none of the following are concrete proof of a chemical change, which of the following definitely could NOT be used as an indication that a chemical change has occurred?
e: Snapping a crayon makes it smaller without changing what it is, showing that size changes are physical, not chemical!

q: The majority of nuclear fission technology currently utilizes what group of elements on the periodic table?
e: Power plants love the actinide family because heavyweight members like uranium are eager to split apart and share their tremendous energy.

q: Isotopes of the same element differ in the number of which of the following particles?
e: Think of isotopes as look-alike sibling atoms: they share the exact same protons, but carry different numbers of quiet neutrons.

q: When using the periodic chart, what number gives the number of protons in a given element:
e: Think of the atomic number as an element's official badge, proudly counting every single proton tucked inside its cozy heart.

q: Radiocarbon dating is a commonly used technique for determining the age of organic material. Which of the following numbers is closest to the age, in years, after which organic material is unsuitable for carbon dating?
e: After about 50,000 years, a fossil runs out of its special ticking carbon, leaving no clues behind for scientists to count.

q: Which of the following energy sources emits the greatest amount of mercury into the atmosphere when it is combusted?
e: Burning dirty coal wakes up trapped mercury hidden inside the rock, puffing far more of it into our skies.

q: The length of a meter was re-defined in 1983 to be based on what physical quantity?
a: The distance light travels in a specific fraction of a second in a vacuum
The length of a one-kilogram bar of iridium [ih-RID-ee-um]
A specific fraction of the length of the meridian through Paris from the North Pole to the Equator
e: Scientists timed zooming light, defining a meter by the tiny fraction of a second it takes to race across space.

q: Which of the following molecules is an alkene [AL- keen]?
e: With two carbons sharing a special double-bond handshake, C2H4 happily belongs to the family of molecules called alkenes.

q: Which of the following statements is LEAST accurate regarding states of matter:
a: gases can be made of a single element
matter on Earth is never in a plasma state
e: Lightning bolts sizzle with fiery plasma right here on Earth, so plasma is definitely not missing from our world!

q: Which of the following is NOT a salt:
e: Potassium hydroxide carries a slippery hydroxide piece that makes it a powerful base instead of a true salt!

q: Currently, almost all used nuclear fuel from power plants in the U.S. is stored at which of the following?
e: Used fuel stays right at home where it was made, resting safely in heavy steel casks at the power plant.

q: Which of the following is the current carrier in a typical electrical conductor:
e: Electric current flows when restless little electrons wander freely through the metal, passing energy along like a merry relay team.

q: Your friend rubs a balloon on your head and your hair sticks to the balloon due to static electricity. This occurs because which of the following particles has been exchanged between your hair and the balloon?
e: Tiny, restless electrons leap from your hair onto the balloon, leaving your strands reaching up for a high five!

q: Which of the following is NOT true about mechanical energy?
a: Mechanical energy represents the sum of an object's kinetic and potential energies in a mechanical system
Mechanical energy possesses energy stored in fuel
Objects possess mechanical energy if they are in motion
An object that possesses mechanical energy is able to do work
e: Fuel actually holds chemical energy, not mechanical energy, which is too busy jumping and moving to snooze inside a gas tank.

q: An astronomer is observing a gas cloud and notes several infrared spectral lines. These spectral lines could allow the astronomer to infer what?
a: The elemental composition of the cloud
The chemical bonds present in the cloud
The rate of collision of the molecules in the cloud
The ionization state of the atoms in the cloud
e: Infrared light reveals the tiny chemical bonds holding molecules together, wiggling and dancing like happy little springs out in space!

q: Gay-Lussac's [LOO-saks] Law would be most useful for determining temperature changes of a gas in which of the following situations?
a: Within a balloon as it is filled
e: A sturdy sealed soda can cannot change its size, perfectly trapping gas so temperature and pressure rise together.

q: Which of the following acids has the smallest dipole moment?
e: Iodine shares electrons much more evenly with hydrogen than its greedy cousins, giving hydroiodic acid the smallest dipole moment.

q: The energy stored in a candle that can be changed into heat and light energy in burning is what type of energy?
e: Wax locks up chemical energy inside its tiny parts, patiently waiting for a spark to turn it into dancing heat and light!

q: In a fission nuclear reactor, which of the following processes occurs, resulting in released energy?
e: Speedy little neutrons bump right into hefty uranium atoms, cracking them open to release bursts of cozy heat energy.

q: What polymer is used to make CDs, safety goggles and riot shields?
e: Polycarbonate is tough yet crystal clear, making it perfect for shields that take hard hits without breaking!

q: Which of the following is a terminal for a battery?
e: An anode is like a busy doorway on a battery, letting zippy little electrons rush out to power up your favorite gadgets.

q: The ionosphere is a region of ionized gas in the upper atmosphere. The ionosphere is extremely important to:
a: The ability of satellites to orbit earth
e: This high-flying blanket of electric air bounces radio whispers around the curve of the Earth, helping our voices travel far.

q: Research at Argonne National Laboratory has been done on nuclear fuel recycling. After a nuclear fuel rod has been removed from a reactor, which of the following is closest to the percentage of the unused uranium that is still present in the rod and could be recycled?
e: Used fuel rods are still packed with power! About 95 percent of the uranium stays untouched, patiently waiting for another turn to shine.

q: When water is electrolyzed, what collects at the anode?
e: Electricity splits water apart, sending cheerful oxygen bubbles straight up to the positive anode to greet the world.

q: Which of the following resulted in petroleum?
a: Dead organisms packed together for millions of years
e: Long ago, microscopic critters settled underground, and millions of years of cozy squishing baked them into rich petroleum.

q: Which of the following is NOT evidence that supports the notion of Snowball Earth?
a: Stable concentrations of atmospheric carbon dioxide
e: During Snowball Earth, carbon dioxide swung on a wild rollercoaster to freeze our world, so steady levels could never be evidence.

q: Scientists at SLAC [slack] are studying excited state proton transfers by using light produced in the Linac [LIH-nak] Coherent Light Source to excite molecules of 2-thiopyridone [two-thigh-oh-PEER-id-own]. Their observations are most relevant to what system?
e: By watching how bright light shakes up these tiny molecules, scientists learn how harsh ultraviolet rays can harm our delicate DNA.

q: Which of the following is a property that is shared by both mixtures and compounds?
a: They always contain the same ratio of component atoms
They consist of atoms bound together
They retain many of the properties of their components
They can be broken down into their individual components
e: Whether atoms are glued tight or just mingled together, both mixtures and compounds can be untangled back into their separate pieces.

q: Which of the following types of coal is produced in the smallest amount in the U.S.?
e: Shiny, rock-hard anthracite is the rarest treasure among coals, which is why America digs up the smallest amount of it.

q: Acids are often defined as proton donors. Which of the following is the common form of this proton:
e: When a friendly acid gives away a proton, it is simply sharing a tiny, positively charged hydrogen ion.

q: Which of the following best explains why clouds appear white, but liquid water is transparent?
e: Billions of tiny water droplets bounce sunlight in every direction, scattering all the colors together into one fluffy, bright white blanket.

q: Which of the following is the BEST evidence that light travels as a wave:
a: a metal that is heated produces different colors
passing light through two pinholes can produce an interference pattern
light has a constant speed in a vacuum
e: Light rippling through two tiny holes overlaps like pond waves, creating striped interference patterns that prove it travels as waves.

q: Burning which of the following produces the least amount of carbon dioxide per unit of energy?
e: Burning natural gas keeps the sky a bit clearer by puffing out less carbon dioxide than coal or oil.

q: Which of the following BEST describes the following reaction: 2CaO 2Ca + O2
e: Just like a block tower tumbling apart into separate pieces, this reaction is a decomposition because one big compound splits into smaller parts.

q: Which of the following mixtures is made of liquids that are miscible?
e: Gasoline is a smooth team of different liquids blending together so seamlessly that they never separate into layers.

q: Which of the following is NOT considered a rare earth element?
e: Heavy uranium lives in its own energetic family of elements, so it is not counted among the rare earth group.

q: Which of the following does NOT describe ideal fluid flow?
e: An ideal fluid glides effortlessly with zero stickiness, so it is never thick or viscous like honey.

q: The reaction of hydrocarbons found in such things as wood and paper with oxygen to produce carbon dioxide, water and heat is called:
e: Combustion is the crackling dance where fuel meets oxygen to release cozy heat, water, and puffs of carbon dioxide.

q: Which of the following forces is felt by an electron with charge e between two parallel plates with area A, carrying a potential difference V, separated by a distance d?
e: The electric push equals voltage divided by distance, so multiplying by the electron's charge gives eV over d.

q: Which of the following factors does NOT impact the vapor pressure of a liquid in a closed container?
a: The molecular composition of the liquid
The surface area of the liquid in contact with the gas
The intermolecular forces between the molecules in the liquid
e: Whether a puddle is wide or narrow, the trapped gas pushes back with the exact same vapor pressure.

q: Compared to almost all other types of waves, electromagnetic waves are unique because they can travel through what?
e: Electromagnetic waves do not need anything to ride on, happily surfing right across the empty vacuum of space!

q: Using the International System of Units, which of the following units would be most appropriate to express force?
e: Every push and pull gets counted in newtons, named for the clever thinker who wondered why apples fall from trees.

q: Which of the following BEST describes electrostatic induction?
a: It is caused by the influence of nearby charged objects
It occurs between two charged objects
It transfers electrons from a charged object to a neutral object
It produces voltage across a conductor by means of a magnetic field
e: Without even touching, a charged object can nudge charges inside a neighbor just by hovering nearby, which is electrostatic induction at work.

q: Which of the following molecules has the highest dipole moments?
e: Greedy fluorine tugs electrons away from hydrogen with unmatched strength, giving hydrogen fluoride the mightiest dipole moment of all.

q: Which of the following cannot be classified within the classical three states of matter?
e: Liquid crystals cannot pick a side, flowing like a liquid while staying neatly lined up like a solid!

q: In a regenerative fuel cell system, the byproducts of a fuel cell are utilized to do which of the following?
a: Provide power to a solar energy system
Provide power to a wind energy system
Produce reactants that are resupplied to the fuel cell via electrolysis
e: Talk about the ultimate recycler! Using electrolysis, this clever system zaps its leftovers right back into fresh fuel to use again.

q: Which of the following elements has the highest first ionization energy?
e: Hugging its electrons tighter than all its neighbors, chlorine is the stingiest, needing the most energy to let go.

q: On the periodic table of elements, elements in the same column have which of the following in common?
e: Elements standing in the very same column act like close siblings, sharing similar properties and friendly chemical habits.

q: DOE scientists are studying nanowires as a potential high-surface area conductor in lithium-ion batteries. The high surface area makes these materials most suitable for what part of the battery?
e: All that extra surface gives roaming electrical charges tons of room to dock, making nanowires a dream home for the battery's hardworking cathode!

q: Which of the following is an example of a chemical change?
e: That crispy black crust on burnt toast is brand-new stuff, and no matter what you try, you can never un-toast it!

q: According to molecular orbital theory, which of the following molecules contains pi bonds?
e: Two nitrogen atoms hug tightly with a strong triple bond, which packs two special pi bonds right between them.

q: Andy is driving a car and has a reaction time of 0.5 seconds. He is driving at a constant speed of 20 meters per second when he sees a deer 50 meters in front of him. If he decelerates at a rate of 6 meters per second squared, how far away, to the nearest meter, from the deer will he stop?
e: Andy rolls ten meters before braking, then slides thirty-three more, stopping safely just seven meters away from the deer!

q: What is the density given as specific gravity, of a one centimeter cube of a metal that weighs 5 grams:
e: Since one cubic centimeter of water weighs one gram, this five-gram metal cube is exactly five times denser.

q: Which of the following would be the most logical instrument to use when a small amount of suspended particles must be separated from a liquid:
e: A centrifuge acts like a super-fast merry-go-round, spinning liquid until every tiny floating speck settles to the bottom.

q: Which of the following elements has the largest atomic weight?
e: Aluminum packs twenty-seven heavy particles in its center, easily outweighing lighter pals like neon, nitrogen, and lithium.

q: Alkali metals like sodium give up electrons when forming ionic bonds. In these ionic compounds, what is their typical oxidation number?
e: Giving away one negative electron leaves these friendly metals with a tidy positive 1 charge.

q: In most developing countries excluding China and India, which of the following is the primary source of energy for household energy consumption in rural and poor areas?
e: To cook dinner, families gather humble tree branches and plant scraps, called biomass, because nature leaves this fuel right in their backyards.

q: Which of the following processes can best be used to separate a mixture of miscible liquids?
e: Distillation gently warms the liquid friends until the most eager one boils away first, easily parting the pair.

q: Which of the following solutions will conduct electricity the best?
e: Salt splits into eager little charged ions in water, building a bustling bridge for electricity to zoom across!

q: What component of the air does humidity measure?
e: On sticky summer days, humidity simply measures the invisible water vapor floating around and tickling your nose.

q: An atom of radon-222 loses an alpha particle to become a more stable atom of which of the following?
e: By tossing away two protons in an alpha particle, heavy radon changes its identity and becomes calmer polonium.

q: What type of reaction combines an acid and a base to form a salt and water?
e: When a feisty acid and a slippery base meet, they cancel each other out, neutralizing into harmless salt and water.

q: Why are alkaline [AL-kuh-lyn] batteries NOT always recyclable?
a: They may contain absorbent glass material
e: Some alkaline batteries hide poisonous mercury inside like a messy villain, making them too hazardous for ordinary recycling bins.

q: What state produces the most coal in the U.S.?
e: Beneath Wyoming's wide-open plains sits an enormous buried treasure of coal, producing more than any other state in America.

q: Which of the following best explains the benefit of adding a solution of ethylene glycol, or antifreeze, to the radiator of a car:
a: lowers the freezing point and raises the boiling point
raises the freezing point and raises the boiling point
lowers the freezing point and lowers the boiling point
raises the freezing point and lowers the boiling point
e: Antifreeze keeps engines cozy, lowering the freezing point so coolant never turns to ice and raising the boiling point against overheating.

q: Two electrons can occupy the same orbital if what value is different?
e: Two electron roommates can share the same cozy space only if their spin numbers point them twirling in opposite directions!

q: Theoretically, an absolute maximum of how many ATP molecules can be produced from the complete oxidation of one glucose molecule through aerobic respiration?
e: By squeezing every drop of energy from a single sugar molecule, a busy cell can craft up to 38 little ATP batteries.

q: What is the purpose of a confirmation well?
a: To verify that the site will physically support a drilling platform
To verify that the oil is accessible
To verify that a formation has enough hydrocarbons to make it worth developing
To verify that the cost of extricating the oil will not be too high
e: This special well acts like a curious scout, double-checking deep underground to make sure there is enough oil to be worth digging up!

q: Which of the following is central to the Lewis definition of acids and bases?
a: Acids donate hydrogen ions, while bases accept hydrogen ions
Acids produce hydrogen ions, while bases produce hydroxide ions
Acids donate protons, while bases accept protons
Acids accept electron pairs, while bases donate electron pairs
e: Lewis saw chemistry as an electron party where greedy acids accept electron pairs and generous bases share them.

q: Jan tosses a football to Nick by exerting a force on the ball with her arm. According to Newton's Third Law, what is the reaction force that opposes Jan's exertion?
a: Jan's arm exerts a force on her body
The football exerts a force on Jan's arm
The football exerts a force on Nick's arm when he catches it
Nick's arm exerts a force on his body when he catches it
e: Every push has an equal partner! As Jan launches the football forward, the ball gently pushes right back against her arm.

q: The dynamic equilibrium [ee-kwuh-LIB-ree-uhm] of a reaction is best characterized by which of the following?
a: Equal amounts of products, enzymes, and reactants
The forward rate of reaction has reached the maximum rate
The forward and reverse rates of reaction are equal
e: It is like a bustling dance where dancers swap partners forward and backward at the exact same speed, keeping everything perfectly balanced.

q: The particles in an atom that determine which element it is are the:
e: Protons are an atom's special name tag, because the exact number of these tiny pals decides which element it gets to be.

q: A discharged capacitor is connected to a DC battery. One-half second after the connection is made, an ammeter in line with the capacitor shows that the current is 1.2 amps. As you continue to watch the ammeter, what will you see?
a: The current will remain constant at 1.2 amps
The current will stay constant at 1.2 amps and then rapidly drop to zero
The current will slowly increase to a maximum and then slowly decrease to zero
The current will steadily decrease to zero
e: As the capacitor fills up with electric charge like a crowded room, new charges slow down until current steadily drops to zero.

q: Research at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory is aimed at reducing methane emissions. According to the Energy Information Administration, which of the following fractions is closest to the estimate of the 100-year net global warming potential of methane?
e: Tiny methane gas packs a mighty punch, trapping enough heat to cause about one-fourth of our planet's warming over a century.

q: Which of the following is generally NOT true:
a: the boiling point of water decreases with increased altitude on Earth
the melting point of table salt is much higher than that of glucose
metals react with nonmetals to form new metals
e: When metals team up with nonmetals, they transform into ionic salts instead of making another metal.

q: A C-H bond is an example of what type of bonding?
e: Carbon and hydrogen become best pals by sharing their outer electrons, hugging tight in a friendly covalent bond.

q: Which of the following is an advantage of using biomass in the form of corn to produce ethanol?
a: Using corn to produce ethanol means that the U.S. will no longer need to import petroleum- based products
Corn-based ethanol is more fuel efficient than gasoline
Corn-based ethanol production has little impact on water supply
Food for cattle is produced when corn grain is converted to ethanol
e: When corn gets turned into fuel, the leftover grain becomes a tasty dinner for hungry cows!

q: The electron volt is a measure of which of the following?
e: Even with "volt" in its name, it actually measures the tiny punch of energy a zooming electron carries.

q: In a circuit, electrons and electric current flow in what respective directions?
a: Negative to positive; negative to positive
Negative to positive; positive to negative
Positive to negative; positive to negative
Positive to negative; negative to positive
e: Tiny electrons march from negative to positive, while electric current was famously drawn traveling the opposite way, from positive to negative.

q: Which of the following is the correctly balanced equation for the electrolysis of water?
e: When electricity zaps water, two water molecules split evenly into two hydrogen pairs and one oxygen pair.

q: Which of the following scientific principles is based on the conservation of electric charge?
e: Every electric charge marching into a crossroad must march back out, because charges can never just vanish into thin air.

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the properties of the plasma state of matter?
a: It doesn't respond to electromagnetic forces
e: Plasma is buzzing with free electrons and ions, which makes it eagerly dance whenever magnetic or electric forces tug on it.

q: Which of the following atomic properties most directly determines that elements in the same group of the Periodic Table have similar chemical properties:
e: Elements in the same family have matching outer electrons, and those tiny helpers decide how they greet other chemicals.

q: In Thomson's experiments with cathode ray tubes, he noted that the presence of a magnet caused the cathode rays to bend. What did he conclude from this observation?
a: Cathode rays are made of charged particles
Cathode rays are made of electrons
Cathode rays are less massive than the hydrogen atom
e: Magnets only push around things that carry an electric charge, so the bending rays proved they were full of tiny charged travelers!

q: Which of the following is NOT a spontaneous reaction under normal atmospheric pressure:
a: rusting of a ship's hull at sea
liquid water changing to water ice at 25C
the combustion of propane in air
e: Water loves staying liquid in a warm room, so it will never freeze into ice cubes at twenty-five degrees Celsius all by itself.

q: Which of the following is introduced at the cathode of a hydrogen fuel cell?
e: Fresh oxygen swoops in at the cathode to greet waiting hydrogen travelers, joining together to make clean water.

q: Formation of a precipitate is one sign that a chemical reaction has occurred. Which of the following is most likely to precipitate in water?
e: Sulfides are shy around water, preferring to clump tightly with metals and settle to the bottom as solid flakes!

q: A balanced chemical equation must possess which of the following?
a: The same number of molecules on both sides of the equation
The same kinds of molecules on both sides of the equation
The same number of each kind of atom on both sides of the equation
The same leading coefficient on both sides of the equation
e: Atoms love fair play, so a balanced equation keeps the exact same number of each atom on both sides.

q: Amino acids all contain an amine group and what other group?
e: Every amino acid loves balance, carrying a friendly amine group on one side and a trusty carboxyl group on the other.

q: If the temperature of a gaseous medium through which a sound wave passes is decreased, what will happen to the speed of the wave?
e: Chilly air makes gas molecules sluggish, so they pass sound along more slowly, decreasing the wave's speed.

q: Of solids, liquids, and gases,which of them can conduct thermal energy?
e: Atoms everywhere love passing the warmth along, so solids, liquids, and gases can all share thermal energy by bumping together.

e: The solution swallows up warm orange light, letting only cool, dancing blue rays bounce into your eyes.

q: What gas is most common in the atmosphere of Venus?
e: Venus wraps itself in a thick blanket made mostly of carbon dioxide, trapping heat like a giant oven!

q: Which of the following statements about sound is not true?

The speed of sound is not dependent on the density of the medium
The speed of sound depends on the temperature of the medium
e: Sound waves actually do care about density, moving faster or slower depending on how tightly packed the particles are.

e: A heterogeneous mixture is like a wild salad where every bite is different, because its parts never fully blend together.

e: Boiling gooey crude oil separates its ingredients by temperature, letting each useful fuel gently bubble up into its own layer.

q: Which of the following is a heterogeneous mixture:

q: Which of the following loses its valence electrons the most readily?

Sodium ions escape the battery enclosure during recharging
Irreversible side reactions occur slowly over time
Sodium ions get reduced to sodium metal over time

e: Graham's law discovered that lightweight gas puffballs can sprint and spread through a room much faster than bulky, heavy ones.

q: Which of the following is an intensive property?

q: Traditionally, a decrease in carbon emissions was linked to economic recession. However, since 2000, more than 20 countries have decoupled their emissions and economic development. What could this imply?

Those countries are increasingly relying on clean energy alternatives

e: Boron steps in like a friendly sponge, soaking up wild particles to keep the bustling nuclear reaction safe and calm.

q: The source of the tremendous energy and rapid rotations of stars detected at the center of the Milky Way is attributed to which of the following?
e: A supermassive black hole sits at the galaxy center like a colossal cosmic drain, whipping nearby stars into a dizzy dance.

q: Which of the following is the best strategy to compensate for random errors during an experiment in an unbiased manner?

q: Imagine if you could weigh electrons and protons on a simple balance. How many electrons do you need to balance a single proton?
e: Protons are heavyweights, needing about 18 hundred featherlight electrons to balance just one on a tiny seesaw!

q: Heating an endothermic reaction will shift equilibrium towards which of the following?
e: Endothermic reactions love warmth, so feeding them heat happily pushes everything forward to make more products!

e: When a nitrogen atom scoops up three extra electrons, it happily matches the complete, peaceful jacket of neon.

e: Iowa and Illinois are the true kings of corn, offering mountains of leftover husks and stalks to power up your plant.

q: Why does sodium becomes positively charged when it combines with chlorine?

q: At a given temperature, the velocity of gases is:

q: Which of the following best describes how a chemical change occurs in a substance?

It is ground into a powder
e: Atoms make brand-new chemical friendships by sharing, borrowing, or giving away tiny electrons to become something completely new.

q: According to the U.S. Energy Information Administration, which of the following industrial sectors is responsible for the largest total energy use in the United States?
e: Turning thick crude oil into usable fuels takes massive heat, making petroleum refining the thirstiest energy user of all.

q: An inorganic binary compound always has a name that ends with what suffix?

q: What functional group can be found in acetyl-salicylic acid that is not found in salicylic acid?
e: Aspirin borrows a sweet little ester group, giving it an extra chemical cape that plain old salicylic acid simply does not wear.

q: Which of the following is NOT an example of a biomass energy source?
e: While biomass comes from freshly grown plants, sleepy old coal snoozed underground for millions of years, becoming a fossil fuel instead.

q: In limestone formations, the development of caves requires water and which of the following:
e: Rain joins hands with carbon dioxide in the air, creating a mild acid that nibbles away rock to carve secret underground caves!

e: Whenever runny mercury mixes with silver to patch up a tooth, scientists call that special metal blend an amalgam.

q: Which of the following pairs are allotropes?
e: Diamond and graphite are pure carbon cousins, built from the exact same atoms wearing two completely different, dazzling outfits.

q: In nuclear reactors, control rods are used to absorb free neutrons without undergoing fission themselves. Which of the following is a frequently used substance to make control rods?
e: Boron acts like a calm, hungry sponge, safely catching stray neutrons in the reactor to keep things peaceful.

e: Most elements on the board are cozy solids at room temperature, making them the easiest target to hit!

q: Which of the following processes could be used to control fission reactions in a nuclear power plant?

Placing gallium control rods between the fuel rods to absorb neutrons
Placing cadmium control rods between the fuel rods to absorb neutrons
Placing uranium-235 control rods between the fuel rods to absorb neutrons

q: Which of the following classes of coal has the highest carbon content?

q: Hydrogen, with its one electron, produces a line spectrum in the visible light range with:

q: Which of the following is NOT an element:
e: While pure elements stand alone, sulfate is actually a cozy little team of sulfur and oxygen holding hands together.

q: What is the category of vehicles that can run on a mixture of up to 85% ethanol in gasoline?

e: Alpha decay tosses out a bundle of four tiny pieces, so oxygen-17 shrinks down to an atomic mass of thirteen.

q: Scientists at the Joint BioEnergy Institute are studying the synthesis of macrolides, which are protein synthesis inhibitors. These molecules are often used for which of the following purposes?
e: Macrolides make wonderful antibiotics by sneaking inside bad bacteria and shutting down their protein factories so your body heals.

q: Scientists working at Ames Laboratory have devised a way to increase the catalytic activity of nanoparticles in fuel cell applications. What quantity related to the particles did scientists focus on increasing?
e: Giving tiny particles more surface area creates extra playground space on the outside for chemical reactions to meet and happen faster.

q: Which of the following substances when pure typically contains ONLY carbon atoms:

q: Which of the following chemical formulas best describes the following statement: "Methanol is converted to formaldehyde by reaction with oxygen?"

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true of halogens?

They only need one electron to fill their outer energy level
They can be used for disinfection of water and for preventing diseases of the thyroid gland
e: Halogens are not sleepy metals at all; they are lively nonmetals bursting with energy to grab new electron friends.

q: What is the current approximate maximum percent efficiency fuel cells can obtain when provided with pure hydrogen?

q: What is the chemical symbol for lead?

q: Which of the following is an accurate description of the liquid phase of matter?
e: Liquids love playing dress-up by changing shape to fit any cup, but they always keep the exact same volume.

e: Biomass is a cozy helper, turning plants into power to quietly supply about 4% of all the energy America needs today.

q: Which of the following is true about liquids in general?

They form droplets due to viscosity [vis-CAW-sih-tee]
They are more densely packed than solids
e: Most liquids cuddle up even tighter when they freeze, so their volume naturally shrinks as they turn solid.

A freezing material to a boiling material
e: Heat is generous, always rushing from cozy, warm spots to give chilly places a warm hug.

q: What country has the largest coal reserves on Earth?
e: Deep underground, the United States holds the world's biggest hidden stash of ancient, buried coal.

q: Which of the following does the subscript 3 indicate in the molecular formula for calcium carbonate?

There are 3 carbon atoms in one molecule of calcium carbonate
There are 3 calcium atoms in one molecule of calcium carbonate
There are 3 atoms each of oxygen, carbon and calcium in one molecule of calcium carbonate

q: Which of the following best describes nuclear potential energy?

The mutual electrostatic energy of two charges
The electric potential energy divided by a charge associated with a static electric field
A force on electrically charged objects near a nucleus

q: Which of the following is NOT true of metals?

They conduct electricity but do not conduct heat
They can be combined to form alloys
e: Metals love sharing warmth, so saying they cannot conduct heat is totally wrong—just ask a hot soup spoon!

q: The Aufbau principle is used to determine which of the following?
a: Position and momentum of an electron
e: Like sleepy campers choosing the lowest bunk beds first, electrons follow the Aufbau rule to build their neat seating chart.

q: Which of the following best classifies iodine?
e: Iodine hangs out with chlorine and fluorine in the halogen family, full of colorful and eager salt-making buddies.

q: Which of the following describes a liquid in which visible particles settle?
e: In a suspension, chunky floating particles drift through the liquid until gravity gently pulls them down to the bottom.

q: In a closed container, if a gas is heated, which of the following occurs:
a: the gas will condense on the inner walls of the container
e: Heating trapped gas particles makes them zoom around frantically, bumping into the walls and sending the pressure soaring!

q: A nucleus of Lithium containing 3 protons and 4 neutrons is surrounded by 4 electrons. Which of the following best describes this?
e: With four negative electrons outnumbering three positive protons, this little atom carries an electric charge, making it an ion.

q: Nuclear power plants generate energy by which of the following processes?
e: Nuclear plants use fission, a clever trick where tiny atoms split in half, releasing giant bursts of energy to make electricity.

q: Which of the following processes is NOT used to produce hydrogen gas fuel?
e: Dry milling is busy crunching corn kernels into ethanol fuel, leaving the bubbly job of making hydrogen gas to other methods.

q: What element is currently the most promising nuclear fuel alternative to uranium due to its greater abundance and better resistance to proliferation?
e: Abundant thorium is uranium's safer cousin, patiently waiting to make clean nuclear power without easily turning into dangerous weapons.

q: Which of the following substances contains a covalent bond?
e: Two chlorine atoms make a friendly pact by sharing their electrons like a pair of cozy mittens.

q: The Rutherford Experiment was actually carried out by Hans Geiger [GYE-gur] and Ernest Marsden at the request of Rutherford. Which of the following statements is NOT true about this work?
a: Rutherford inferred the gold electrons were responsible for deflecting the alpha particles by small angles
Rutherford inferred the gold nuclei were responsible for deflecting the alpha particles by large angles
The deflected alpha particles were detected as points of light on a fluorescent screen
Approximately 1 in 20,000 alpha particles was deflected by 90 degrees or more
e: Tiny electrons are far too light to bounce bulky alpha particles, so Rutherford knew they were not to blame.

q: Researchers at Princeton Plasma Physics Lab recently developed a device that can manufacture on demand technetium-99m [tek-NEE-shee-um 99 M], a radioactive isotope with a half-life of 6 hours. For what purpose will this technetium isotope be used?
a: Research into CP violation in the weak force
e: Doctors use this glowing helper in medical diagnostics, like a tiny, gentle flashlight that lets special cameras see inside your body.

q: The cesium atom is used to define which of the following SI units?
e: Cesium atoms tick-tock with super steady vibrations, making them the ultimate tiny clock used to define the second.

q: At 100 degrees Fahrenheit, which of the following substances would feel hottest to touch?
e: Gold is such a speedy heat conductor that it rushes its warmth into your fingers way faster than the others.

q: Which of the following BEST describes what atomic particle was the last to be discovered and why:
a: the electron because it has very small mass
the proton because it resides in the nucleus
the proton because it does not have any angular momentum
the neutron because it has no charge
e: Neutrons were master hide-and-seek champions because their lack of electric charge made them invisible to early detectors.

q: Which of the following fuels has an octane rating of greater than 100?
e: Propane resists engine knocks so well that its power score zooms right past one hundred on the octane scale.

q: Typical households using natural gas consumed 22% less natural gas in 2009 than in 1990. Which of the following is NOT a reason for the decline?
a: Decreased use of natural gas for home heating
Reduction in the number of consumers
e: Gas customers never actually shrank, because more families joined the cozy club! Each home simply used less fuel thanks to clever heaters that sip energy.

q: Which of the following is the most efficient type of solar cell?
e: Multijunction cells stack different layers to catch many colors of sunlight at once, making them the most efficient light-catching champions around.

q: Elements are often classified by their atomic number. The atomic number denotes the number of:
e: Every atom wears a special badge called its atomic number, which proudly counts the positive protons sitting in its cozy center.

q: Which of the following best explains why diamond is much harder than graphite even though both are made of arranged carbon atoms?
a: Graphite is arranged in sheets, whereas diamond's layers are intertwined in a crystalline structure, making it stronger
Graphite is opaque and grey while diamond has a greater clarity and sheen to it
Diamond is arranged in sheets, whereas graphite's layers are intertwined in a crystalline stucture, making them weaker
The density of graphite is greater than that of diamond, meaning the carbon atoms are more likely to leave the structure
e: Diamond locks its carbon atoms in a super-strong three-dimensional box, while graphite just stacks slippery flat sheets that slide right off.

q: Which of the following types of organisms does NOT utilize oxygen for respiration?
e: Anaerobic critters happily munch their snacks and make energy without ever needing a single breath of oxygen.

q: If 90 grams of metal has a volume of 8.7 cubic centimeters, which of the following metals is it?
a: Lead, with a specific gravity of 11.3
Silver, with a specific gravity of 10.3
Nickel, with a specific gravity of 8.9
Tin, with a specific gravity of 7.3
e: Dividing ninety grams by its size gives a density of about ten point three, pointing straight to shiny silver!

q: Which chemical element was originally known as Alabamine?
e: Before getting named astatine, element 85 was called alabamine by researchers who thought they found it in Alabama.

q: Which of the following energy sources used in power plants contributes the least to the plants' carbon dioxide emissions?
e: Spinning turbines let the friendly breeze do all the pushing without burning anything, releasing zero dirty carbon dioxide.

q: Which of the following atoms has the largest atomic radius?
e: Potassium has so many fluffy shells of electrons that it puffs out much bigger than the others!

q: For the redox reaction of tin(II) and iron(III) to produce tin(IV) and iron(II), the sum of the coefficients of the balanced reaction is:
e: One tin atom and two iron friends trade sparky electrons on each side. Counting all the teammates together adds up to six!

q: In which of the following states would you be more likely to find a methane digester on a farm or ranch?
e: Wisconsin is packed with dairy cows, so its farms use special digesters to turn smelly manure into bright, clean energy.

q: Which of the following are NOT emitted by radioactive materials?
e: While busy atoms shoot out real rays, phonons are just friendly sound vibrations rippling through solids, not radioactive escapees.

q: Which of the following will occur when an unbalanced force acts on an object:
e: When an uneven push gives an object a shove, it cannot sit still, so it accelerates into motion!

q: Which of the following does NOT represent a chemical reaction?
e: Falling water is just taking a splashy trip downhill without changing its identity, so no chemical magic happens there.

q: What type of coal has the highest carbon content?
e: Peat is like a cozy swamp sponge packed with ancient plants, holding the highest amount of trapped carbon on land!

q: Consider a graph with the mass of a sample on the y-axis and the sample volume on the x-axis. Which of the following substances would have the steepest slope on this graph?
e: Liquid rain packs the most weight into the tiniest space, making its density line climb the steepest of all!

q: Which of the following is a substance that does NOT conduct electricity when it is a solid but does conduct electricity when it is melted or in a molten state:
e: Sodium chloride locks its charged ions in solid crystals, but once melted, they flow freely to carry electricity.

q: What happens as the activation energy of a reaction increases?
e: Higher activation energy is like a steeper hill, making it harder for molecules to climb over, which slows the reaction down.

q: How are ionically-bonded compounds generally named?
a: After the scientist who first created the compound
By using the name of the positive ion followed by the name of the negative ion
By using the name and Roman numeral associated with the metal involved
e: We politely name the cheerful positive ion first, followed by its negative partner, just like in table salt!

q: What is the difference between the two stable isotopes boron 10 and boron 11?
e: Boron-11 simply carries one extra neutron in its heart, like a twin holding a tiny little backpack.

q: Ionic compounds are most commonly formed between what two types of elements?
e: Generous metals love giving away their electrons to eager nonmetals, locking them together in a happy ionic hug!

q: The removal of silver tarnish by placing it in a bowl containing aluminum foil and a base is an example of which of the following types of reaction?
e: Aluminum generously passes its electrons over to the tarnished silver, making this clever swap a classic redox reaction!

q: At which temperature would water most likely boil on Mount McKinley:
e: High on chilly mountaintops, thinner air presses less on water, letting bubbly steam escape much sooner at ninety degrees.

q: What is the molecular geometry of methane?
e: Carbon hugs four hydrogen friends that spread out as far as possible, forming a neat four-sided pyramid shape called a tetrahedral.

q: The rate of a reaction is directly dependent on which of the following?
a: Difference between reactant energy and product energy
e: Think of activation energy as an energy hill chemicals must climb. The easier the climb, the faster the reaction happens!

q: Assuming that the light bulbs, wires, and batteries are all the same in two different circuits, how would the brightness of two light bulbs in series differ from the brightness of just one light bulb?
a: The brightness of the two in series would be dimmer than the single bulb
The bulbs in series would not light up with the same amount of battery power
The bulbs in series would be brighter than the single bulb
The bulbs in series and the single bulb would have the same brightness
e: When two bulbs share a single path, they must split the battery's electrical energy and glow noticeably dimmer than a lone bulb.

q: How many moles of carbon dioxide are required to react with 2 moles of water to form carbonic acid?
e: Carbon dioxide and water team up one-to-one, so two water molecules need two carbon dioxide friends to make acid.

q: Ames National Lab researchers are studying alane, or aluminum hydride. This substance is generally used in synthetic chemistry labs to perform what chemical role?
e: Alane acts as a reducing agent, like a generous friend happily giving away its hydrogen to help transform other chemicals.

q: At a particular temperature T and pressure P, carbon dioxide is in the vapor phase. Which of the following is NOT possible if the pressure of the vapor is increased while the temperature stays the same?
a: The vapor enters the compressible liquid phase
The vapor enters the solid phase without entering the liquid phase first
The vapor enters the solid phase and then enters the liquid phase
e: Squeezing carbon dioxide packs its particles closer, so a solid cannot magically melt into a looser liquid just from more squeezing.

q: Which of the following is the least dense at standard temperature and pressure:
e: Heavy metals pack their atoms tightly like crowded elevators, while gentle liquid water stays spread out and least dense.

q: Fuel cells produce electric currents by means of:
e: Fuel cells use electrochemical reactions to turn the secret energy locked in chemicals straight into zippy, glowing electricity.

q: What makes a material a good insulator?
a: Having electrons that are bound and cannot move completely away from their nucleus [NOO-klee-uhs]
Having a nucleus that contains a number of positively charged protons
Having electrons that are farther away from the nucleus
Having electrons that can drift away
e: Good insulators are like cozy homebodies whose electrons hug their home nucleus tightly and refuse to wander off into the neighborhood.

q: Which of the following is the hardest coal and gives off a great amount of heat when it burns:
e: Anthracite was squeezed tight underground for ages, making it the hardest rock in the coal family that burns super hot!

q: Which of the following causes a drop of liquid to be rounded?
e: Water drops pull their own edges inward with surface tension, hugging tightly to form a neat little bead.

q: What impurity found in coal contributes to acid rain?
e: Sneaky sulfur hides in coal, and when it burns, it drifts into clouds to turn raindrops sour and acidic.

q: Atoms of which of these elements tend to form three covalent bonds?
e: Nitrogen loves to share, reaching out with three little atomic hands to form three cozy covalent bonds.

q: A proton exchange membrane fuel cell exchanges which of the following ions?
e: A proton is really just a little H+ ion, and this fuel cell lets only H+ zoom through its special wall!

q: Which of the following is LEAST accurate regarding the element helium:
a: it is the second most abundant element in the universe
it is constantly escaping from Earth's atmosphere into space
it is toxic to humans even in very low concentrations
e: Gentle helium is completely non-toxic in small puffs, happily lifting party balloons and making your voice squeak without poisoning anyone.

q: Until the mid-1800s, biomass provided a significant portion of US energy needs. Which of the following is closest to the percentage of US energy usage that was provided by biomass before 1850?
e: Long ago, crackling wood fires did almost all the work, happily providing ninety percent of America's energy to keep everyone warm!

q: When do water molecules move back and forth between the liquid and the gaseous state?
a: Only when the air is saturated
Only when the outward movement of vapor molecules produces a pressure equal to the atmospheric pressure
e: Restless little water molecules never stop dancing, jumping into the air and diving back into the puddle at all times.

q: A balloon is filled with air at room temperature and is then dipped into liquid nitrogen. Which of the following will occur?
e: Super-chilly liquid nitrogen makes the bouncing air molecules shiver and huddle close together, so the whole balloon collapses flat.

q: Which of the following fuel types was used in the past to prevent engine knocking?
e: Old cars used to get grumpy hiccups, so drivers gave them leaded fuel to hush that noisy engine knocking.

q: Which of the following is NOT true regarding radioactive decay?
a: In gamma decay, no transmutation occurs
Different isotopes of the same element will decay at the same rate
Radioactive decay may cause an atom to lose protons or neutrons
Radioactive decay is a process by which unstable atoms emit ionizing particles
e: Each isotope marches to its own ticking clock, so two cousins of the same element will decay at completely different speeds!

q: The Sun consists of mostly which two elements?
e: Our glowing Sun is a giant, crackling campfire built almost entirely from swirling hydrogen and helium.

q: One gram of which of the following substances will be most dense at standard temperature and pressure?
e: Gold packs its heavy atoms so closely together that one tiny gram takes up the least space of all!

q: Which of the following most closely relates to the first law of thermodynamics:
a: energy moving from a cold to a hot object
kinetic energy of molecules and atoms
e: Energy is a master shapeshifter that never truly disappears, only trading one costume for another because energy is always conserved.

q: Which of the following elements has chemical properties similar to oxygen?
e: Sulfur lives right under oxygen in the same chemical family, so they share tricks and behave like look-alike cousins.

q: The ejection of an alpha particle from a nucleus results in which of the following?
a: An increase in the atomic number by one
An increase in the mass number by four
A decrease in the atomic number by two
A decrease in the mass number by two
e: When the nucleus tosses out an alpha particle, it loses two protons, dropping its atomic number by two.

q: Which of the following is TRUE about chemical elements:
a: fluorine is a very reactive element
rare earth metals are also known as alkaline earth metals
catalysts are typically consumed in chemical reactions
metalloids are some of the best-known conductors of heat and electricity
e: Fluorine is like an impatient puppy that desperately wants electrons, making it a wildly reactive element.

q: What type of heat transfer is demonstrated when a metal spoon placed in an operational frying pan heats up enough to burn anyone that directly touches the spoon?
e: Heat loves to share, crawling directly from the sizzling pan right up the spoon through touch!

q: Researchers are beginning to focus on butanol instead of ethanol as a replacement for gasoline. What is the primary reason for this shift in focus?
a: Butanol is more cost-effective than ethanol
Butanol is easier to work with
Butanol can be used in cars without any modifications
Butanol contains more chemical energy than ethanol
