e: Butanol is an easygoing fuel that regular cars can sip right away, without needing any engine makeovers to hit the road!

q: Which of the following is true about a mixture of gasses?
a: The sum of the partial pressures of each gas is equal to the total pressure
The sum of the temperatures of each gas is equal to the total temperature
The total volume is equal to the largest partial volume
The total number of moles is equal to the total volume multiplied by the sum of the moles of each gas
e: Each gas gently pushes on its container, and adding up all those little pushes gives you the total pressure.

q: After which Danish city is the 72th element on the periodic table named?
e: Hafnium was discovered in lovely Copenhagen, taking its name from the ancient, storybook word for that very city.

q: A beaker of water is placed in a vacuum chamber and the chamber evacuated. Which of the following will NOT happen?
e: Water will not heat up because rapid boiling steals its warmth away, leaving the chilly puddle to freeze instead.

q: If a car could go 30 miles on one gallon of gasoline, approximately how far in miles would the same car go on one gallon of ethanol?
e: Ethanol packs less punchy fuel energy than gasoline, carrying the car about twenty miles instead of thirty.

q: Which of the following pairs of elements are liquid at room temperature?
e: Mercury and bromine are the only two special elements that stay runny like puddle water at ordinary room temperature.

q: A friend tells you that he thinks that all processes that change a substance's color are chemical changes. Which of the following processes could you use as an example of a color change that is NOT a chemical change?
e: Adding water to dark juice just spreads the color molecules apart without changing them, making dilution a purely physical trick.

q: A student is preparing 500 milliliters of a 6-millimolar solution of copper (II) sulfate. Which of the following pieces of glassware would be best for the most precise measurement of 500 milliliters of this solution?
e: A volumetric flask has one special line etched on its neck, making it the master of exact measurements.

q: Which of the following is not part of Dalton's atomic theory?
a: All matter is composed of atoms of elements
Chemical reactions occur when atoms are rearranged
Atoms are composed of protons, neutrons and electrons
Atoms cannot be created or destroyed
e: Dalton imagined atoms as solid little marbles, long before scientists peeked inside and discovered protons, neutrons, and electrons playing within!

q: Which of the following most accurately describes the difference between graphite and diamond?
a: The carbon atoms are arranged in hexagonal planes in graphite, while they are arranged in a crystal structure in a diamond
The carbon atoms in graphite are held together by weak hydrogen bonds, while they are held together by strong covalent bonds in a diamond
The carbon atoms in graphite are mixed in with impurities, while diamond contains no impurities
The carbon atoms in graphite are bonded to more other atoms than the carbon atoms in diamond
e: Graphite stacks carbon in slippery flat sheets, while diamond locks those same atoms into a sparkling, ultra-strong crystal cage!

q: The pH scale can be used to quantify which of the following properties of a solution?
e: The colorful pH scale acts like a mood ring for liquids, measuring how sour an acid is or how high its basicity climbs.

q: Which of the following compounds is LEAST soluble in water?
e: Nitrogen molecules are shy around water, preferring to float in the air rather than dissolve into the puddle below.

q: Most of today's plug-in hybrid and all-electric vehicles incorporate a common battery. This battery is also onboard the Boeing 787 Dreamliner. What type is this battery?
e: Lithium-ion batteries are lightweight superstars, packing enough punch to push electric cars down the road and lift giant Dreamliner airplanes sky-high!

q: Which of the following is TRUE of gases:
a: their particles are in uniform motion
e: Gas particles love zooming apart, leaving lots of room between them to squish closely together when you give them a gentle squeeze!

q: Approximately 45% of biomass energy production in the US comes from what fuel source?
e: Sturdy wood from chopped trees and forest scraps burns brightly to make nearly half of all our biomass energy.

q: What type of reaction is Na2S + 2HCl yields 2NaCl + H2S an example of?
e: The dancing atoms politely swap partners in pairs, making this chemistry square dance a double replacement reaction!

q: Which of the following states produces the most coal?
e: Wyoming digs up more coal than any other state, thanks to giant, energy-packed layers buried under its rolling plains.

q: Which of the following elements has the highest first ionization [eye-on-ih-ZAY-shun] energy?
e: Oxygen clings to its electrons with fierce, tiny arms, demanding the highest ionization energy to pull one away.

q: Which of the following sectors is the most important factor in assessing future trends in demand for liquid fuels?
e: Transportation gulps the most oil because millions of cars, planes, and ships are always on the move, thirsty for fuel.

q: Given that fuel cells operate on reduction-oxidation reaction pairs, which of the following occurs during the oxidation half-reaction?
a: Oxygen is created by the reaction
Oxygen is removed from the reaction
e: In oxidation, a generous atom cheerfully lets go of a tiny electron, releasing it so it can race through the wire and make electricity!

q: Which of the following sectors in the United States uses the most petroleum?
e: All our hungry cars, trucks, and airplanes guzzle up the biggest share of oil just to keep us moving.

q: Which of the following compounds contains an ionic bond?
e: Magnesium cheerfully gives away its electrons to hungry bromine atoms, snapping them together like magnets in an ionic bond.

q: What subatomic particle is principally responsible for the differences in chemical properties between elements?
e: Busy little electrons dance on the outside of atoms, deciding how elements bond and play with one another.

q: E-85, also known as "flex-fuel," gets its name from which of the following?
a: It is 85% more efficient than gasoline
It is a mixture of 85% gasoline and 15% ethanol
It is a mixture of 85% ethanol and 15% gasoline
It has an equivalent octane rating of 85
e: That name tells us the fuel is mostly plant power, mixing eighty-five percent ethanol with fifteen percent gasoline.

q: In a modern optimally functioning internal combustion engine, most of the energy is lost as:
e: Car engines work hard to zoom, but most of their fuel's energy accidentally slips away as toasty heat.

q: Which of the following BEST describes the following reaction: 4Fe + 3O2 2Fe2O3
e: Iron and oxygen join hands to build shiny new rust, teaming up in a reaction called synthesis.

q: Molecules that have the same chemical formula but have different shapes or geometric arrangements are called:
e: Think of isomers like little Lego models built with the exact same bricks, just snapped together into totally different, wonderful shapes!

q: Lanthanides are elements with which of the following orbitals partially filled?
e: Lanthanides are quiet neighbors that tuck their newest, wandering electrons right into fancy, flower-shaped f orbitals.

q: About what fraction of the petroleum consumed in the United States is used for transportation?
e: About three-fourths of our oil fuels zoomy cars, trucks, and planes, keeping our busy nation constantly on the move.

q: The behavior of light has lead scientists to generally consider light as behaving as:
e: Light loves playing dress-up! Sometimes it zips along like tiny bouncing balls, and other times it ripples like gentle ocean waves.

q: The addition of equal moles of which of the following to water will decrease the freezing point the most?
e: Sulfuric acid splits into three busy little pieces that crowd water so much, it gets way too tricky for ice crystals to link up.

q: Which of the following solutions could be used to titrate an oxalic acid solution?
e: Oxalic acid needs a strong, helpful base like sodium hydroxide to neutralize it in their bubbly chemistry dance.

q: Which of the following does NOT depend on a chemical reaction?
a: Your voice squeaking when you breathe helium
Fizzing of an Alka-Seltzer in water
e: Helium does not change your vocal cords; sound waves just zip faster through the light gas to make you squeak.

q: Which of the following chemical names is NOT correctly matched with its chemical formula:
e: The chemical symbol Be actually belongs to beryllium, not boron, making that name a silly case of mistaken identity.

q: Distillation will NOT work very well under which of the following situations:
a: the components in the mixture have the same boiling points
the mixture consists of a solid and a liquid
e: Distillation separates liquids by boiling them apart, but if they boil at the exact same temperature, they fly away together like best friends!

q: Which of the following intermolecular forces is strongest?
e: Hydrogen bonding acts like an extra-strong hug between molecules, pulling them together with far more power than the other forces!

q: Lawrence Berkeley National Lab researchers use high-energy charged particles to generate materials with unique properties. What is the term for a particle or molecule that has an electric charge?
e: Meet the ion, a spunky little particle that gained or lost electrons, leaving it buzzing with an electric charge!

q: Vinegar is a liquid solution containing acetic acid and water. It could be accurately classified as which of the following?
e: The acid and water blend so smoothly that every single drop looks identical, making it a cozy homogeneous mixture.

q: Which of the following is NOT possible using a solar box cooker?
e: Solar cookers trap cozy sunshine to warm food, but purifying anhydrous ethanol takes fancy lab equipment that a sunny box cannot manage.

q: In which of the following pairs are both properties colligative?
a: Freezing point depression and lowering of vapor pressure
Boiling point elevation and ionic strength
e: Both change only because of how many tiny dissolved guests are at the party, not who they actually are!

q: Copper is known for many properties, two of which in particular make it excellent for power lines. One of them is that it has a rather high electrical conductivity. The other property is that it is relatively easy to stretch it into great lengths of wire without breaking. What is the scientific name of the latter property?
e: Ductility is copper's stretchy superpower, letting it pull out into miles of skinny wire without ever snapping in two.

q: Nitrogen, sulfur, and selenium are all:
e: None of these elements shine or carry electricity like metals, which makes them proud members of the nonmetal club.

q: The organic molecule found in vinegar is an example of what class of organic molecule?
e: Vinegar gets its famous tangy splash from acetic acid, a proud member of the carboxylic acid family.

q: Assuming equal lengths of copper wire, which of the following gauges of wire would have the greatest load?
e: Skinny wires get crowded fast, and heat makes things even wilder, giving this toasty twelve-gauge wire the biggest electrical resistance to push against.

q: Which of these elements on the Periodic Table is a Noble Gas?
e: Neon is a calm noble gas that glows happily in signs and keeps its electrons all to itself.

q: Atoms are made up of mostly empty space. Which basic force prevents the atoms of your hand, which are mainly empty space, from easily passing through the atoms in a table top, which are also mainly empty space?
e: Electrons in your hand push against the table using the electromagnetic force, stopping you like an invisible wall.

q: Which of the following describes most of the elements on the periodic table?
e: Most elements are metals, friendly conductors that love passing warmth and electricity down the line to their neighbors.

q: What is the name of the lowest energy subshell of an atom where electrons are found:
e: The cozy s subshell sits closest to the nucleus, making it the perfect low-energy spot for sleepy electrons to snuggle up first.

q: Which of the following fuels used for electricity production produces radioactive waste?
e: Burning coal releases tiny bits of natural uranium and thorium hidden inside the rock, leaving behind radioactive ash.

q: Which of the following is a halogen?
e: Fluorine belongs to a spunky chemical family called the halogens, always eager to grab one more electron to feel complete.

q: Which of the following statements is TRUE of buffers:
a: all neutral pH solutions have equal numbers of buffers
hydronium ions are present in large amounts in most buffers
certain buffers will absorb hydrogen ions to prevent a change in a solution's pH
buffers are artificial chemicals rarely found in nature
e: Helpful buffers act like little sponges, soaking up stray hydrogen ions so the liquid stays peaceful and keeps its balance.

q: What phase of matter can NOT be found in a fluorescent light that is powered on?
e: Inside the solid glass tube, buzzing gas turns into glowing plasma, leaving no room for sloshy liquids.

q: Which of the following subatomic particles are charged?
e: Zooming electrons bring negative sparks while protons carry positive vibes, leaving quiet neutrons without any charge at all.

q: Which of the following does NOT include a chemical reaction?
a: Immersing an iron nail in a copper sulfate solution to coat the nail with copper metal
Combining water, rocks and gravel with cement to make concrete
Combining copper and tin to make bronze
e: Melting copper and tin into bronze is just a physical mix, letting the two metals mingle without creating a new substance.

q: Given the pressure, volume, and temperature of a gas sample, the ideal gas constant allows you to determine what about that gas sample?
e: This handy math tool lets you count every single invisible gas molecule bouncing around inside the container.

q: Atoms with one or more unpaired electrons are which of the following?
e: Lonely electrons love to dance with magnets, making these friendly atoms paramagnetic as they get gently pulled in.

q: What is the name for the SI derived unit for energy?
e: Whenever you jump or run, scientists measure every single bounce of that lively energy in units called joules.

q: What state of matter has a definite volume but not a definite shape?
e: A liquid happily takes the shape of whatever cup it visits, but it always keeps the exact same amount of splash!

q: Which of the following fuel types is extracted by hydraulic fracturing?
e: Water shoots deep underground to crack tight rocks, tickling trapped natural gas so it bubbles up into our homes!

q: The chemical behavior of an atom is determined by its:
e: An atom's atomic number tells us its proton count, which decides how it makes friends and reacts with others.

q: Which of the following requires the most energy:
a: Raising the temperature of one gram of water by one degree Celsius
Changing one gram of ice from a solid to a liquid
Changing one gram of water from a liquid to a gas
Lowering the temperature of one gram of water by one degree Celsius
e: Water droplets love clinging together, so breaking them apart from liquid into floating gas takes the most energy.

q: Which of the following is the BEST example of a chemical reaction:
a: an acid is added to a clear solution in a test tube and a white substance appears and falls to the bottom of the test tube
milk is added to water and the water turns a milky color
e: When two clear liquids suddenly create a brand-new solid snow falling down, a true chemical change has occurred!

q: During science lab, several students discovered that iodine dissolved readily in ethanol. In this case, the ethanol could be classified as which of the following?
e: A solvent is the liquid that welcomes another substance to dissolve inside it, just like ethanol does.

q: The key factor in deciding an electric car's lifespan is the battery life. Once the electric car's battery can't deliver the required power for a car it must be replaced. What is one possible new use for old electric car batteries?
a: Being used in smaller vehicles like scooters
Rebuilding the battery for a different car
e: Too tired to zoom on highways, these cozy old batteries get a second job storing extra electricity for whole neighborhoods!

q: Where are the atoms with largest atomic radii found on the periodic table?
e: Down in the lower left corner, atoms puff out their electron clouds like fluffy giants!

q: Which of the following is a rare earth metal?
e: Lutetium perches down in the special lanthanide row, earning its cozy spot among the rare earth metals.

q: In a lithium-ion battery, what happens to the battery when the anode and cathode reactions are run in reverse?
e: Running the reactions in reverse pushes tiny energy particles right back home, happily recharging the battery for another adventure!

q: An atom containing only a single proton and no electrons is which of the following?
e: When an atom loses its negative electron, its happy positive proton makes it a positively charged cation!

q: Which of the following is closest to the potential energy in joules of a 50 pound boulder on top of a 100 foot cliff relative to the base of the cliff and given 9.8 meters per second squared as g?
e: Perched way up high, gravity gives that heavy rock about 6,800 joules of stored energy just waiting to tumble down!

q: The triple alpha process is primarily responsible for directly producing which of the following?
e: Inside a roaring star, three energetic helium atoms join in a tight bear hug to build brand-new carbon-12.

q: Which of the following statements best describes the properties of semiconductors?
a: They are more conductive than metals but less conductive than nonmetal insulators
Their conductivity is the same as metals
Impurities make them less conductive than metals and nonmetals
They are less conductive than metals but more conductive than insulators
e: Semiconductors are the clever middlemen, letting electricity flow better than stubborn insulators, but not quite as freely as speedy metals.

q: Which of the following energy sources is nonrenewable?
e: While the wind and sun dance forever, Earth only made a limited secret stash of uranium rock deep underground. Once it's gone, it's gone!

q: In which of the following organizational sections of the Periodic Table are lithium, beryllium, boron and carbon all sequentially located:
e: These four elements march side-by-side in a horizontal row called a period, just like classmates standing in line.

q: Approximately how long would a 100 watt bulb burn on the energy needed to manufacture one throw-away soft drink can?
e: Making just one shiny soda can takes so much power that a lightbulb could glow brightly for ten whole hours!

q: A child's seesaw would be considered:
e: A seesaw is a class 1 lever because its balance point sits comfortably right in the middle between both giggling riders.

q: Which of the following best describes chlorine at room temperature?
e: At room temperature, chlorine drifts around as a bubbly, greenish-yellow cloud of gas that you definitely cannot miss.

q: Which of the following properties best determines the difference between a liquid and a gas?
e: Density tells the story, because cozy liquid molecules cuddle close together, while airy gas molecules wander far apart.

q: Which of the following units is used to measure the diameter of protons?
e: Protons are so unimaginably tiny that scientists use the femtometer, a super microscopic measuring stick, to gauge their size.

q: Which of the following BEST explains where the bubbles in a boiling pot of water come from:
a: hydrogen gas is produced and it rises quickly through the water
oxygen from the atmosphere enters the water
e: When water gets super hot, it vaporizes into steam bubbles that happily float right to the top!

q: Which of the following is true of periodic trends?
a: The smaller the atom, the greater the ionization energy
The larger the electronegativity, the smaller the ionization energy
Elements with the highest metallic character are located at the upper left corner of the periodic table
The process of removing an electron from an atom is always exothermic
e: Tiny atoms hug their outer electrons super close, making it take tons of energy to yank one away!

q: Which of the following is the scientific term for a drink that settles and needs to be shaken to redistribute the particles throughout the drink:
e: In a suspension, heavy little juice bits sink to take a nap at the bottom until you shake them awake.

q: Which of the following metals has the most similar valence electron configuration to silver?
e: Gold sits right below silver in the periodic family, so their outer electrons wear matching coats.

q: One benefit to storing carbon dioxide in a deep coal seam is the potential capture of what valuable resource, produced when the carbon dioxide displaces it?
e: When heavy carbon dioxide sneaks deep into coal beds, it nudges valuable methane gas right out of hiding so we can capture it.

q: Which of the following electricity generation methods would work best as a peaker plant?
e: Natural gas plants can fire up in minutes like a speedy racecar, rushing extra power to homes right when everyone flips on their lights!

q: Biopolymers are, in general, what type of polymer?
e: Nature snaps living chains together by squeezing out tiny drops of water, making biopolymers clever condensation polymers.

q: A fifty-fifty solution of distilled water and pure ethanol will appear:
e: Water and pure ethanol blend together seamlessly, letting light pass right through to make a completely clear liquid.

q: Knowing that an extensive property of a system is a physical quality whose value DOES depend on the amount of the substance in a system, which of the following is an extensive property:
e: A giant bonfire holds far more heat energy than a tiny match, because heat grows with size.

q: Which of the following elements exists as a diatomic molecule in its lowest energy state?
e: Nitrogen atoms get lonely by themselves, so they pair up as best buddies to float peacefully through our air.

q: When four moles of solid aluminum react with three moles of oxygen gas to form aluminum oxide, this reaction is known as which of the following types of reaction?
e: Aluminum and oxygen join hands to build something brand new together, which makes this teamwork a synthesis reaction.

q: To prevent lithium ion batteries from catching fire and exploding, which of the following devices is utilized?
e: A trusty monitoring circuit acts like a watchful helper, keeping an eye on heat and electricity so batteries stay calm and cool.

q: The first public demonstration of vegetable-oil-based diesel fuel took place at the 1900 World's Fair. What type of oil was used?
e: At the grand fair, an engine happily gulped down peanut oil to prove that crunchy snacks could fuel the future!

q: Sound energy passes as a wave through an object when energy causes the molecules in the object to:
e: Sound waves tickle tiny molecules, making them vibrate back and forth to pass the sound along like friendly high-fives.

q: Which of the following states that no two electrons can have the same four quantum numbers?
e: The Pauli exclusion principle politely insists that no two electrons can share the exact same cosmic seat number.

q: How many neutrons does fluorine-19 have?
e: Fluorine always has nine protons, so nineteen minus nine leaves ten quiet neutrons cuddled in the middle.

q: What is the term for the process of burning a fuel?
e: Combustion is the sparky science word for burning fuel, setting energy free to make crackling heat and dancing light!

q: In which of the following states would you not expect to find a coal mine?
e: While Nevada is famous for sparkly gold and silver treasures, its dusty desert ground does not hide any coal to dig up.

q: Scientists at SLAC [slack] National Accelerator Lab are studying the reactions that alkenes can undergo. Which of the following descriptions most accurately describes alkenes?
a: Molecules containing a carbon-carbon double bond
Molecules containing only carbon and hydrogen
Molecules that contain an organic acid group
Molecules that are saturated with carbon-hydrogen bonds
e: Alkenes are special little molecules where two carbon friends hold hands twice, forming a snug carbon-carbon double bond.

q: The amount of CO2 produced from burning natural gas will be what percent of the CO2 produced from burning coal, for the same amount of energy output?
e: Natural gas burns far cleaner than lumpy coal, puffing out only about 50 percent as much carbon dioxide to make the same energy.

q: Acetylene has a triple bond between its two carbons. Which of the following shapes does it have:
e: With a mighty triple bond pulling between its carbons, this little molecule stands in a perfectly straight line like an acrobat on a tightrope.

q: Metallic bonding accounts for all but which of the following physical characteristics of metals:
e: Metals are wonderful at sharing heat, so they actually have fantastic thermal conductivity, not poor at all!

q: In the radioactive decay of uranium, what is the final stable element?
e: Wandering uranium keeps tossing off radioactive pieces until it finally settles down as cozy, stable lead.

q: Which of the following is NOT true of pH:
a: the terms basic or alkaline describe a solution with pH greater than 7
the highest value on the pH scale is 14
strong acids dissociate almost completely in water
a pH meter operates by measuring small differences in the density of different fluids
e: A pH meter listens to tiny electric whispers in a liquid to check acidity, not how dense it is.

q: Which of the following metals is attracted to a magnet?
e: Magnets simply cannot resist iron, eagerly pulling it close like a long-lost best friend for a cozy hug.

q: The particles of which of the following states of matter have the strongest attraction between them?
e: Particles in a solid hug each other super tightly, refusing to let go because their attraction is the strongest around!

q: Why are old documents preserved by sealing them in containers filled with helium?
a: Helium will react with any poisonous gas that enter the container and prevent the gas from harming the document
Helium is inexpensive and easy to find
Helium is a gas that will not react with any other element including the paper of the document
Helium will brighten the print on the document
e: Helium is a shy noble gas that refuses to react with anything, keeping fragile old papers safe from decay.

q: An atom's ability to react with other atoms is determined by what type of subatomic particle?
e: Busy little electrons zoom on the outside of atoms, reaching out their tiny hands to bond with neighbors!

q: A saturated aqueous solution of potassium chloride contains 34 grams of solute. Which of the following terms best describes an aqueous solution containing 30 grams of potassium chloride?
e: Because the water could hold four more grams of salt snacks, it is still unsaturated and ready for more.

q: Which of the following reactions always releases heat?
e: Exothermic reactions love sharing their cozy energy, happily sending heat out into the world like a crackling campfire.

q: When nuclear fuel rods are placed underwater, a blue glow can be observed around them. What is the term for this phenomenon?
e: When speedy particles outrun light in water, they create that magical, glowing blue shockwave called Cherenkov radiation!

q: Batteries require energy transfer in a redox reaction. Which of the following describes one possible type of cell in a battery?
e: Inside many batteries, a busy galvanic cell uses chemical reactions to push electrons along, powering up your favorite toys.

q: Which of the following is NOT true of the Earth's magnetic field?
a: It is created by the molten iron in the Earth's outer core
The intensity of the field is the same at the poles and at the equator
It is possible that in a few hundred thousand years, the Earth's magnetic north pole will be reversed
e: Earth's magnetic blanket pulls much tighter at the icy poles than at the equator, so its strength is never identical everywhere.

q: Which of the following represents a typical rechargeable battery?
e: Nickel cadmium batteries are special buddies you can recharge again and again, cheerfully waking up ready to power your favorite toys!

q: Which of the following increases with the addition of sodium chloride to water?
a: The boiling point of the solution
The freezing point of the solution
The vapor pressure of the solution
e: Salt holds onto water molecules tightly, so they need a lot more heat before they can bubble and boil.

q: For two samples of mercury, one with a mass of 10 grams and the other with a mass of 20 grams, which of the following would NOT be the same?
e: Double the mercury means double the space it fills, so its volume definitely changes while its density stays identical.

q: Which of the following phase changes releases heat?
e: As water settles down to freeze into ice, it hugs its molecules together and gently sends its extra heat out into the room.

q: Which of the following is NOT true about phase changes in substances:
a: energy is exchanged during a phase change
sublimation is a type of phase change involving solids
freezing is an exothermic phase change
a phase change cannot be reversed
e: Phase changes love to backtrack, so melted ice can always freeze right back into a solid cube!

q: Which of the following substances has a pH value that is less than 7?
e: Tart, sour vinegar is an acid, which gives it a spunky pH score resting comfortably below seven.

q: Which of the following compounds is most soluble in water of 25 Celsius at 1 atmosphere of pressure?
e: Aluminum chloride loves a good swim, breaking apart and dissolving in water far easier than the others.

q: In a standard lithium-ion battery, from what substance is the anode made?
e: Inside the battery, tiny lithium travelers nestle happily into sheets of carbon, making it the perfect home for the anode.

q: Which of the following is an example of a compound?
e: Hydrogen and chlorine hold hands to build HCl, teaming up two different elements to make a brand-new compound!

q: Which of the following is NOT a property of a base?
a: Reacts with carbonates to form carbon dioxide
e: Making carbonates fizz into bubbly carbon dioxide gas is a special trick for acids, not gentle bases.

q: Which element has the atomic number of 7?
e: Nitrogen proudly carries seven protons in its heart, floating all around us to fill up the big blue sky.

q: Which of the following gases is being captured at landfills and used as a fuel?
e: Munching microbes deep inside our rotting trash burp out methane gas, which clever workers catch and burn for useful fuel!

q: Neon has an atomic mass of 20.19 amu. Which of the following explains why this is?
a: Each atom of neon has a mass of 20.19 amu
Neon likely has a true atomic mass of 20 amu, but mass spectrometry is not precise enough to determine its exact mass
Neon can have a variable number of protons and therefore a range of masses
Neon has three naturally abundant isotopes, but the most common is neon-20
e: Neon comes in three slightly different family sizes, with neon-20 being so popular it tilts the average weight to 20.19!

q: Which of the following statements about precipitation is FALSE?
a: Can occur by converting a soluble substance into an insoluble form
Results in a higher purity solid if higher concentration solutions are used
Can be used to remove metal ions from aqueous solutions [AK-wee-uhs]
Can occur by changing the composition of a solvent to diminish the solubility of a substance in it
e: Crowding too many ingredients together makes them rush and trap messy dirt, so higher concentrations actually lower the purity.

q: Which of the following is LEAST accurate of ionic solids such as NaCl:
a: they conduct electricity when dissolved in water
e: Salt crystals cling to each other with super-strong bonds, so they actually need blistering heat to melt, not low temperatures.

q: A quantum number is not associated with an atomic electron's:
e: Quantum numbers describe an electron's energy, shape, and twirl, but its mass is already fixed and never changes.

q: Which of the following reflects the approximate percentage range of coal produced from surface mines as a fraction of total coal production in the U.S.?
e: Because scooping from above beats digging underground, giant machines collect more than 60% of America's coal right at the surface!

q: All metals:
e: Every metal has free electrons ready to zip around, eagerly sharing heat and electricity down the line.

q: A chemical reaction will always be spontaneous under which of the following conditions?
a: When it is endothermic and with a decrease in entropy
When it is exothermic and with an increase in entropy
When it is exothermic and with a decrease in entropy
When it is endothermic and with an increase in entropy
e: Nature loves sharing heat and making a messy room, so releasing energy while spreading out chaos always happens on its own.

q: When a substance contains more of a dissolved compound than can be dissolved by the solvent under standard conditions, it is referred to as which of the following?
e: When a drink is tricked into holding even more sweetness than it normally can, it becomes super saturated!

q: Which of the following is NOT a physical property?
e: Catching fire turns a substance into something totally brand new, making flammability an exciting chemical trick rather than a physical trait!

q: Carbon-14 emits beta radiation and decays with a half life of 5730 years. Four half lives are about how long in years?
e: Multiplying one giant waiting period of 5,730 years by four gives a grand total of 22,920 years!

q: Which of the following pieces of glassware would be LEAST useful for measuring a given volume of liquid?
e: A test tube is just a smooth glass cup with no measurement lines to tell you how much juice is inside.

q: Which of the following types of energy production yields the most energy per gram of fuel?
e: Fusing deuterium and tritium copies our sun, squeezing tiny atoms together to unleash the biggest blast of energy per gram!

q: A decrease of 1 unit on the pH scale represents which of the following:
a: a 10-fold increase in the hydrogen ion concentration
a 10-fold decrease in the hydrogen ion concentration
a 100-fold increase in the hydrogen ion concentration
a 100-fold decrease in the hydrogen ion concentration
e: Each tiny step down the pH ladder makes things ten times more sour, packing in ten times more hydrogen ions!

q: Which of the following elements will most likely gain two electrons during a chemical reaction?
e: Oxygen already has six outer electrons, so it happily snatches two more to complete its cozy group of eight!

q: The smallest particle that maintains the chemical properties of a compound is called which of the following?
e: A molecule is a tiny team of atoms holding hands, keeping all their special compound powers in one tidy package.

q: Which of the following best describes the law of multiple proportions?
a: When two pure substances react to form a compound, they do so in a definite proportion by mass
When two substances react with each other to form a compound, they do so in multiple proportions according to their mass
When one element can combine with another to form more than one compound, the mass ratios of the elements in the compounds are simple whole-number ratios of each other
There is no change in total mass during a chemical change
e: Elements team up like neat toy blocks, combining in simple whole-number ratios to build entirely different molecules.

q: Which of the following elements has the highest atomic number?
e: Lawrencium wins the grand prize with a whopping 103 protons packed inside its busy heart.

q: In the early 20th century, physicists were unknowingly fissioning uranium by which of the following methods:
a: exposing heavy elements to immense pressure using explosive devices in heavy-walled containment vessels
e: Scientists gently nudged uranium with tiny neutrons, not knowing they were splitting atoms right in two!

q: Which of the following has the highest pH?
e: Chlorine bleach sits right near the top of the basic ladder, boasting the highest pH to wash away stubborn messes.

q: Which of the following groups of the periodic table contain nearly all of the metalloid elements?
e: Metalloids love hanging out together on a cozy staircase in groups 13 through 16, bridging metals and nonmetals.

q: Which of the following metals is the most reactive with water?
e: Potassium gets so super excited around water that it instantly fizzes, pops, and even bursts into bright little flames!

q: Which of the following is typically TRUE:
a: rare earth metals are also known as alkali metals
noble gases are very reactive elements
a reaction in equilibrium cannot move forward or backward
e: Combustion is just fire happily burning fuel, which always shares cozy heat with the world around it.

q: Which of the following kinds of reaction does the following equation exemplify: CH2S + 6 F2 (read as: yields) CF4 + 2 HF + SF6 + heat?
e: Greedy fluorine swoops in to steal electrons from its neighbors, making this a fiery oxidation-reduction swap meet!

q: The production of water from barium hydroxide and ammonium chloride is an example of what type of reaction?
e: This chilly reaction drinks in surrounding heat like a thirsty sponge, making it endothermic as it turns delightfully frosty.

q: An atom that loses its outer electron or electrons readily is which of the following?
e: Active metals are eager givers, gleefully tossing away their outer electrons to join hands with new chemical friends.

q: In a nuclear reactor, moderators play a key role in helping to slow down rapidly moving neutrons. Which of the following is NOT a moderator frequently used in nuclear reactions?
e: Heavy iron atoms are too bulky to slow down speedy neutrons, making iron a terrible choice for a moderator.

q: Which of the following elements has the lowest atomic number?
e: With sixty-six protons in its center, dysprosium has fewer than the others, giving it the lowest atomic number on this list.

q: Metals that can be hammered into thin sheets are called:
e: When a metal is malleable, its atoms gently slide past each other, flattening into shiny sheets instead of snapping into pieces.

q: John and Michael look from their 80 meter high balcony to a swimming pool with a 20 meter horizontal distance from the base of their building. If they were to jump off the balcony into the pool, how fast in meters per second would they have to jump horizontally to succeed in reaching the pool?
e: Gravity gives you a four-second fall, so leaping forward at five meters each second lands you right in the pool.

q: Scientists at Brookhaven National Lab are studying catalysts for the conversion of carbon dioxide to methanol. What general type of reaction is this?
e: Carbon dioxide trades tiny electrons with its neighbors to become methanol, playing a grand game of give-and-take called a redox reaction.

q: Ejecting electrons from the ground state of a metal atom typically requires light from which of the following regions of the electromagnetic spectrum?
e: Tightly held electrons need a giant zap of high energy to break free, and mighty X-rays pack just the right punch.

q: Which of the following lists contains only metals?
e: Magnesium, manganese, and lead all belong to the shiny metal family, with not a single sneaky nonmetal among them.

q: Which of the following properties is NOT a property of a covalent molecular compound?
e: Covalent molecules keep their electrons tightly tucked away, meaning electricity cannot zip through them easily.

q: With which of the following is Brownian motion most directly related:
e: Thermal energy is pure heat, which makes invisible water molecules dance and bump floating specks all around the room.

q: Water ice floats because its density is less than liquid water at the same temperature. Which of the following intermolecular forces best explains this effect?
e: As water freezes, gentle hydrogen bonds push the molecules into a roomy, open pattern, helping ice float like a raft.

q: Which of the following elements has the highest melting point at standard atmospheric pressure?
e: Tungsten holds its atoms together with astonishing strength, refusing to melt even in heat that turns other metals into soup.

q: In which of the following compounds does hydrogen have an oxidation state that is NOT +1?
e: In sodium hydride, hydrogen grabs an electron from generous sodium, wearing a rare minus-one charge instead of its usual plus-one.

q: The carboxyl functional group is MOST associated with which of the following classes of molecules?
e: The carboxyl group has a hydrogen atom ready to hop away, which is the signature trick that makes organic acids acidic.

q: What is the primary component of natural gas?
e: Deep underground, natural gas is mostly made of friendly methane, a tiny fuel floating ready to create cozy warmth.

q: Which of the following substances would show the Tyndall effect?
e: Blood is crowded with floating cells that bump into passing light, scattering beams so you can see the Tyndall glow.

q: How do alkali metals differ from alkaline [AL-kuh- lyn] earth metals?
a: Alkali metals have one electron in their outer shells; alkaline earth metals have two
Alkali metals do not conduct electricity; alkaline earth metals do
Alkali metals are highly reactive; alkaline earth metals are not
Alkali metals are malleable [MAL-ee-uh-buhl]; alkaline earth metals are ductile
e: Alkali metals have just one lonely electron wandering on their outer shell, while alkaline earth metals proudly carry a pair of two.

q: When calculating the equilibrium constant for a reaction, the concentration of which of the following is generally included?
e: Solutes are the dissolved swimmers whose numbers can change, so chemists always count them in the reaction recipe.

q: Clean coal research is currently NOT focused on which of the following?
a: Improving the purity of coal ore
Increasing efficiency of power plants using coal
Capturing carbon generated when burning coal
Reusing carbon dioxide generated when burning coal
e: Scientists do not try purifying raw coal ore, focusing instead on catching sneaky smoke before it drifts into the sky!

q: Which of the following laws would be most useful for determining the change in volume of a gas as it changes temperature at constant pressure?
e: Charles’s law shows how warm, happy gas puffs up bigger when heated, matching volume straight to temperature.

q: What impurity found in coal contributes most significantly to acid rain?
e: Sneaky sulfur hides inside dirty coal, floating up into clouds to brew grumpy, sour acid raindrops!

q: Which of the following elements possesses the highest ionization energy?
e: Neon is a noble gas with a full, happy family of electrons, so it clutches them tightly and stubbornly refuses to let any go.

q: Raw natural gas contains approximately 5 percent of which of the following gases?
e: Natural gas is mostly methane, but cozy little propane tags along, quietly making up about five percent of that underground mix.

q: Electric vehicles convert about 60% of the electrical energy from the grid to power at the wheels. In a gasoline-powered vehicle, which of the following is closest to the percentage of the energy stored in gasoline that is converted to energy at the wheels?
e: Gas engines are noisy, hot heaters that lose most energy, sending only about twenty percent to actually spin the wheels.

q: Which of the following molecules has a tetrahedral geometry?
e: With four hydrogen buddies standing evenly around a carbon center, methane puffs into a neat little four-cornered tetrahedral shape.

q: A flywheel battery consists of which of the following?
a: A voltage source providing power to a spinning disk
A voltage applied to a motor to make a flywheel rotate, storing energy as the motion of a spinning wheel
Energy converted when a disk is rotated backwards
Potential energy converted into magnetic energy
e: Electricity spins a heavy wheel super fast, saving up energy in that nonstop spin until you need it back.

q: Which of the following is largely responsible for the characteristic bad odor of a rotten egg?
e: That grumpy, nose-pinching stink comes from sneaky hydrogen sulfide gas escaping when the egg's proteins break down!

q: Which of the following is NOT an important step in natural gas processing and treatment?
e: Since natural gas sleeps deep underground without any fresh air, plant workers never need a step to pull out oxygen!

q: 400 joules of energy are required to boil 2 kilograms of nitrogen liquid at its boiling point. What is the heat of vaporization of nitrogen in joules per kilogram?
e: Dividing four hundred joules by two kilograms gives two hundred, the exact energy needed to boil each icy kilogram.

q: Which of the following quantities is dimensionless?
a: The volume of an internal combustion engine
The number of molecules in 1 gram of water
The mass of one mole of sodium atoms
e: Counting molecules is just tallying up tiny friends, so it gives a pure number with no units like meters or grams attached.

q: When measuring liquid in a buret [byur-ET], your eyes should be at the same height as the top of the liquid for accurate measurement. This is a best practice to correct for what?
e: Looking eye-level prevents parallax, a sneaky trick of angles that makes liquid look higher or lower than it is.

q: Which of the following nitrogen-containing functional groups also contains oxygen?
e: An amide is a cozy chemical group where a nitrogen atom teams up directly with a lively oxygen atom.

q: The electrons that are shared in chemical bonds between atoms are most accurately called:
e: Valence electrons live on an atom's very outer edge, reaching out like eager little hands to link up with their neighbors.

q: Tetraethyllead was banned as an anti-knocking additive to gasoline due to concerns that it released dangerous heavy metal emissions into the environment. During what decade did the phaseout of leaded gasoline begin?
e: In the 1970s, people realized lead from car exhaust was polluting the air, so they began phasing it out of gasoline.

q: Which of the following correctly explains why cellulosic ethanol is more expensive to produce than starch ethanol?
a: Conversion of glucose into ethanol is expensive
Cellulose contains many impurities that are expensive to remove
More chemical reactions must be performed
e: Tough plant fibers lock their sugars in a stubborn fortress, so making cellulosic fuel requires extra chemical reactions to break them free.

q: In 1986, the Chernobyl nuclear power plant released several radioactive isotopes into the environment. Which of the following radioactive isotopes is most likely to have replaced the calcium in the bones of people who lived near Chernobyl?
e: Strontium acts so much like its chemical cousin calcium that our bones mistakenly welcome it right in.

q: Which of the following units is most commonly used in the U.S. to compare the energy content of two different fuel sources?
e: To see which fuel packs the warmest punch, people compare their heat energy using a trusty measurement called the BTU!

q: Which of the following substances is most likely to be able to combust?
e: Octane is the fiery champion in gasoline that happily catches fire to zoom cars down the road!

q: Which of the following must be TRUE for a tree that doubled its mass over a growing period of 2 years:
a: it has doubled its number of atoms
e: A tree with twice the mass gets twice as stubbornly heavy to push, which means its inertia has doubled!

q: What property of a fluid would enable a metal wire to float on the surface?
e: Water molecules hold hands so tightly at the top that they make an invisible trampoline called surface tension.

q: In the periodic table, elements are arranged by which of the following?
e: Elements line up in a neat parade by their atomic number, counting the protons tucked inside their tiny hearts.

q: For the balanced combustion reaction of methane to produce carbon dioxide and water, which of the following would NOT be expected?
e: Methane needs no catalyst helper to burn; give it a tiny spark, and it happily bursts into warm flame on its own!

q: In nuclear chemistry, a mass defect exists due to:
e: Some mass mysteriously vanishes because it converts into the mighty glue, called binding energy, holding atomic centers together.

q: How many atoms of magnesium are present in two molecules of the compound Mg3N2?
e: Each tiny molecule holds three magnesium buddies, so when two show up, they bring six happy atoms together.

q: A student is performing an electroplating experiment in which he places two nickel electrodes in a solution of copper sulfate and connects the electrodes to a battery. He notes that the electroplating only occurs on one of the electrodes, while the other electrode remains pure nickel. Which of the following would cause the other electrode to participate in the plating instead?
a: Changing the nickel to a metal with a higher reduction potential
Changing the nickel to a metal with a lower reduction potential
Waiting until the entirety of the first electrode has been plated
Switching the terminals of the battery to which the electrodes are connected
e: Electricity only marches one way, so switching the battery terminals turns the current around and plates copper onto the other electrode instead.

q: Typically, gasoline contains hydrocarbons that contain a number of carbon atoms per molecule in which of the following ranges?
e: Gasoline molecules like traveling light, holding hands in tidy chains of four to twelve carbon atoms so cars can zoom.

q: Barium will form an ionic compound in a one-to-one ratio with which of the following elements?
e: Barium gladly gives away two electrons, and sulfur eagerly takes two, making them a perfectly matched one-to-one pair.

q: Which of the following is TRUE of a gas contained in a tall, sealed cylindrical container at 1 atmosphere of pressure and 25C:
a: the gas exerts the same pressure on all the walls of the container
the gas exerts a higher pressure on the top of the container
the gas exerts a higher pressure on the bottom of the container
the gas exerts a higher pressure on the sides of the container
e: Energetic gas particles bounce in every direction, gently bumping against every container wall with the exact same push.

q: What is the mass of an electron:
a: about the same as a proton
about as much as a proton
e: Compared to a hefty proton, a tiny electron is a featherweight, weighing only about one eighteen-hundredth as much.

q: Mars's seasonal polar ice caps are primarily composed of what molecule?
e: Chilly Mars gets so frosty that carbon monoxide gas freezes solid, bundling up the polar caps like giant scoops of space ice cream!

q: Scientists at Brookhaven National Lab are studying how increasing atmospheric carbon dioxide and increasing Arctic temperatures may result in greater Arctic carbon dioxide uptake as plants begin to grow there. Which of these most closely describes this example?
e: When warmer air helps hungry Arctic plants sprout and gulp down carbon dioxide, Earth cleverly balances itself through negative feedback.

q: X-rays are composed of beams of what particles?
e: Even though they can peek through your skin, X-rays are simply high-energy light carried by tiny packets of energy called photons.

q: Which of the following is NOT characteristic of an atom?
e: Tiny atoms balance positive protons and negative electrons, keeping the whole little family completely neutral rather than positively charged.

q: Which of the following correctly explains how nails become rusty?
a: Nails attract rust particles from the air
The iron in the nail becomes another element
Iron reacts with oxygen and moisture in the air to become rust
A decrease in temperature causes rust to form
e: When iron hangs out with damp air and oxygen, they team up in a slow dance to create crumbly rust.

q: Lawrence Berkeley National Lab researchers are developing new techniques to visualize chemical reactions. In their experimental setup, laser light passes through a sample and contacts a device called a CCD. Which of the following roles does the CCD play?
e: Just like your phone's camera, this clever detector catches laser light to snap tiny pictures of molecules dancing mid-reaction!

q: A carboxyl group is the functional group in which of the following classes of compounds:
e: A carboxyl group loves hanging out with organic acids, giving them their spunky sour kick and defining who they truly are.

q: Which of the following would best describe a 14- karat gold bracelet?
e: Pure gold invites stronger metals to join the party, blending into a tough, shiny mixture called an alloy.

q: On the periodic table of elements, what is the symbol for Tin?
e: Tin borrows its symbol Sn from its ancient Latin name, stannum, like a secret code from the past!

q: Which of the following is NOT an example of oxidation?
e: Electroplating zinc makes metal gain electrons instead of losing them, which means it is reduction rather than oxidation.

q: Which of the following is not a form of energy?
e: Petroleum is a gooey liquid that stores energy inside, which means the fuel itself is matter, not a form of energy.

q: Waste-to-energy plants generally cost more to operate than coal-fired plants. What benefit do they provide?
e: Instead of letting smelly trash pile up forever in giant landfills, these helpful plants gobble up junk to make electricity!

q: Which of the following is the MOST appropriate term for a mixture of two liquids that is uniformly distributed and does not separate:
e: When two liquids swirl together so perfectly that they become inseparable buddies, scientists call that happy blend a solution.

q: What is the name for the procedure which is used to separate molecules of different polarity by placing them on paper and then placing the bottom edge of the paper on in a certain polar or nonpolar solvent?
e: Chromatography lets colors race across paper, separating them as the liquid creeps along.

q: Which of the following metals is the best conductor of electricity?
e: Shiny silver is the ultimate champion of conductors, happily letting energetic electric sparks zoom through it faster than any other metal.

q: Which of the following is formed when three atoms combine to produce a single unit of a larger substance?
e: When atoms hug tightly and stick together to build a brand-new team, they form a molecule.

q: Which of the following is the oxidation number of fluorine gas?
e: When identical fluorine atoms share electrons equally as a pure gas, their oxidation number is zero.

q: Which of the following is most accurate regarding the force of gravity:
a: it is caused by the weight of an object
it is cannot travel through a vacuum
it theoretically acts over unlimited distances
it is caused by the strong nuclear force within atoms
e: Gravity stretches its invisible arms across the entire universe, gently tugging on distant stars because its reach never truly stops.

q: Air is best described as a:
e: Air is a breezy blend where oxygen, nitrogen, and other friendly gases mingle together without chemically locking hands, making it a mixture!

q: Which of the following compounds is LEAST soluble in water and is frequently used as a radiocontrast agent in imaging of the GI tract:
e: Barium sulfate refuses to dissolve in water, traveling safely through your tummy to show doctors bright, clear pictures inside!

q: Which of the following processes is exothermic:
a: solid water changes to water vapor
solid water changes to liquid water
liquid water changes to solid water
liquid water changes to water vapor
e: As wiggly liquid water cuddles together to freeze into solid ice, it releases warmth into the air, making it exothermic!

q: Which of the following properties of an atomic electron is not associated with a quantum number?
e: Every electron carries the exact same unchanging mass, so nature never needs a quantum number ticket to describe how heavy it is.

q: Which of the following is the BEST description of a colloid:
a: a homogeneous mixture of uniform particles in solution
a mixture of different substances that never settle out of solution
e: In a colloid, tiny particles stay forever floating and dancing around, completely refusing to settle to the bottom.

q: Which of the following types of coal has the highest carbon content?
e: After baking under giant mountains for eons, hard, shiny anthracite coal holds the highest carbon of any coal.

q: Which of the following actions would NOT change the strength of an air core electromagnet?
a: Inserting an iron core inside the loop
e: Turning the electric flow backwards only flips the magnet's poles upside down without weakening its mighty pulling power.

q: When you bombard uranium-235 with a slow- moving neutron, the resulting atomic change is called:
e: That tiny neutron taps the uranium atom, splitting it neatly in two during an energetic dance called nuclear fission.

q: Which of the following BEST explains whether a U.S. quarter will accelerate down an inclined plane faster than a silver ring of the same diameter, assuming both roll without slipping:
a: the ring accelerates faster because it has less inertia
the ring will accelerate slower because all its mass in the outer rim
the quarter will accelerate faster because it has more mass
the quarter will accelerate at the same rate as the ring since both have the same diameter
e: With all its weight pushed out to the rim, the ring is stubborn to start spinning and rolls down slower than the quarter.

q: Which of the following metals is the least magnetic?
e: While cobalt, iron, and nickel love clinging to magnets, quiet titanium barely feels any magnetic pull at all.

q: Which of the following musical instruments can produce a pure tone:
e: While instruments play a rich swirl of notes, a clever synthesizer can whistle out one single, perfectly smooth sound wave.

q: When alkali metals such as sodium are placed in water, a gaseous substance is produced. What is this gas?
e: Sodium gets so excited in water that it kicks out atoms, sending bubbly hydrogen gas floating up into the air.

q: Which of the following would increase the rate of rusting on a fixed quantity of iron?
a: Using iron filings instead of iron nails
Putting more water over the iron
Placing the iron in an ice bath
It is not possible to change the rate of rusting
e: Crushing iron into filings gives oxygen way more surface to touch, helping rust spread much faster!

q: A perfectly efficient engine would transform the chemical energy in gasoline into:
e: In an ideal world with zero wasted heat, every drop of fuel energy would turn directly into useful work!

q: The primary use of natural gas by the residential sector is which of the following?
e: Natural gas acts like a cozy blanket, working hard mostly to heat up our chilly homes and bathwater!

q: Raising a bucket of chicken fat from the floor to 3 meters high off the floor would increase the bucket's:
e: Hoisting that silly bucket up high stores potential energy, giving gravity a chance to do some work if it drops!

q: The reactivity of an element depends predominantly on its:
e: Atoms make friends using their outermost valence electrons, so this outer shell decides just how wild and reactive they are!

q: Which of the following electron configurations would be the most chemically stable?
e: With a full outer coat of eight electrons, this atom feels completely peaceful and never needs to trade or share.

q: Atoms of the most active nonmetals have which of the following characteristics?
a: Small atomic radii and high ionization energies
Small atomic radii and low ionization energies
Large atomic radii and high ionization energies
Large atomic radii and low ionization energies
e: These tiny, energetic atoms hug their electrons tight and refuse to let go, staying small while pulling neighbors close!

q: A chemist is trying to pick a weak base for performing a titration. Which of the following could she choose?
e: Unlike fierce, pushy bases, potassium acetate is gentle and holds back in water, making it a delightfully weak base for experiments.

q: Researchers are currently working on generating fuel from algae, known as algal biofuel. Which of the following is NOT expected to be replaced with an equivalent algal biofuel?
e: Scientists brew pond algae for zooming planes and speedy cars, not for quietly warming basements as home heating oil.

q: Which of the following statements is true of a reaction that has a very large equilibrium constant?
a: It requires the input of energy
e: A huge equilibrium constant means the reaction eagerly rushes forward all by itself, making it naturally spontaneous.

q: Scientists at Lawrence Berkeley National Lab are using molecules such as fluorescein [FLORE-eh-scene] isothiocyanate [eye-soh-THIGH-oh-SIGH ah-nate] for experiments that depend on the emission of light. What technique are they performing with this molecule?
e: Because this special molecule glows bright, scientists use fluorescence microscopy to peek at tiny worlds lit up like fireflies!

q: The atomic weight (in amu) of an element most nearly reflects the atom's total number of which of the following?
e: Tiny electrons weigh almost nothing, so the heavy protons and neutrons huddled inside give the atom nearly all its weight.

q: Which of the following is LEAST accurate regarding most solids:
a: particles in a solid vibrate around fixed positions
particles in a solid have no kinetic energy
solids have definite melting points in their pure state
e: Even frozen in place, particles in a solid are secretly dancing with a little bit of kinetic energy!

q: What is the atomic number of Uranium
e: Uranium proudly packs ninety-two positive protons right at its bustling heart.

q: What are the DC voltages from conventional A, AA and D cell batteries?
e: Whether skinny or chunky, these friendly everyday batteries all pack the exact same electric push of 1.5 volts.

q: Which of the following is a strong acid since it ionizes almost completely in water:
e: Sulfuric acid, or H2SO4, jumps into water and completely lets go of its parts, making it a famously strong acid.

q: Researchers at Argonne National Lab Chemical Sciences and Engineering Division are studying the decomposition of H2CO into H2 and CO. If they are specifically examining the hydrogen-carbon bond stretching and breaking, what type of structure are they examining?
e: Caught right in the middle of stretching and snapping apart, the molecule is in its fleeting transition state, like a runner mid-leap!

q: Which of the following is NOT true about boiling liquids:
a: all boiling liquids are too hot to touch
the boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is 373.15 kelvin
the boiling point of a liquid depends on the surface pressure above the liquid
adding a handful of table salt to a quart of boiling water will change its boiling point
e: Some liquids boil at freezing temperatures, so boiling does not mean something is always scorching hot to touch!

q: What fuel is used in a nuclear reactor?
e: Nuclear reactors run on uranium-235, special heavy atoms that eagerly split apart to make giant bursts of heat!

q: DOE researchers recently were able to capture a 3D sequence of the water- splitting reaction of photosynthesis in action. The oxygen atoms released by this step are eventually incorporated by photosynthesis into what molecule?
e: Plants crack open water droplets and pair up the leftover oxygen atoms, puffing out fresh oxygen gas for us to breathe!

q: Which of the following materials best prevents the flow of electricity?
e: Without any mineral buddies to carry a spark, pure distilled water politely stops electricity right in its tracks.

q: What role is fission-based nuclear power used for in the energy production and distribution grid?
e: Nuclear plants are steady giants that hum day and night, providing reliable baseload power to keep our towns glowing!

q: Which of the following is a metalloid?
e: Silicon is a quirky metalloid, acting half like a shiny metal and half like a shy nonmetal.

q: Which of the following elements would be expected to have the most polar bond when bonded with oxygen?
e: Oxygen tugs electrons much harder than tiny hydrogen, creating an uneven, super-polar tug-of-war game between them.

q: Which of the following is closest to the theoretical mechanical advantage of a screw with a mean diameter of 1 centimeter and a lead of 2 millimeters?
e: Turning around a one-centimeter circle covers about thirty-one millimeters, giving sixteen times the pushing power over a tiny two-millimeter step!

q: Which of the following fuels is cooled cryogenically to -260 Fahrenheit?
e: To travel across the ocean, natural gas gets chilled to minus 260 degrees, shrinking into a neat puddle called liquefied natural gas.

q: Which of the following is a mixture?
e: Air is a breezy party where nitrogen, oxygen, and other gases swirl together freely as a happy mixture.

q: Which of the following elements can form a monatomic gas at standard temperature and pressure?
e: Neon is a noble loner with full electron shells, happily floating around all by itself as a single atom.

q: Which of the following elements is able to escape Earth's gravitational field in significant amounts?
e: Hydrogen is the featherweight champion of elements, so light and fast that Earth's gravity just cannot keep it from floating into space.

q: Which of the following activities will increase your carbon footprint?
a: Eating a more local vegetarian diet
Keeping your family's car tires inflated to the correct level
Using public transportation like buses and trains
e: Raising cattle takes lots of land and food, plus burping cows release potent methane gas that puffs up your footprint.

q: In 1953, two scientists, Stanley Miller and Harold Urey, conducted a famous experiment on the origin of life. They passed an electrical charge through a closed system containing methane, ammonia, hydrogen, and water. What did this process produce that led to the currently accepted theory of biogenesis?
e: Zapping pretend ancient storm clouds made amino acids, the tiny, cheerful building blocks life needed to start piecing itself together!

q: The secret to the prevention of oxidation is to provide a layer of protection between the exposed material and the air. Which of the following is NOT an example of a process used to prevent oxidation?
a: Putting lemon juice on exposed fruit
e: Anodizing does not stop oxidation because it actually uses controlled oxidation to grow a tough, colorful outer shell on aluminum.

q: The combination of two deuterium [doo-TEER-ee- uhm] atoms to form a single helium atom is known as which of the following?
e: Two little atoms hug so tightly that they merge into one, showing off the powerhouse magic of nuclear fusion!

q: Which of the following liquids at room temperature and 1 atmosphere would have the GREATEST surface tension:
e: Pure water molecules hold hands so tightly that they create the strongest surface tension, acting like a tiny trampoline.

q: Which of the following compounds is binary?
e: A binary compound is a simple duo made of just two ingredients, like calcium chloride holding hands with only calcium and chlorine.

q: Cellulosic biomass can be converted via fermentation to what usable form of energy?
e: Tiny microbes happily ferment tough plant scraps, turning that woody green lunch into a powerful liquid fuel called ethanol!

q: Which of the following BEST explains why the halogens are found in nature as compounds or ions:
a: they have an excess of neutrons and are unstable in pure form
they have 1 electron in their outer shell
they need only one electron to fill their outermost shell so they are highly reactive
they are non-metals with unfilled energy shells
e: Halogens are eager party guests who need only one last electron to complete their circle, making them react with almost anyone!

q: Alkali metals all have the same:
a: number of electrons in their outer shells
e: Every alkali metal family member shares the exact same trait: just one lone electron dancing in its outermost shell.

q: Which of the following substances is likely to be the most reactive in water?
e: Drop little sodium into water, and it fizzes, zips around, and throws a fiery, bubbly party in an instant!

q: Steel is an alloy of Iron and Carbon.
e: It is true because strong iron mixes with a pinch of carbon to become super-tough steel!

q: Which of the following isotopes was responsible for the only known naturally occurring fission reactors, the Oklo Fossil Reactors?
e: Deep underground, special uranium-235 atoms were packed just right to split apart, powering Earth's only natural nuclear reactor millions of years ago.

q: Which of the following best describes static electricity?
a: Any interaction between a person and a metal object
The charging of a neutral object by an electrically charged object
The net accumulation of electric charges on an object
The movement of electrons through a conducting material
e: It happens when a bunch of tiny electric charges pile up in one spot, just waiting to give you a tickly zap!

q: Which of the following is the scientific term for the energy needed to transform a given quantity of a substance from a liquid to a gas at standard pressure:
e: Heat of vaporization is the exact energy needed to help liquid molecules take flight as a floating gas vapor.

q: Which of the following transformations is NOT a chemical change?
a: Mixing solutions of magnesium sulfate and barium nitrate
Heating calcium carbonate until it expels a gas
e: When ethanol vaporizes into gas, its molecules just float up to stretch, staying the exact same alcohol with no chemical change.

q: What type of battery is commonly found in rechargeable consumer electronics?
e: Lithium-ion batteries are trusty little powerhouses that happily drink up energy again and again to keep our favorite gadgets awake.

q: Five batteries are connected in series. A sixth battery is added to the circuit in series without changing the resistance of the circuit. What happens to the current?
a: Increases only if the new battery has a higher voltage than the others
e: Adding another battery gives an extra push of voltage, sending even more electric current rushing through the wire!

q: The octet rule MOST directly involves which of the following:
a: only atoms with 8 or more protons
the balance of neutrons to protons
the loss of protons in radioactive decay
e: Atoms love holding hands and sharing their outer valence electrons until they reach a cozy, stable group of eight.

q: Which of the following inventions is Alessandro Volta credited with?
e: Long ago, Volta stacked metal discs like a clever sandwich to create the world's very first battery.

q: Mendeleev [mendah-LAY-ev] organized the elements according to their reactivity. Which of the following elements would be grouped with lithium?
e: Sodium sits right under lithium in the same chemical family, happily sharing its bubbly, energetic personality.

q: Gravity assist is a great way to save money on spacecraft fuel. Which of the following is one reason NASA might NOT be able to use it to send a spacecraft to Neptune?
a: The planets are rarely lined up in the right places
Gravity assist only works for small planets
The gravity of gas giant planets is difficult to predict
Neptune's orbit crossing with Pluto creates a chaotic system
e: Planets dance in giant circles, but they rarely line up just right to slingshot a spaceship all the way to Neptune.

q: Which of the following most likely occurs when one molecule is oxidized:
a: there is a release in work
e: Chemistry loves teamwork, so whenever one molecule gets oxidized and gives away electrons, another molecule is reduced by catching them!

q: Which of the following does not affect the reaction rate of the Haber synthesis of ammonia?
e: Inside the sealed tank where gases make ammonia, outside humidity cannot sneak in to change how fast they mix.

q: For which of the following molecules would elemental analysis give you the molecular formula?
e: Because SiO2 is already in its simplest ratio of one silicon to two oxygens, testing reveals its exact formula!

q: Which of the following elements is often added to steel to make it harder?
e: Adding shiny chromium gives steel extra strength, locking its atoms tight to make it tough and scratch-resistant.

q: Which of the following reactions is endothermic?
a: Chlorine gas reacts with hydrogen gas to form hydrogen chloride gas
Liquid water vaporizes to yield steam
Sodium metal reacts with water to yield sodium hydroxide and hydrogen gas
Liquid water freezes to yield solid ice
e: Water droplets must eagerly soak up heat from the stove before they can transform into floating puffs of steam.

q: Which of the following elements is NOT a gas in its standard state:
e: While other elements float off as airy gases, bromine prefers to splash around as a heavy, reddish liquid.

q: Which of the following is a substance that can accept a pair of electrons from another substance?
e: A Lewis acid is like a lonely puzzle piece, happily opening its arms to accept a pair of electrons.

q: Which of the following elements is NOT diatomic in its natural state?
e: While twin elements travel in pairs of two, sulfur prefers rolling around in a giant ring of eight atoms.

q: All liquids are:
a: Unable to accommodate the size of their containers
At a state of higher kinetic energy than any solids
e: Liquid molecules are already packed together so snugly that no matter how hard you push, they refuse to be squished any tighter.

q: Which of the following is an example of a compound with an ionic bond?
e: Sodium happily gives electrons away to sulfur like a gift, creating charged partners that stick together with an ionic bond!

q: The electrical potential or power of a battery is an expression of its:
e: Voltage measures a battery's electrical potential, acting like an eager push ready to send energy leaping into action!

q: Which of the following is MOST commonly used to separate substances based on solubility differences:
e: In paper chromatography, colors race across the page, separating as the most soluble inks travel the farthest.

q: Which of the following elements is NOT a metalloid [MET-ah-loid]?
e: Silicon and germanium like playing both sides, but carbon is proudly and completely a nonmetal.

q: Which of the following molecules is considered the most polar:
e: Greedy fluorine tugs electrons away from tiny hydrogen in HF, creating a huge tug-of-war charge that makes it the most polar.

q: Researchers at Lawrence Livermore National Lab recently studied a new phase of water ice in the lab. What type of bond is responsible for holding together adjacent water molecules in normal water ice?
e: Water molecules love holding hands using hydrogen bonds, linking tightly together to freeze into chilly, solid ice crystals.

q: Which of the following is the typical operating voltage of a fuel cell?
e: Like a busy little battery, a typical working fuel cell quietly hums along at about 0.7 volts of electricity.

q: Researchers at Pacific Northwest National Lab are studying the process of aberrant O-linked glycosylation [glye-kaw-sil-AY-shun] that occurs in some neurodegenerative diseases. In this process, sugars are linked to proteins through oxygen atoms. Which of the following best describes when this process occurs in cells?
e: Once a cell finishes translating and building a fresh protein, it decorates it with sweet sugar tags.

q: Which of the following correctly explains why liquid fuel rockets are preferred over solid fuel rockets for long term space missions?
a: Liquid fuel rockets can store more fuel
The use of liquid fuel rockets can be stopped and restarted
Liquid fuel is safer than solid fuel
Liquid fuel is less volatile than solid fuel
e: Space explorers love liquid engines because you can switch them off to glide, and then restart them whenever you need.

q: Which of the following substances has the highest heat of vaporization?
e: Water molecules hug each other so tightly that it takes a giant heap of heat to turn them into steam.

q: Which of the following is one of the main disadvantages of molten carbonate fuel cells, when compared to solid oxide fuel cells?
a: Risk of corrosion at high temperatures
They require an external reformer to convert more energy-dense fuels to hydrogen
e: The melted liquid inside gets so sizzling hot that it can slowly eat away and corrode its own metal home.

q: Which of the following is a diatomic molecule?
e: Diatomic means two atoms joined together, just like these two friendly hydrogen buddies holding hands in H2.

q: When a hydrogen atom is in its ground state, what is TRUE about its electron?
a: It is in its lowest energy level
It has escaped from the atom
e: In its cozy ground state, this little electron snuggles down into the lowest energy level for the ultimate nap.

q: What is the theoretical maximum voltage that can be produced from a hydrogen fuel cell?
e: Even on its absolute best day, nature only lets a single hydrogen fuel cell reach a top limit of 1.23 volts.

q: About how fast, in meters per second, does a released neutron travel in a fission reaction?
e: When an atom splits, a zippy neutron zooms away at an astonishing 2 times 10 to the seventh meters per second!

q: In order for a compound to be analyzed using infrared spectroscopy, the molecule must exhibit a change in which of the following?
e: To dance with infrared light, a molecule must wiggle its electric balance, creating a shifting dipole moment.

q: Why do noble gases almost never form chemical bonds?
a: It is difficult for gases to form bonds
They have completely filled outer valence shells
They have very small atomic radii [RAY-dee-eye]
e: Noble gases have completely full outer shells, so they sit back happily and never need to trade electrons.

q: At the Environmental Molecular Sciences Laboratory, part of the Pacific Northwest National Laboratory, scientists are examining the formation of soot using jet fuel. How is soot formed?
e: When fuel does not get enough air to burn completely, messy leftover carbon gathers into dark, smoky flakes of soot.

q: Sodium becomes positively charged when it combines with chlorine because sodium:
e: Generous sodium happily gives away one negative little electron, leaving it with a cheerful positive charge!

q: Which of the following is NOT true of chemical reactions:
a: energy is either absorbed or released
chemical bonds are broken and formed
e: Some reactions are a one-way trip, like baking a cake—you cannot unbake it back into eggs and flour!

q: In which of the following processes does the entropy of the system decrease?
e: When silver chloride precipitates, messy floating particles snap together into neat solid crystals, tidying up the room.
