q: Under what conditions does the behavior of real gases deviate most from that predicted by the ideal gas law?
e: Squeezed tightly under high pressure and chilled by the cold, crowded gas particles stop behaving like ideal little ghosts.

q: Which of the following is a difficulty related to nuclear fusion?
a: The temperature required to start the reaction
The lack of deuterium on Earth
The products of the fusion process are radioactive
e: Copying the sun is tricky because you need scorching, blistering temperatures just to get the fusion party started!

q: Which of the following compounds is covalently bonded?
e: In carbon monoxide, carbon and oxygen act like friendly neighbors who share their electrons instead of giving them away.

q: Sterling silver contains 92.5% silver and 7.5% copper. Which of the following substances is the solute?
e: Silver is the big host here, making the smaller amount of copper the guest known as the solute.

q: The sum of the number of protons and neutrons in an atom of an element is referred to as the element's what?
e: When protons and neutrons cuddle together in the center, adding them up gives an atom its total mass number.

q: The U.S. Department of Energy is currently developing methods aimed at carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS). How can the CO2 captured in this way also be used to increase energy output in the U.S.?
e: Engineers pump trapped carbon dioxide deep underground to nudge stubborn oil to the surface, helping those fields produce even more energy!

q: Which of the following compounds is NOT used as fuel in a nuclear reactor?
e: Uranium-236 is the sleepy leftover made after splitting atoms, so it cannot be used as reactor fuel.

q: Which of the following is an electronic device that amplifies electronic signals and was used as a switching device in the first electronic computers:
e: Long before tiny chips, glowing glass vacuum tubes acted like little lightbulbs, boosting signals and flipping electric switches.

q: Researchers at SLAC [slack] are developing zeolite catalysts for methanol production. Which of the following statements best explains why zeolites are such effective catalysts?
a: They have a lot of pores
e: Zeolites act like tiny rock sponges, packed with millions of cozy pores where busy molecules meet up to make new things!

q: Coal is primarily used to generate electricity. Which of the following is the second largest use of coal?
e: After making electricity, coal is baked red-hot in giant furnaces to melt iron rocks into shiny steel for skyscrapers!

q: Which of the following phases of matter can change shape, but is nearly incompressable?
e: Water loves to shape-shift into any cup it visits, but its snug molecules refuse to squeeze tighter, making liquids nearly incompressible.

q: Which of the following elements has the largest electron affinity?
e: Tiny fluorine is desperately hungry for just one more electron, making it snatch them up the fastest!

q: An element in the second column of the periodic table will have the most similar chemical reactivity to which of the following?
a: The element directly to the left
The element directly to the right
The element at the end of the row
e: Elements in the very same column are like copycat family members, sharing almost the exact same personality.

q: Methoxyethane is an example of what class of organic molecule?
e: An oxygen atom happily holds hands between two carbon groups, making methoxyethane a classic member of the ether family.

q: On the periodic table, potassium is in what family?
e: Potassium belongs to the alkali metal family, a super lively group of soft metals that love to react quickly.

q: Which of these types of heat transfer explains how the water molecules in coffee carry scent molecules across a restaurant?
e: Rising warm air swirls like an invisible dance, using convection to carry that cozy coffee smell straight to your nose.

q: Francium has the lowest electronegativity of the elements. This would indicate that francium is in what corner of the periodic chart:
e: Francium relaxes way down in the lower left corner, being the gentle giant that cares the least about grabbing electrons.

q: Which of the following crops is NOT used widely in the western hemisphere as a biofuel feedstock?
e: While corn and sugarcane power our cars, wheat prefers staying in the kitchen to become yummy bread and tasty treats!

q: Which of the following properties of water is most responsible for the tempering influence of the ocean on climate?
e: The vast ocean acts like a warm sponge, using its huge heat capacity to keep nearby weather delightfully mild.

q: What country made the largest monetary investment in solar, wind, biofuels, and other low-carbon energy technologies in 2014?
e: Back in 2014, China spent the biggest mountain of treasure to build sunny solar panels and giant, spinning wind turbines.

q: A precipitation reaction is used to make which of the following?
e: Cooking sweet fudge forces sugar crystals to suddenly tumble out of the warm syrup, building a delicious solid treat!

q: A reaction where the system absorbs energy is known as which of the following?
e: An endothermic reaction acts like a thirsty sponge for heat, greedily soaking up surrounding energy to make things chilly.

q: Which of the following elements does not occur naturally in nature:
e: Technetium is a shy element that nature forgot to make, so curious scientists had to create it in a lab!

q: Which of the following elements is a metalloid?
e: Silicon is a clever metalloid that cannot decide between being shiny metal or dull rock, happily behaving like both.

q: The nucleus of the most common isotope of hydrogen is formed from which of the following?
e: At the heart of everyday hydrogen, a single brave proton sits all by itself without any neutron friends.

q: Au on the Periodic Table refers to which element?
e: Au stands for gold, coming from an old word for glowing dawn, shining bright like buried treasure.

q: What country is the world's largest producer of natural gas?
e: Deep underground, the busy United States taps into hidden energy pockets, pumping out more natural gas than any other country on Earth!

q: Which of the following correctly describes the typical progression from dead organic matter to coal?
e: Squished under heavy earth for millions of years, soggy peat slowly transforms into lignite, then bituminous coal, and finally shiny anthracite!

q: Which of the following elements has the highest boiling point?
e: Gold atoms grip each other with amazing strength, needing incredible, blazing heat before they finally let go and boil into vapor.

q: Along with Oxygen, which element is primarily responsible for the sky appearing blue?
e: Nitrogen fills most of our air, happily scattering blue sunlight in every direction to paint the sky above us.

q: There are many beautiful colors in an aurora. Which of the following primarily determines the colors you see?
a: Whether you are observing the aurora borealis or the aurora australis
What atoms or molecules the solar wind ions collide with
What time of night it is
How close you are to city light
e: When energetic space particles bump into different gas molecules high above us, each gas glows with its own special, dazzling color!

q: In a closed system, exergonic reactions may NOT increase the available:
e: These reactions freely release heat and energy, but inside a closed space, they cannot increase the available pressure.

q: Which of the following men does not have a chemical element named after him?
e: Even though an apple helped him discover gravity, Sir Isaac Newton never got his own element on the periodic table.

q: Which of the following elements is released during coal burning and contributes to acid rain?
e: When coal burns, hidden sulfur escapes into the sky, mixing with fluffy clouds to turn peaceful raindrops into sour, acidic rain.

q: Hydrocarbons that contain at least one double bond between carbon atoms are classified as which of the following?
e: Sharing a double bond means carbons have room left over for more hydrogen friends, making the molecule unsaturated.

q: You dip a piece of pH paper into a one-molar solution of hydrochloric acid. What color does it turn?
e: That fierce acid has so much sour power that the paper blushes a fiery red right away.

q: Which of the following pairs of types of solids and their properties is NOT correctly matched?
e: Network solids like diamonds lock their atoms so tightly together that they crack instead of bending into new shapes.

q: Which of the following correctly explains why electrolysis is not used for the industrial production of hydrogen?
a: Hydrogen gas produced by electrolysis is relatively impure
Hydrogen gas is produced very slowly by electrolysis
Hydrogen gas produced by electrolysis is relatively expensive
Hydrogen gas produced by electrolysis is unreactive
e: Splitting water with electricity takes heaps of costly power, making that hydrogen way too expensive for big factories to produce.

q: Which of the following is NOT a base unit of measure in the metric system?
e: In the official metric club, the heavy kilogram got the badge as the true base unit, while the little gram is just a helper.

q: The mass spectrum for a compound has a parent peak at 80 M over Z and another peak at 65 M over Z. This indicates that what species is present in the compound?
e: A tiny piece weighing fifteen units snapped off, which is the exact calling card of a lost methyl group!

q: Scientists supported by the Department of Energy are studying vibrational energy levels in molecules. What region of the electromagnetic spectrum are they using to probe these energy levels?
e: Invisible infrared waves have just the right cozy warmth to make tiny molecules wiggle and dance to a lively beat.

q: Bio Syngas is a synthetic composition of what pair of gases?
e: Bio syngas is a bubbly partnership where carbon monoxide and energetic hydrogen team up to make useful fuel.

q: A chemist might use filter paper and a funnel when she wants to do which of the following separations?
e: Filter paper catches clumsy solid pieces like a net, letting the polite liquid slip right through into the funnel.

q: Brookhaven National Lab researchers are developing catalysts to break down sarin [SAIR-in] gas. Sarin is a poison that inhibits what neurotransmitter-related enzyme?
e: Acetylcholinesterase is a busy helper that clears nerve signals, but sneaky sarin freezes this enzyme right in its tracks!

q: Which of the following components of a reaction is decreased when an organic catalyst is added to speed up the rate of a reaction?
e: A catalyst acts like a helpful shortcut, lowering the steep energy hill molecules have to climb to react.

q: Which of the following elements is found in Period 2 and Group 4A of the Periodic Table:
e: If you follow the chart's map to row two and column 4A, you will discover clever carbon waiting there.

q: Which of the following metals appears on flame tests as bright green and is responsible for blue colors in fireworks?
e: Copper loves showing off in fire, glowing bright green in campfire flames and dazzling the night sky with brilliant blue fireworks!

q: Which of the following materials in pure form would register the LOWEST amount of ohms for a given electric current at 20C if all other variables are constant:
e: Shiny silver gives electricity the smoothest, easiest ride of all, offering the lowest resistance to any traveling spark.

q: During beta decay, carbon-14 decays into nitrogen-14 along with an electron and what other particle?
e: When the electron zooms away, a tiny, ghost-like antineutrino zips out alongside it to balance the cosmic books.

q: When each of the following metals is added to a dilute solution of hydrochloric acid, which will react the fastest?
e: Magnesium is full of bubbly energy, eagerly tossing electrons to the acid much faster than the sleepier metals.

q: Which of the following is NOT a transition metal?
e: Shiny aluminum skips the middle neighborhood of transition metals, living on its own colorful side of the chart.

q: Which of the following choices is NOT an example of a chemical change:
a: shiny new copper tarnishing to a green color
bubbles forming in a solution of vinegar following the addition of baking soda
e: Glowing red from heat is just steel blushing hot, not changing into a whole new substance!

q: If you stick a thermometer into a frozen slurry of lemonade as it is melting, you will find that the reading on the thermometer is:
a: Not changing, as long as there is ice
e: All the warmth goes into melting icy slush first, so the temperature stays perfectly still until the ice disappears.

q: Which of the following is classified as a homogeneous [hoh-muh-JEE-nee-uhs] mixture?
e: In a solution, tiny particles blend so smoothly together that every single sip looks and tastes perfectly uniform.

q: An electrical generator converts:
e: Like a whirling wind turbine, a generator captures busy mechanical motion and turns all that spinning movement into zippy electrical energy.

q: Deuterium is an isotope of which element?
e: Deuterium is simply a hydrogen atom that packed an extra neutron friend into its backpack, making it a bit heavier!

q: Silver nitrate reacts with copper metal to form copper nitrate and silver metal. What type of reaction is this?
e: Copper tosses tiny electrons over to silver like a friendly game of catch, making this a redox swap!

q: The atomic number of molybdenum [muh-LIB-den-um] is 42. What does this number indicate?
a: Every atom has 42 total protons & neutrons in the nucleus
Every atom has a mass of 42 a.m.u.
Every atom has 42 protons in the nucleus
Every atom will form bonds that measure 42 degrees
e: Every molybdenum atom proudly wears the number forty-two, which tells us forty-two protons are cuddled inside its nucleus.

q: If each of the following objects is allowed to roll down a ramp without slipping, which reaches the bottom with the greatest speed?
e: A solid sphere keeps its weight tucked neatly near its middle, helping it roll downhill faster than any other shape!

q: The second electron shell in an atom can hold up to how many electrons, and contains how many different orbital shapes, respectively?
e: The second shell has two cozy room shapes, sphere and dumbbell, fitting up to eight happy electrons.

q: Consider a chemical reaction with a standard enthalpy change of 10 kilojoules per mole and a standard entropy change of 10 joules per mole kelvin. When is this reaction spontaneous?
e: Crank the heat above one thousand kelvins, and the messy energy finally wins, letting the reaction run wild on its own!

q: The density of an object is a property that depends on:
a: the total volume of the object
the liquid the object is suspended in
e: Density is a secret recipe built into the material itself, so it does not depend on any of those things!

q: What substances, by definition, produce ions when dissolved in water?
e: Electrolytes love swimming in water, splitting into little charged ions that help electricity dance right through.

q: For a brick of gold, which of the following properties would change if you transported the brick from the surface of the Earth to the surface of the Moon?
e: The brick keeps all its stuff, but the Moon pulls more gently, so its weight drops magically!

q: What is the term for the heat content of a system?
e: Enthalpy is the special scientific name for all the cozy heat energy tucked inside a system's pockets.

q: Which of the following is closest to the percentage of the nuclear power reactors in the U.S. that use nuclear fusion for developing the heat required for generating electricity?
e: Humans haven't tamed star-power yet, so exactly zero percent of our power plants run on fusion.

q: A piece of zinc is in a beaker of water. As you add hydrochloric acid to the beaker you see small gas bubbles forming around the zinc. What is this gas?
e: The hungry acid nibbles at zinc, freeing trapped hydrogen gas to bubble up like fizzy soda pop.

q: Which of the following is the lowest atomic number above which all elements are synthetic?
e: Nature crafted elements up through uranium at number 92, but every heavier one had to be cooked up by humans in a lab!

q: Which of the following molecules has a pyramidal [peer-uh-MIH-dul] geometry?
e: Ammonia sits like a neat little three-legged stool, where one nitrogen atom perches proudly on top like a tiny pyramid roof.

q: Which of the following kinds of solutions is a mixture in which the solvent has dissolved all the solute it can at a given temperature?
e: When a drink is saturated, it is completely full of dissolved sugar and politely says, "No more sweets for me, please!"

q: Which of the following is the minimum amount of energy needed to start a chemical reaction?
e: Molecules need a little wake-up push called activation energy before they can begin their exciting chemical adventure.

q: Which of the following is NOT true of plug-in hybrid electric vehicles?
a: They can drive using only electricity for between 10 and 40 miles
They are powered both by a battery and an internal combustion engine
Inductive charging equipment is systematically used to recharge the batteries
e: These clever cars drink power through ordinary plug-in cords, because inductive wireless pads are not routinely used to charge them.

q: Which of the following energy sources produces the greatest carbon dioxide emissions?
e: Burning dark, dusty coal unleashes far more carbon dioxide into the air than any other power source.

q: What term is used to describe the number density of water vapor in the air?
e: Humidity simply measures how many invisible water droplets are floating around, giving the air that cozy, damp hug.

q: Which one of these scientists conducted the Gold Foil Experiment which concluded that atoms are mostly made of empty space?
e: Ernest Rutherford shot tiny beams at golden foil and gasped to discover that atoms are mostly empty, open space.

q: Approximately how many days could a single person be fed from the corn needed to produce enough 100% ethanol to fuel a single SUV?
e: That thirsty SUV gulps down enough corn in one tank to fill your belly every day for a whole year, all 365 days!

q: Which of the following is an example of an amorphous solid?
e: Unlike neatly stacked blocks, the atoms in glass froze in a wild, scrambled jumble without forming tidy crystals.

q: In any given row of the periodic table, which of the following families typically has the largest neutral atomic radius?
e: Starting each row, alkali metals puff up the biggest because their centers have not pulled their electrons in tight yet.

q: Which of the following could be used to neutralize an acid spill?
e: Calcium oxide acts as a trusty base, bravely neutralizing wild acid spills to bring everything back into safe balance.

q: A positron is an antiparticle of a what?
e: A positron is the mirror twin of an electron, matching its tiny size perfectly but wearing a positive charge instead.

q: Which of the following characteristics best describes metals?
a: Brittle, highly reactive, and have low melting points
Lustrous, malleable, and are good conductors
Dense, form salts, and are highly reactive
Hard, form negatively charged ions, and are good resistors
e: True metals love to gleam in the light, bend gently instead of snapping, and pass electricity along like a baton.

q: Deionized water is water with which of the following removed?
e: Deionizing sweeps away charged mineral visitors like iron, leaving the water delightfully pure and free of stray electric charges.

q: Which of the following is the most common electronic device used for storing electric energy in a process commonly called charging:
e: A capacitor acts like a tiny energy sponge, happily soaking up electric zaps when charging and holding them tight until needed.

q: Which of the following is NOT a hazard that would be listed on the Material Safety Data Sheet for concentrated sulfuric acid:
e: While sulfuric acid is a fierce liquid that can burn skin, it will not catch fire, so it is never labeled flammable.

q: Which of the following CANNOT be readily used as a source of energy in a fuel cell?
e: A fuel cell drinks hydrogen to make clean power, while oxygen only helps the reaction and cannot be the fuel.

q: Which of the following materials is the best thermal conductor?
e: Metals love sharing warmth, and solid aluminum quickly passes heat along like a speedy runner winning a relay race.

q: Which chemical element has the lowest boiling point?
e: Helium atoms are super independent and barely stick together, boiling into gas at the coldest temperature around.

q: The atomic number of chlorine is 17. What does this necessarily imply about chlorine atoms?
a: They have a mass number of 34
e: An element's atomic number is its special identity card, always counting the exact number of protons tucked inside its heart.

q: An electron in the second main energy level and the second sublevel of an atom is described by which of the following orbital designations?
e: The number two marks the second energy level, while the letter p labels its second room, neatly making the address 2p!

q: Which of the following is NOT an example of a physical change?
e: Rusting turns shiny iron into completely new crumbly stuff, making it a chemical adventure instead of a physical one!

q: Identify which of the following factors must be measured in order to apply Archimedes' principle [ahr-kuh-MEE-deez].
a: Temperature of liquid in which an object is submerged
Density of liquid in which an object is submerged
e: To see how high an object floats, you must know the liquid’s density, revealing how heavy each splash truly is.

q: Which of the following is the pH of a substance with a hydronium concentration of 1 10-13 moles per liter?
e: Counting thirteen zeroes behind the decimal point gives this slippery, super basic solution a matching pH of thirteen.

q: Maxwell based his theory of electromagnetic waves on the hypothesis that a changing electric field gives rise to which of the following?
e: Whenever a shifting electric field ripples, it magically sparks a companion magnetic field to dance right alongside it.

q: Which of the following usually indicates a physical change?
e: Melting or freezing simply changes a substance's outfit, keeping the exact same identity underneath!

q: Which of the following laws could be used to calculate the current flowing through a resistor when it is connected to a battery?
e: Ohm's law acts like a friendly math bridge, connecting battery voltage, resistance, and the marching electric current.

q: The largest portion of biomass fuel in the United States is made from which of the following?
e: Friendly trees do the heavy lifting, as chopped logs and wood scraps make up most of America's plant fuel!

q: Which of the following did NOT come from a once-living organism?
e: Unlike coal or oil from ancient critters, uranium is a heavy metal born deep inside exploding stars long ago.

q: When making homemade ice cream, salt is added to crushed ice surrounding the cream mixture. Which of the following does NOT occur when the salt is added to the ice?
a: The freezing temperature of the cream mixture is lowered
The freezing temperature of the ice is lowered
The temperature of the system is lowered
Some of the ice is melted
e: The salt only touches the outside ice, so it cannot change the cream mixture's own freezing point at all!

q: Which of the following BEST describes a cathode ray?
a: A device that emits light through a process of optical amplification based on the stimulated emission of photons
An electrode through which electric current flows out of a polarized electrical device
A stream of electrons observed in vacuum tubes
An electrode through which electric current flows into a polarized electrical device
e: A cathode ray is just a zippy stream of tiny electrons racing happily through an empty glass tube.

q: Which of the following quantities is kept constant by a gas undergoing an isobaric [eye-soh-BARE-ik] process?
e: In an isobaric journey, a gas can expand or warm up, but its pushing pressure stays totally steady.

q: Which product of coal gasification can be used for power production?
e: Cooking coal into gas sets tiny hydrogen free, and this energetic gas happily zips off to make electric power!

q: Which of the following groups consists entirely of allotropes of carbon?
a: Lonsdaleite (read as: lohnz-day-LEET), graphene, and fullerene
Fullerene, lonsdaleite (read as: lohnz-day-LEET), and alamosite
e: Carbon loves dress-up, building sheets of graphene, tiny soccer balls called fullerenes, and super-tough lonsdaleite all from pure carbon atoms.

q: Gasoline is mostly composed of which of the following?
e: Tiny hydrogen and carbon pals link hands to form hydrocarbons, packing gasoline full of bouncy energy for the road.

q: Which of the following has the greatest density:
e: Gold packs its heavy atoms so closely together that it squeezes way more matter into tiny spaces than the others.

q: An electric vehicle has two stages. If the first stage, the battery, has an efficiency of 90% and the second stage, the inverter, has an efficiency of 80%, calculate the approximate overall efficiency of the vehicle.
e: When the battery shares ninety percent of its spark and the inverter keeps eighty percent, multiplying them leaves seventy-two percent ready to roll!

q: Which of the following is closest to the most probable radius, in angstroms, of an electron in the ground state of a hydrogen atom?
e: Hydrogen’s lonely little electron loves to dance about point-five angstroms away from home, keeping its cozy center just half a step away.

q: For a given redox [REE-dox] reaction, which of the following pairs of thermodynamic statements is NOT possible?
a: K-equilibium greater than 1 and delta-H greater than zero
E-cell greater than zero and delta-G greater than zero
delta-H greater than zero and delta-G greater than zero
K-equilibium greater than 1 and E-cell greater than zero
e: An eager reaction with a positive cell voltage always gives away free energy, so delta-G must be negative instead of positive.

q: Which of the following salts will produce an acidic solution when dissolved in water?
e: Tiny aluminum ions get greedy in water, tugging on water molecules to set loose sour hydrogen bits that make aluminum nitrate acidic.

q: According to VSEPR bonding theory, if one of the bonded atoms in a trigonal bipyramidal molecule is replaced by 2 electron pairs, the molecule will assume what geometric shape, such as in ClF3:
e: Two chubby electron pairs push the other three bonded atoms sideways, nudging them into a neat little T-shaped pose.

q: A variety of manufacturing processes may be employed in nanotechnology. Which of the following processes can coat almost anything by transferring material from its source to the substrate without changing chemical composition?
e: Vapor deposition lets tiny particles float like a gentle mist, settling softly onto surfaces as a snug coat without changing what they are.

q: Which of the following elements can stably bond with three atoms, leaving it with an empty p orbital?
e: Friendly boron is perfectly happy sharing bonds with three atoms, leaving an empty little p-orbital pocket tucked away for later.

q: A student observes the dimerization [dye-mur-ih-ZAY-shun] of a solution of cyclopentadiene [sigh-kloh-penta-DYE-een]. Assuming the reaction is second-order in cyclopentadiene, which of the following will she observe as she continues to monitor the reaction?
e: As the reacting molecules thin out, bumping into partners takes longer, so each half-life stretches out and increases.

q: A student performs combustion analysis on a compound composed of carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, and possibly nitrogen - with molecular mass 56 grams per mole. One mole of the compound reacts with 3 moles of oxygen gas to generate 2 moles of carbon dioxide, 1 mole of water, and an unknown product. How many nitrogen atoms are in the chemical formula?
e: Matching the puzzle pieces of carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen leaves room for just fourteen mass units, meaning exactly one nitrogen atom fits.

q: Which of the following acts as a Lewis acid in the presence of water to form carbonic acid?
e: Carbon dioxide happily welcomes an electron pair from water to craft bubbly carbonic acid, making it the Lewis acid of the pair.

q: The reaction CuCl2 + Na2S CuS + 2NaCl2, is an example of what class of chemical reaction:
e: The copper and sodium swap their partners like dancers changing places, which makes this a double replacement reaction!

q: Which of the following is a disadvantage of flexible fuel vehicles?
a: They get about 25% fewer miles per gallon when fueled with E85
They experience significant loss in power when operating on E85
They are very different than gasoline-only models
e: Ethanol carries less energy per drop than gasoline, so flex-fuel cars get about twenty-five percent fewer miles per gallon on E85.

q: Which of the following correctly identifies the effect that the presence of an uncompetitive inhibitor has on a Lineweaver - plot?
a: Km [K-M] and Vmax [V max] are raised, and the ratio Km/Vmax [K-M over V max] increases
Km and Vmax are raised, and the ratio Km/Vmax is unchanged
Km and Vmax are lowered, and the ratio Km/Vmax is unchanged
Km and Vmax are lowered, and the ratio Km/Vmax decreases
e: This sneaky inhibitor slows both Km and Vmax down by the exact same amount, leaving their special ratio completely unchanged.

q: Which of the following is NOT a polyprotic acid?
e: Formic acid has only one single proton to give away, so it cannot be polyprotic like acids with multiple protons to share.

q: Many salts dissolve to a greater extent in hot water than cold water. Which of the following best explains this fact?
a: There are more collisions between salt ions and water molecules at a higher temperature
The ion-dipole forces between water molecules and salt ions increase with temperature
e: Most salts love soaking up heat to break apart, so dissolving endothermically helps them melt away much better in warm water.

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the central tenets of Valence Bond Theory?
a: Whenever possible, a bond involving p or d electrons will orient in the direction that minimizes overlap
The extent of the overlap depends on the shapes and directions of the orbitals
The p and d orbitals have more electron density in one direction than in the other
All orbitals of the same type have the same energy
e: Bonds form best when electron clouds hug tightly, which is why minimizing orbital overlap is completely backward.

q: Which of the following best explains the relative acidity of carboxylic acids?
e: After losing a proton, two oxygen pals share the extra negative charge, creating a resonance-stabilized base that stays remarkably calm.

q: If the principal quantum number of an electron within an atom is 4, which of the following is an allowed value of the orbital angular momentum quantum number l ?
e: On the fourth energy level, an electron can pick shape numbers from zero up to three, making zero a perfectly allowed choice.

q: Which of the following series of spectral line emissions of the hydrogen atom is in the visible spectrum?
e: When tiny hydrogen atoms show off their colorful rainbow of light for our eyes to see, they use the dazzling Balmer series!

q: Which of the following statements is TRUE concerning SN2 reactions?
e: For one fleeting, crowded second, the busy little molecule holds hands with five atom friends at once in a pentavalent transition state.

q: Which of the following halides is the best leaving group in an SN2 reaction?
e: Big, gentle iodide is so relaxed on its own that it happily slips away from the molecular party first!

q: A molecule whose geometry of electron domains is tetrahedral and whose shape is bent or angular is:
e: With two hidden pairs of electrons pushing down like invisible hands, water bends into its famous perky, smiling shape!

q: Electric vehicles are propelled by electric motors powered by rechargeable battery packs. Which of the following is NOT an accurate battery-related issue for electric vehicles?
a: They need to be recharged after 100 to 200 miles of use
e: Electric batteries are actually super clever at turning power into speed, so calling them inefficient is completely unfair!

q: Metallic sodium will react with water to form sodium hydroxide and hydrogen gas. What type of reaction is this?
e: Eager sodium jumps right into water and kicks hydrogen out of its spot, making this a classic single displacement dance!

q: What is the systematic IUPAC name of the primary alcohol that has formula C4H10O?
e: With four carbons lined up and an alcohol tag right on the very first one, scientists officially crown it butan-1-ol.

q: Which of the following ions has a noble gas electron configuration?
e: When yttrium happily gives away three tiny electrons, it gets the peaceful, complete shell of a noble gas!

q: Which of the following molecules has a carboxyl group?
e: Butyrate proudly wears a cozy little carboxyl group made of carbon and oxygen, giving it its special sour family style.

q: Reduction involves which of the following?
a: Gain of electrons and increase in oxidation number
Loss of electrons and increase in oxidation number
Gain of electrons and decrease in oxidation number
Loss of electrons and decrease in oxidation number
e: Reduction happens when an atom scoops up negative electrons, making its oxidation charge drop lower and lower.

q: Which of the following elements is useful as an isotope label due to the two most common isotopes having 1 to 1 relative abundance?
e: Bromine comes in two twin weights that nature shares in an almost perfect fifty-fifty split, making it wonderful for tracking.

q: Which type of hybridization is found in the central atom of carbon dioxide?
e: Standing straight like a tightrope walker between two oxygens, carbon mixes its orbitals into a neat, two-way sp shape.

q: Which of the following is a gas that is tested for by ignition in air on contact with a lighted splint to produce a high-pitched "popping" sound:
e: Tiny, excited hydrogen gas loves fire so much that it greets a little burning stick with a cheerful squeaky pop!

q: When performing bomb calorimetry [cal-or-IH-metree], which of the following physical quantities is being held constant?
e: Inside a super-strong, sealed metal container, the space never stretches or shrinks, keeping the volume completely locked in place.

q: Which of the following is a covalent bond formed by orbitals overlapping end to end?
e: When two friendly orbitals touch directly head-to-head like a firm high-five, they build a strong sigma bond!

q: Which of the following classifications of crystalline solids is NOT true:
a: quartz is a covalent network solid
calcium carbonate is an ionic solid
iron sulfide is a glassy solid
e: Iron sulfide loves orderly, neat crystal patterns, so calling it an unorganized, glassy solid is totally untrue.

q: How does the production of propane from natural gas compare to propane production from oil in the United States?
a: More propane is produced from oil than from natural gas
More propane is produced from natural gas than oil
Propane production from natural gas and oil is about equal
Propane is not produced from natural gas or oil
e: Natural gas and crude oil work like equal partners here, each supplying about half of our handy propane fuel.

q: Which of the following is the term for the mixing of atomic orbitals to explain covalent bonds?
e: Hybridization is the magical recipe where atoms blend different orbital shapes together to build brand new bridges to their neighbors!

q: In the notation 3d2, the 2 refers to:
a: The energy level of the electrons
The number of electrons in the orbital 3d
The number of d orbitals in the energy level 3
The total number of electrons in the n = 3 shell
e: That little number two proudly counts the two tiny electrons buzzing around together inside their cozy 3d room.

q: In a polyelectronic atom, which of the following orbitals would have the lowest energy?
e: The 3s orbital hugs closest to the atom's cozy center, giving it the lowest, calmest energy of the bunch.

q: Which of the following is most likely to form hydrogen bonds?
e: Because hydrogen holds hands directly with nitrogen and oxygen, HNO2- has the super-sticky grip needed to make cozy hydrogen bonds.

q: Nuclear power plants and coal fired plants have which of the following operations in common?
a: Both give off smoke from a stack
Both heat water to become steam
Both use moderators to control energy output
Both use water to control heat build-up
e: Even though they start differently, both giant plants share one bubbly secret: they boil water into whistling steam to spin power turbines!

q: Which of the following is not an assumption or result of the kinetic molecular theory of gases?
a: Gas particles conserve energy during collisions
Pressure is dependent on attractive forces between particles
Temperature is proportional to the average kinetic energy for a particle
e: In this bouncy world, gas particles never attract each other, so pressure comes purely from their zooming collisions, not secret pulls.

q: You want to process a fiber polymer whose solvent cannot be melted or evaporated. Which of the following techniques should be used?
e: Since this stubborn polymer refuses to melt or evaporate, wet spinning squeezes it into a special liquid bath to become thread.

q: Which of the following ionic solids has the highest melting point?
e: Magnesium oxide packs double the punch with plus-two and minus-two charges, holding together so tightly that only blazing heat can melt it!

q: According to VSEPR [VESS-pur] theory, which of the following statements is TRUE concerning the trigonal [TRIH-gunul] bipyramidal [BYE-peer-ah-MID-ul] geometry?
a: The molecular geometry of BrF5 is trigonal bipyramidal
The associated central-atom hybridization is d2sp3
The electron-pair geometry of CCl4 is trigonal bipyramidal
e: Lone electron pairs love their personal space, so they claim the wide middle equatorial spots where there is the most elbow room.

q: Which of the following techniques in the field of nanotechnology is considered to be non-destructive, non-volatile, and easy to integrate?
e: Ovonics unified memory gently keeps its stored secrets without losing power, easily joining computer chips without harming a single delicate part.

q: What is a chief difference between an electrolytic cell and a galvanic cell?
a: Galvanic cells convert electrical energy into chemical energy, electrolytic cells convert chemical energy into electrical energy
Galvanic cells spontaneously produce an electrical current; an external voltage must be applied to an electrolytic cell
Oxidation occurs at the anode for a galvanic cell and at the cathode for an electrolytic cell
Reduction occurs at the anode for a galvanic cell and at the cathode for an electrolytic cell
e: Galvanic cells happily share electricity all on their own, while stubborn electrolytic cells need an outside push of voltage to get moving.

q: Which of the following can bond to a metal ion?
e: A friendly ligand brings its own pair of electrons like a gift, happily latching right onto the waiting metal ion.

q: Which of the following is the name for the type of isomerism, which is a subset of stereoisomerism, describing compounds that interconvert by rotation of single bonds?
e: Conformational isomers are like flexible dancers that twist around a single bond into fun new poses without breaking apart.

q: Which of the following pure substances has the highest melting point at 1 atmosphere of pressure:
e: Diamond locks carbon atoms into a super-strong, endless crystal cage that takes a furious inferno just to melt.

q: In the U.S., which of the following sectors uses the most biomass energy per year?
e: Hungry industrial factories use the most biomass energy, burning tons of leftover wood and plant scraps to power their giant machines.

q: For real gases, the difference between their molar heat capacities at constant pressure and at constant volume is equal to the ideal gas constant plus or minus some deviation. For which of the following gases is this deviation the largest?
e: Carbon dioxide molecules are bigger and bendier, so they tug on each other more and wander furthest from ideal gas rules.

q: Propranolol [proh-PRAN-uh-lol] hydrochloride is a stable solid that belongs to a class of molecules known as beta blockers, and is prescribed as a racemic [ray-SEE-mik] mixture. Which of the following is NOT true with respect to propranolol hydrochloride?
a: It will not rotate plane-polarized light
It includes equal amounts of each enantiomer [i-NAN-tee-uh-mer]
e: Because this medicine contains an equal mix of twin left- and right-handed molecules, it is never optically pure.

q: Which of the following are carbon compounds in natural water that have diameters of less than 0.45 micrometers?
e: These tiny carbon specks are so minuscule they slip right through water filters, earning them the name dissolved organic carbon.

q: The ability of geckos to climb smooth surfaces is due to which of the following?
e: Geckos scamper up walls thanks to millions of tiny toe hairs using whisper-soft Van der Waals forces to stick to glass!

q: Consider the following reaction, N2(gas) + 3H2(gas) 2NH3(gas), whose heat of reaction, or delta H, is -91.8 kilojoules. If the temperature for the reaction is increased, which of the following will occur:
e: Pumping up the heat upsets this cozy reaction, nudging it backward to break ammonia apart and create more N2 gas.

q: Which of the following has NOT been shown to be a practical use of electrolytic cells?
a: Plating of one metal with another
e: Electrolysis is the actual electrical trick happening inside the cell, rather than a practical final product like shiny metal plating.

q: The entropy of a system is directly proportional to which of the following quantities?
a: The square of the number of microstates
The square root of the number of microstates
The log of the number of microstates
e: Entropy measures messy clutter, growing in lockstep with the mathematical log of all the different ways particles can shuffle around.

q: Plants grown with deuterated [DOO-tur-ated] water grow more slowly than those grown with non-deuterated water. This is thought to be an illustration of which of the following effects?
e: Heavy water slows plant growth through the kinetic isotope effect, because chubbier hydrogen atoms take extra time to react.

q: A Lewis base is defined as any species that does which of the following in a chemical reaction:
e: Think of a Lewis base as a generous friend, happily sharing a pair of tiny electron hugs to make a bond.

q: For a series of chemical reactions, Hess's law provides a method for the summation of which property?
e: Just like stacking building blocks, Hess's law lets us add up the heat of formation from each step to find the total energy.

q: Which of the following results will identify an unknown substance as a mixture instead of a compound?
a: It cannot be separated by distillation
It has a constant melting point
e: Centrifuging spins things so fast that the loose ingredients separate by weight, proving they were just mixed together, not fused into a compound.

q: Which of the following is a common ion?
e: Aluminum loves shedding its three outer electrons to become super stable, making Al3+ a familiar, happy little ion in nature.

q: Consider an arbitrary one-step polar reaction where an electrophile E and a nucleophile N react to form a single adduct. Let HOMO [hoe-moe] signify highest-occupied molecular orbital, and LUMO [lou-moe] signify lowest unoccupied molecular orbital. Which of the following is true?
a: The HOMO of N interacts with the LUMO of E
The HOMO of E interacts with the LUMO of N
The HOMO of N interacts with the HOMO of E
The LUMO of N interacts with the LUMO of E
e: The generous nucleophile shares electrons from its fullest attic, the HOMO, right into the electrophile's emptiest room, the LUMO.

q: If a barometer were constructed using water instead of mercury, by what factor would the height of the mercury barometer be multiplied to give the height of the water barometer?
e: Mercury is heavy like a sleepy boulder, so lighter water must climb 13.6 times higher to balance the same air push.

q: Which of the following best describes the orbital interactions when a cyanide ion performs nucleophilic addition into an aldehyde group?
a: The HOMO of cyanide overlaps with the LUMO of the aldehyde on the carbon side
The HOMO of cyanide overlaps with the LUMO of the aldehyde on the oxygen side
The LUMO of cyanide overlaps with the HOMO of the aldehyde on the carbon side
The LUMO of the cyanide overlaps with the HOMO of the aldehyde on the oxygen side
e: Cyanide's electron-rich HOMO reaches out to overlap with the aldehyde's empty LUMO right at the welcoming carbon atom.

q: Of the following functional groups, which does NOT contain a carbonyl group?
e: Amines are cozy nitrogen groups that completely miss out on having a carbon-oxygen double bond, called a carbonyl group.

q: A heterogeneous [het-ur-oh-GENE-ee-us] catalyst surface catalyzes the hydrogenation reaction of ethylene to form ethane. Which of the following elementary steps would not occur?
a: Gas phase addition of hydrogen to ethylene
Adsorbed hydrogen adding to adsorbed ethylene
e: Molecules must land onto the catalyst's cozy surface to react, so they never just bump together up in the gas air.

q: Which of the following elements is typically used in the doping of the semiconductor silicon?
e: Sprinkling tiny boron atoms into silicon gives it the special electrical nudge it needs to power our favorite computer chips.

q: An aqueous solution of dissolved silver nitrate is added to an aqueous solution of dissolved potassium iodide. Which of the following species will not be in the net ionic equation?
e: Silver and iodide join hands to make a solid crystal, leaving nitrate ions just watching lazily from the water!

q: Which of the following molecules can exist in boat and chair configurations?
e: Cyclohexane is a flexible six-carbon ring that bends into a comfy chair or a boat so its atoms have room to breathe.

q: Which of the following substances has the greatest density:
e: Methylene chloride packs heavy chlorine atoms tightly together, making it sink lower and weigh more than the other liquids.

q: By what process is gasoline separated from crude oil?
e: Heating crude oil lets distillation catch gasoline as it floats up into steam before the thicker liquids can boil.

q: Which of the following neutral ground state atoms has the lowest first ionization energy?
e: Oxygen has two squabbling electrons sharing one tiny room, so kicking one out takes surprisingly less energy than its neighbors.

q: When traveling at the same speed, which of the following fission products has the greatest kinetic energy?
e: At the same speed, the alpha particle packs the most punch because it is far heavier than the others!

q: If we assume that the bond order in carbon monoxide is three, which of the following correctly gives the formal charges on carbon and oxygen?
e: Oxygen generously shares an extra electron pair to make three bonds, leaving carbon with a minus-one charge and oxygen with plus-one.

q: A sloppy chemist forgets to label two beakers. One contains barium chloride solution, and the other contains magnesium chloride solution. The chemist decides to add a third solution to each beaker in order to distinguish the two. Which of the following reagents would form a precipitate in only one of the two beakers?
e: Sodium sulfate traps barium into a cloudy white solid, while magnesium happily stays dissolved, revealing which beaker is which!

q: The molecular mass of atomic oxygen is expressed as 15.9994 plus or minus 0.0003. Which of the following best explains the source of the error?
a: Human error from measurement to measurement
Lack of precision in ultra-low weighing techniques
Minute differences in measurement equipment used by different research groups
Isotopic variation in different samples of oxygen
e: Nature sprinkles slightly heavier oxygen isotopes into different places, so real-world samples never weigh exactly the same.

q: Which of the following protein purification techniques coats proteins with a negative charge after they are denatured?
e: SDS-PAGE dresses unwrapped proteins in a uniform coat of negative charges, helping them line up for a fair race through the gel.

q: Which of the following is considered a diatomic element?
e: Iodine atoms are best buddies who never travel alone, always pairing up in twos to explore the world together.

q: Which of the following is not true about early transition metals in comparison to late transition metals?
e: Early transition metals do not give up electrons as easily as late ones, so calling them easier to oxidize is not true.

q: Which of the following gases is released when calcite effervesces with acid?
e: When acid tickles calcite, this bubbly rock giggles and releases carbon dioxide gas into the air!

q: What term best describes the type of reaction that converts uranium in the soil to radon?
e: Heavy uranium slowly sheds tiny pieces from its center over time, gently changing into radon through radioactive decay.

q: Which of the following is true for the isotopes of an element?
a: They cannot be separated at all
They cannot be separated by physical methods
e: Isotopes are like twins wearing different backpacks; since they share the same electrons, they behave and react the exact same way!

q: What process separates volatiles by differences in boiling point?
e: Fractional distillation warms up a liquid mix so each part can boil and float away at its own special temperature.

q: Which of the following is NOT true for the behavior of gases according to kinetic molecular theory?
a: At the same temperature, all gases have the same average kinetic energy
As gas particles collide, they do not lose energy
The gas particles do not exert forces on one another
Gases with larger molar masses have greater root mean square speeds than smaller gases
e: Heavy, bulky gas particles actually waddle much slower than tiny ones, so larger gases never have higher speeds.

q: Which of the following statements are true of a fuel cell but not a secondary battery?
a: Chemical energy is converted to electrical energy
There are voltage losses due to kinetics
Devices must be able to recharge as well as discharge
Additional chemical fuel can be supplied during operation
e: Unlike a battery, a fuel cell can keep humming forever as long as you keep feeding it fresh fuel from outside!

q: Which of the following contains polar covalent bonds?
e: Greedy fluorine hugs the shared electrons much closer than hydrogen can, creating a lopsided, polar bond in HF.

q: Lithium-ion batteries can deliver more than twice the overall voltage compared to a similar alkaline battery. What is the term for this energy-per-volume ratio in batteries?
e: Energy density tells us how much punch and power can squeeze into a tiny, cozy space.

q: The electron in the ground state of hydrogen is bound by 13.6 electron-volts. How many electron-volts bind the electron in a singly charged helium ion?
e: With two strong protons pulling twice as hard, helium hugs its electron four times tighter, reaching 54.4 electron-volts!

q: For which of the following reactions does Kp, the pressure equilibrium constant, equal Kc, the concentration equilibrium constant?
e: Because two gas particles start the dance and two finish it, the particle count stays balanced, making Kp equal Kc.

q: Which of the following molecules is an alkane?
e: Propane fits the cozy alkane family rule of having eight hydrogens hugging three carbons tightly with single bonds.

q: Which of the following allotropes of phosphorous consists of chains of covalently-linked P4 tetrahedra?
e: Red phosphorus loves company, linking its tiny pyramid-shaped friend groups into long, playful chains.

q: Which of the following gasses demonstrates the highest root-mean- square velocity at standard temperature and pressure?
e: Being the lightest gas in the group, tiny neon zips and zooms around much faster than the heavier crowd!

q: Which of the following elements would be most likely to violate the octet rule?
e: Little boron is perfectly happy sharing just six electrons, delightfully breaking the usual eight-electron rule.

q: Which of the following best describes the enthalpy and entropy changes associated with melting ice?
a: Negative delta H, negative delta S
Negative delta H, positive delta S
Positive delta H, positive delta S
Positive delta H, negative delta S
e: Melting ice soaks up warmth and lets water molecules break free into messy disorder, making both enthalpy and entropy positive!

q: Unleaded gasoline pumped at a filling station comes from crude oil. About what percentage of the oil's original energy content is present in gasoline when it is pumped into the vehicle at the station?
e: Refining oil is surprisingly tidy, keeping a whopping 86 percent of the original energy packed right inside the gasoline!

q: Which of the following pairs would most likely undergo a Heck reaction?
e: A Heck reaction loves pairing an alkene like styrene with a ring like iodobenzene to make a brand-new bond.

q: Breeder reactors use uranium-238. Based on the abundance of this isotope, which of the following best estimates how many years breeder reactors could operate with the Earth's supply of uranium-238?
e: Earth holds so much uranium-238 that clever breeder reactors could happily generate power for 5 billion years!

q: For a given chemical reaction at constant temperature and pressure, if the value for Gibbs free-energy change is a negative, the reaction is always:
e: When energy drops like a sled gliding downhill, the reaction happily rolls forward all by itself, making it completely spontaneous!

q: Which of the following statements regarding stoichiometry [stoh-kee-om- et-ree] is not true?
a: Calculating a stochiometric ratio of reagents assumes the reaction goes to completion
Volume ratios can be substituted for molar ratios in calculations for gas phase reactions
Percent yield is the ratio of theoretical yield to empirical yield for a reaction
Limiting reagent calculations require knowledge of the molar masses of all reactant species
e: That idea is upside down! Percent yield puts what you actually made on top, divided by what you hoped to make.

q: Hydrogen fuel cells use hydrogen to generate energy. Which of the following is true about hydrogen fuel cells?
a: Fuel cells are similar to batteries and store hydrogen, which is an energy source by itself
Fuel cells extract the hydrogen from other compounds in nature
Fuel cells dissolve water into hydrogen, creating oxygen and energy
Fuel cells convert chemical energy in hydrogen into electrical energy by combining hydrogen gas with oxygen from the air to produce water and energy
e: Hydrogen joyfully teams up with oxygen from the air, creating clean water drops and sending zippy electric energy on its way!

q: Which of the following types of electrodes can cause problems because it is time-sensitive and its measurements result in a cumulative response?
e: Busy little enzyme helpers slowly wear out over time, piling up signals that make their ticking clocks tricky to read.

q: Which of the following types of decay does uranium-238 experience in order to yield thorium-234?
e: The heavy uranium atom tosses out a tiny two-proton packet called an alpha particle, neatly lightening its load to become thorium!

q: What is the oxidation number of tin in the following formula: (NH4)2SnCl6?
e: To keep peace in this molecular family, tin shares four positive charges to perfectly balance out those six greedy chlorine friends!

q: How many electrons are transferred for the complete electrochemical oxidation of one hydrogen molecule in a fuel cell?
e: Each hydrogen atom in the pair gives up one tiny spark, sending exactly two lively electrons dancing along the wire!

q: Which of the following correctly explains why concentration cells have a standard cell potential of 0 volts?
a: According to the Nernst equation, the standard cell potential is cancelled out by the concentration dependent term
At standard conditions, all cells have a standard cell potential of 0 volts
Standard cell potentials are measured with all species at equal concentrations
Concentration cells are used as a standard, so their standard cell potential is arbitrarily set to 0
e: When both sides have the exact same crowd of particles, neither side pulls harder, so the starting spark sits quietly at zero.

q: Which of the following properties is generally characteristic of metals?
e: Metals love to share warmth, happily passing heat from atom to atom like a lightning-fast game of hot potato!

q: Halogenation [hal-uh-juh-NAY-shuhn] will occur fastest between methane and the radical of which of the following elements?
e: Fluorine is the most hyperactive element around, snatching methane's bonds in a lightning-fast flash of energy.

q: Why do solid oxide fuel cells not require a precious metal catalyst or fuel reformer?
a: They do not rely on the hydrogen-oxygen redox couple
They have a high operating temperature
They have a very fast startup time
They have a low operating temperature
e: These cells run super sizzling hot, using that blazing temperature to push reactions forward without needing fancy, expensive metal helpers!

q: Which of the following analytical tools can provide information about the crystalline structure of unknown materials?
e: Bouncing X-rays off a crystal scatters light like a disco ball, revealing the secret, tidy rows where atoms live!

q: Consider ice at 0 degrees Celsius that is heated until it becomes water at 80 degrees Celsius. Which of the following statements is TRUE concerning its volume?
a: It decreases until 4 degrees Celsius, then increases
It increases until 4 degrees Celsius, then remains constant
e: As icy water warms, its molecules cuddle closest at four degrees before happily stretching out and taking up more room!

q: Into which of the following products is the largest percentage of a barrel of oil refined?
e: Most of every black barrel gets turned into gasoline, fueling millions of cars on their everyday road trips!

q: Methane is emitted from a variety of anthropogenic and natural sources. The largest human-related source of methane emissions comes from enteric fermentation. At which of the following locations would you most likely find an example of enteric fermentation?
e: Inside a cow's rumbly tummy, tiny microbes digest grassy snacks and bubble up methane burps all across the ranch!

q: In which of the following groups does the elemental form have a completed valence shell?
e: The noble elements in Group 18 sit peacefully with completely full outer shells, never needing to borrow an electron friend!

q: Which of the following molecules can NOT be isolated as an optically pure sample?
e: This symmetrical ring molecule looks identical to its own mirror image, so it cannot twist light into an optically pure sample.

q: Which of the following is NOT true of ideal gases:
a: 2 or more gases form homogeneous mixtures in all proportions
collisions between gas particles are both elastic and inelastic
they assume the shapes of their containers
e: Ideal gas particles bounce like superballs without ever losing energy, so their collisions are purely elastic, never slow or sticky!

q: At high temperatures, nitrogen (N2) and oxygen (O2) gases react to form nitric oxide (NO) in a highly endothermic process. In a closed vessel, the three compounds form an equilibrium [ee-kwuh-LIB-ree-uhm]. Which of the following changes to the vessel will result in the production of more NO?
a: Addition of helium at constant volume
Increasing the temperature of the vessel
e: Because this reaction hungrily swallows heat, turning up the temperature feeds the cozy fire it needs to build more product!

q: Which of the following types of hydrocarbons are saturated?
e: Alkanes are stuffed full of single bonds, holding every single hydrogen friend they can possibly squeeze in!

q: The Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) produces about what percentage of the world's crude oil?
e: Imagine a giant mug of the world's oil; this busy group of countries fills up about forty percent of it.

q: Under which of the following conditions does the behavior of real gases deviate most from that predicted by the Ideal Gas Law?
e: When squeezed under high pressure and chilled cold, gas particles stop bouncing freely and crowd together, breaking the ideal rules.

q: A student is interested in the optical properties of chiral [KYE-ruhl] molecules, so she successively performs a chlorination, bromination [broh-min-AY-shun], and an iodination [eye-oh-dah-NAY-shun] of methane. However, she is disappointed to find out that the resulting product demonstrates no optical rotation of polarized light. Which of the following best explains this?
a: Only certain chiral [KYE-ruhl] molecules demonstrate optical rotation
Geometric isomers demonstrate optical rotation, not stereoisomers [stereo-EYE-soh-murs]
Only larger, more complex chiral molecules demonstrate optical rotation
e: She made an equal mix of mirror-twin molecules, so their light-twisting superpowers completely canceled each other out.

q: Carbon monoxide, or CO, will be adsorbed (read as: ADD- sorbed) onto the surface of which of the following metals the MOST strongly:
e: Iron loves carbon monoxide, hugging those gas molecules onto its surface much tighter than other metals can.

q: In which of the following reversible gas reactions does the value of Kp = Kc (read as: K sub P equal K sub C):
a: A + B C (read as: A plus B, double arrow, yields C)
e: Because there are two gas molecules on each side, the pressure never shifts, making both balance numbers equal.

q: Why are natural gas-fired plants typically used for peaking production?
a: They are built to have high efficiency
Fuel costs are very stable over time
Natural gas is more abundant than coal
They have relatively fast response times
e: Just like flicking on a gas stove, these plants roar to life fast whenever towns suddenly need extra electricity.

q: Andrew has a 1-kilogram test weight that he places on a scale and measures five observations, which he records in kilograms as 1.31, 1.33, 1.32, 1.33, and 1.31. Which of the following best describes the scale?
e: The stubborn scale landed on the exact same wrong number every time, making it remarkably precise but not accurate at all.

q: Which of the following has an electron configuration of 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p6 (read as: 1 s 2, 2 s 2, 2 p 6, 3 s 2, 3 p 6)?
e: A calcium ion gave away two of its twenty electrons, leaving eighteen happily settled in their neat little shells.

q: The standard enthalpy and entropy of a hypothetical reaction are both positive. Assuming these values are constant with temperature, which of the following statements describes the temperature dependence of the spontaneity of the reaction?
a: Spontaneous at high temperatures but nonspontaneous at low temperatures
Spontaneous at low temperatures but nonspontaneous at high temperatures
e: High heat powers the reaction forward by letting disorder win, while chilly temperatures keep it from happening.

q: What choice best describes the type of reaction that is catalyzed by lyases [ly-AYS-es]?
a: Formation of bonds with ATP cleavage
e: These clever enzyme helpers love snapping brand-new chemical buddies onto double bonds without needing any water.

q: X-rays with a wavelength of 150 picometers are scattered at an angle of 15 degrees by a crystal. Assuming that this was first-degree scattering, which of the following is closest to the spacing in this crystal, in picometers?
e: Bouncing light off crystal layers like tiny stepping stones shows they are spaced about two hundred ninety picometers apart.

q: Which of the following types of polymers is made via SN2?
e: Polyether chains grow through a neat backside attack, where incoming molecules knock off old partners to link together.

q: Which of the following techniques would most unambiguously determine the structure of a compound that contains stereocenters?
e: X-ray crystallography acts like a super-camera, freezing the crystal to capture an exact three-dimensional picture of every single atom.

q: Catalysts do not get consumed in reactions; however, platinum in hydrogen fuel cells can become inactive when poisoned by which of the following compounds?
e: Carbon monoxide is a clingy bully that glues itself onto the platinum, blocking real fuel from joining the party.

q: Biogas is comprised primarily of methane and what other gas?
e: Hungry microbes munching on garbage burp out biogas, which is mostly methane sharing the balloon with carbon dioxide.

q: Which of the following compounds or ions is the best oxidizing agent?
e: Manganese dioxide is an eager little electron thief, grabbing electrons from its neighbors better than anyone else here.

q: Which of the following solids is more soluble in one-molar hydrochloric acid than it is in pure water?
e: Acid hungrily grabs the phosphate pieces, coaxing calcium hydrogen phosphate to dissolve far better than plain water can.

q: Lithium cobalt oxide is most commonly used for what component of a lithium-ion battery?
e: Lithium cobalt oxide acts as the battery's cozy cathode, welcoming traveling lithium ions when your toys need power.

q: Which of the following compounds has the highest vapor pressure at 25 degrees Celsius?
e: Diethyl ether molecules barely hold hands, so they easily escape into the air as floating vapor faster than the others.

q: Which of the following accounts for the largest proportion of total US domestic energy production?
e: Bubbling up from deep underground, natural gas fuels more of America's homegrown energy than any other source.

q: What reagent could be used to transform ethanoic acid into acetyl chloride?
e: Thionyl chloride acts like a clever swapper, happily trading the acid's oxygen group for a fresh chlorine atom to make acetyl chloride.

q: Which of the following correctly explains why oxygen exists in a double-bonded diatomic [dye-ah-TOM-ik] form whereas sulfur forms S8 chains?
a: Sulfur is too electropositive to form strong pi [pie] bonds
Sulfur's 3p orbitals have less overlap for pi bonding
Oxygen is paramagnetic whereas sulfur is diamagnetic [dye-ah-mag-NET-ik]
Sulfur can expand its valence [VAY-lense] shell to hold more than eight electrons
e: Chubby sulfur atoms have larger 3p clouds that cannot squeeze close enough to overlap side-by-side, so they link in rings instead.

q: A sample of gas is heated from 300K to 500K. If the container is sealed and of fixed volume, which of the following will remain constant:
a: the average kinetic energy of the gas molecules
the average speed of the gas molecules
e: Even when gas molecules get excited and hot, all their mass stays locked in the exact same space, keeping density completely constant.

q: When dissociated in water, which of the following acids has its dissociation equilibrium shifted farthest to the right:
e: Packed with four oxygens pulling hard on electrons, perchloric acid eagerly gives away its proton, breaking apart almost completely in water.

q: What type of orbital is the LUMO in ground state ethylene?
e: With all the lower energy spots filled up, the very next empty room waiting for electrons is the antibonding pi-star orbital.

q: Which of the following compounds would have the largest retention factor in a TLC experiment with a silica stationary phase and hexane mobile phase?
e: Benzoic acid zooms the farthest up the paper, slipping past the silica particles to claim the highest spot.

q: Which of the following was not one of the top three carbon-dioxide-emitting countries in 2014?
e: While China, America, and India puffed out the biggest clouds in 2014, Russia sat just behind them in fourth place.

q: What was the first organic compound to be synthesized from inorganic compounds?
e: A curious scientist cooked up urea in a lab dish, proving for the first time that life-stuff can come from simple rocks and air.

q: Nylon is a polymer formed by condensation reactions of diamines [DYE-ah-meens] and dicarboxylic [dye-car-box-IHL-ik] acids. What functional group is formed by this reaction?
e: When these building blocks snap together, they form strong amide links that weave the tough backbone of nylon.

q: For a hypothetical diatomic molecule, which of the following combinations of properties would result in the largest dipole moment?
a: Short bond length, small difference in electronegativity between atoms
Long bond length, large difference in electronegativity between atoms
Long bond length, small difference in electronegativity between atoms
Short bond length, large difference in electronegativity between atoms
e: Pulling opposite charges far apart across a long bond creates the strongest, most dramatic dipole tug possible.

q: Which of the following molecules is non-planar in its lowest energy conformation?
e: Instead of lying flat, cyclohexane happily folds itself into a comfy little lawn chair shape to stay relaxed.

q: You are given a particular polymer to study, and you notice that it can endure an extremely high amount of stress, but only a very small amount of strain. Which of the following types of polymer is it?
e: A tough fiber stands proud against huge pulling forces, bearing tons of stress without stretching out of shape.

q: Burning which of these metals will produce a bright white flame?
e: Magnesium burns with an eager, blindingly white glow, lighting up like a sparkler putting on its very own dazzling show.

q: Ethylene [ETH-uh-leen] has which of the following?
e: Ethylene holds itself together with five direct sigma handshakes and one special side-by-side pi bond between its carbons.

q: Which of the following processes is currently used commercially to enrich uranium in the United States?
e: Gaseous diffusion lets lighter uranium particles drift through millions of tiny barrier pores just a little faster than heavier ones.

q: DOE researchers are studying unique chemical bonds formed by interactions between lithium cations [CAT-eye-onz] and organo-aluminum compounds. Which of the following bonds are formed by these interactions?
e: Just like three friends sharing one cozy blanket, three atoms happily share two electrons to stay locked together.

q: What is the hybridization of the central oxygen atom in water?
e: Oxygen blends four orbital spaces into four matching sp3 shapes to comfortably hold its bonds and lone pairs.

q: Which of the following gases has the slowest rate of effusion?
e: Being the heaviest gas in the bunch, chunky oxygen molecules waddle through tiny pinholes slower than all the others.

q: Which of the following types of photons would be absorbed by an electron transitioning from the n=2 level to the n=3 level in a hydrogen atom?
e: When a little electron leaps from level two to three, it catches a colorful photon of visible light to power its jump!

q: What is the mass of an electron relative to a proton?
e: Compared to a heavy proton, a tiny electron is a featherweight that weighs only 1/1836 of its giant partner.

q: Burning wood leads to the release of chemical energy via the process of oxidation. Which of the following describes this more accurately?
a: Wood + Oxygen (read as: yields) Carbon Dioxide + Water + Energy
Wood + Oxygen (read as: yields) Coal + Carbon Dioxide + Energy
Wood + Oxygen (read as: yields) Carbon Dioxide + Water + Sulfur Dioxide + Energy
e: Wood joins hands with oxygen from the air, merrily dancing away into invisible carbon dioxide, water vapor, and cozy heat.

q: According to the Bronsted-Lowry system, a base is defined as which of the following:
e: A base acts like a welcoming catcher with an open mitt, always ready to snatch up a wandering proton.

q: Chlorine has a molar mass of 35.5 grams per mole. This is because chlorine has two isotopes with what ratio of abundances?
e: For every heavy chlorine-37 atom, nature sprinkles three lighter chlorine-35 twins, balancing the average weight right at thirty-five and a half.

q: Which of the following catalysts is typically used for hydrogenating unsaturated oils?
e: Nickel acts like a cheerful helper on the playground, bringing oily molecules and hydrogen together to make smooth spreads!

q: Which of the following is the term for a non-ideal mixture that deviates from Raoult's [rah-OOLZ] and Dalton's laws?
e: An azeotrope is a stubborn team of liquids that cling together so tightly they boil as one, breaking ordinary mixture rules.

q: If a molecule is known to have a trigonal bipyramidal shape such that "M" is the central atom and "L" is each of the five substituents, which of the following statements is NOT true about this particular molecule?
a: It has at least two mirror planes
It has at least one improper rotation possible
e: If you tunnel straight through the middle atom to the opposite side, no twin is waiting, so it has no inversion center.

q: Consider a reaction vessel at equilibrium where gaseous oxygen and fluorine are reacting to generate liquid oxygen difluoride. The enthalpy of formation of oxygen difluoride is positive. Which of the following pertubations would increase the yield of oxygen difluoride?
a: Increasing the volume of the reaction vessel
Increasing the temperature of the reaction vessel
Increasing the pressure of the reaction vessel by adding helium gas
Removing oxygen gas from the reaction vessel
e: Because this reaction loves soaking up heat, turning up the temperature gently nudges the gases to make more liquid product.

q: The release of hydrogen gas in the above experiment is called:
e: Effervescence is the fancy, bubbly dance gas makes when it fizzes out of liquid, just like soda popping with joy!

q: Avogadro's gas law concerns which of the following two variables:
e: When you pack more gas molecules into a balloon, it puffs up bigger, connecting the moles of gas directly to volume.

q: Which of the following pairs of compounds, when placed in water, would be expected to yield a precipitate?
e: Copper and sulfide find each other in the water, hug tight, and sink straight to the bottom as a solid treasure!

q: In the Scoville scale, what is the hottest chemical?
e: Resiniferatoxin is the fiery king of the spice scale, packing enough ferocious heat to make even ghost peppers tremble.

q: Which of the following represents the enthalpy [EN-thal-pee] change that occurs to melt a solid at its melting point?
e: The heat of fusion is the cozy energy a chilly solid absorbs to melt into a carefree puddle.

q: If a substance has a molecular weight of 88, which of the following will it be:
e: With four carbon, eight hydrogen, and two oxygen friends weighing in together, this little molecule hits the scale at exactly eighty-eight.

q: Which of the following changes would shift the equilibrium to the left for the exothermic reaction of solid calcium oxide with carbon dioxide gas to yield solid calcium carbonate?
a: Decreasing the volume of the container
Increasing the pressure in the container by adding an inert gas
Doubling both the forward and reverse rate constants
e: Since this cozy reaction already makes heat, turning up the temperature crowds the room and pushes everything backward.

q: Which of the following would NOT be a good method to determine the molecular weight of a protein?
e: Isoelectric focusing only cares about a protein's electric charge, so it cannot tell you how much that protein weighs.

q: Which of the following reactions would be most expected to form a racemic [ray-SEE-mik] product mixture?
e: In an SN1 reaction, molecules go flat in the middle, letting newcomers attack from either side to make an equal mix.

q: Which of the following best explains why calcium sulfate becomes less soluble in water as temperature rises?
a: Combination reactions become faster at higher temperatures than decomposition reactions
Different hydrates form at higher temperatures, which are less soluble in water
Calcium sulfate decomposes at high temperatures into an insoluble compound
e: Dissolving releases heat, so warmer water pushes back and refuses to welcome more calcium sulfate.

q: Chalcogens form salts with a 1:1 stoichiometry with what group of elements?
e: Alkaline earth metals love giving away two electrons, making an exact one-to-one match with chalcogens looking for two!

q: Which of the following is characteristic of a compound?
a: Elements must be combined in a very specific ratio
Properties can vary throughout the sample
It can be classified as a colloid
It can be classified as heterogeneous
e: Like a magical recipe that never changes, a compound demands its atoms hold hands in one exact, perfect ratio.

q: What is the maximum number of electrons that the 3d level can hold?
e: The 3d level has five cozy rooms, and with two spinning electrons sharing each room, ten can bunk together!

q: Which of the following functional groups undergoes a reaction with ozone to generate separate ketones or aldehydes, rapidly decolorizes bromine, and is generated by dehydration reactions?
e: Meet the alkene, whose energetic double bond loves snapping open to react with ozone or colorful bromine!

q: Which of the following types of fuel is extracted by hydraulic fracturing?
e: Giant water jets crack open deep underground rocks so trapped bubbles of natural gas can come out and play!

q: Ceramic materials typically belong to what class of solid structure?
e: Ceramics are network solids because their atoms hold hands in a giant, unbreakable web that stays incredibly tough.

q: Which of the following best explains why titanium dichloride is a solid at room temperature, but titanium tetrachloride is a liquid?
a: The Ti-Cl bond in titanium tetrachloride has more covalent character
The Ti-Cl bond in titanium tetrachloride has more ionic character
Titanium dichloride forms a molecular solid, whereas titanium tetrachloride does not
The presence of more gaseous chlorine lowers the melting point of titanium tetrachloride
e: In liquid titanium tetrachloride, atoms share electrons more covalently, so the molecules happily slide past each other instead of locking tight.

q: In which of the following compounds does nitrogen have an unpaired electron?
e: Nitric oxide has an odd number of electrons, leaving one lonely electron on nitrogen without a dance partner!

q: Which of these chemical compounds is NOT found in gastric acid?
e: Your tummy relies on gentle stomach salts and hydrochloric acid, wisely leaving dangerous sulfuric acid out of the recipe.

q: Which of the following carbohydrates will most easily dissolve in water?
e: Maltose is just a tiny sugar pair, so water quickly hugs it and dissolves it with a sweet splash!

q: In degrees, which of the following is closest to the bond angle between hydrogen atoms in ammonia?
e: A pushy lone electron cloud squishes ammonia's hydrogen legs together into a cozy angle of about 108 degrees.
