q: If you wanted to synthesize iso-butyl-benzene through a Friedel-Crafts [free-dell-crafts] alkylation [AL-kil-lay-shun] reaction, what molecule would you react with benzene and aluminum chloride?
e: Iso-butyl-chloride brings the perfect four-carbon branch, letting aluminum chloride pluck away chlorine to connect with benzene.

q: In which of the following ways would oxygen's electrons fill the 3 p subshells?
e: Oxygen has four outer p-electrons, so two bunch up as a pair while the other two get their own cozy rooms.

q: Converting carbon dioxide to carbon monoxide through reduction would be effective method for reducing harmful levels of atmospheric carbon dioxide. However, this conversion is very difficult for which of the following reasons?
a: There is a limited supply of rhenium in the world
Not all steps of the reduction have been completely determined
The final step takes an extremely long time
The carbon dioxide is too difficult to harness
e: Turning carbon dioxide into carbon monoxide needs a rare helper metal called rhenium, but our planet only has a tiny pinch of it!

q: Which of the following best describes the bonding of the highest occupied molecular orbital set of a neutral dioxygen molecule?
e: Oxygen’s topmost electrons live in pi-antibonding orbitals, pushing slightly apart like two playful magnets that refuse to touch.

q: Which of the following elements is most electronegative according to the Pauling scale?
e: Carbon hugs shared electrons much tighter than iron, arsenic, or tellurium can, making it the grabbiest of the bunch!

q: The strength of the dispersion forces between two non-polar molecules increases with:
a: The number of hydrogen atoms in the molecule
The number of electrons in the molecule
The magnitude of the largest electronegativity of the atoms involved
The magnitude of the difference in electronegativity between the atoms
e: The more electrons a molecule has, the squishier its cloud gets, creating stronger little tugs that pull neighbors together.

q: Which of the following acids is triprotic [try-PRO-tic]?
e: Triprotic means having three proton gifts to give, and arsenic acid happily shares three hydrogens with water!

q: Which of the following best explains why NaCl has a higher melting point than HCl?
a: HCl can form hydrogen bonds, while NaCl cannot
HCl has stronger London dispersion forces
HCl is a molecular compound, while NaCl is an ionic compound
HCl is a network compound, while NaCl is a molecular compound
e: Salt is an ionic compound held by powerful electric grips, whereas molecular hydrogen chloride lets go and melts far more easily.

q: Which of the following is NOT true of conjugated dienes [DY- eens]?
a: Increasing conjugation is proportional to increased UV wavelength absorption
Heats of formation are lower than unconjugated dienes
s-trans dienes participate in Diels-Alder cyclization
e: To perform the Diels-Alder ring dance, molecules must curl into an s-cis shape, so stretched-out s-trans dienes cannot participate.

q: A physical chemist has determined the vapor pressure of a liquid at multiple temperatures and wants to determine the standard entropy of vaporization. Which of the following sets of axes will enable the chemist to graph the data as a line and determine the entropy from the y-intercept?
a: Pressure on y, temperature on x
One over pressure on y, temperature on x
Natural log of pressure on y, temperature on x
Natural log of pressure on y, one over temperature on x
e: Graphing the natural log of pressure against one over temperature creates a straight path where entropy waits at the y-intercept!

q: Which of the following would be the MOST soluble in water at room temperature:
e: While other sulfates stubbornly sink, aluminum sulfate loves water and dissolves in a lively, splashing crowd of ions!

q: Each of the following pairs of chemicals are dissolved in aqueous [AK-wee-uhs] solution at concentrations of 1 molar. Which pair would form a buffer solution?
e: Formic acid and sodium formate team up as a weak acid and its trusty partner, balancing acidity like gentle see-saw buddies.

q: Which of the following fuels is used in peaker power plants?
e: When everyone flips their lights on at once, natural gas swoops in like a speedy stovetop flame, firing up in mere seconds!

q: Which of the following substances can behave as either a Lewis acid or a Lewis base?
e: Friendly ammonia can share its spare electron pair like a snack, but it can also make room to accept one.

q: In which of the following ranges of the electromagnetic spectrum are the Paschen series hydrogen lines found?
e: When excited hydrogen electrons hop down to floor three, they beam out invisible, warm infrared light like a cozy secret message.

q: Which of the following was NOT an effect of removing sulfur from diesel fuel?
a: It lowered the nitrous oxides and soot emissions
It slightly increased gas mileage in diesel engines
It allowed the use of advanced emissions control systems
It reduced the lubricity of the fuel
e: Removing sulfur gave diesel cleaner air, but it never boosted mileage—engines actually lost a tiny sip of energy.

q: Addition of which of the following compounds will increase the solubility of calcium carbonate in water?
e: Hungry phosphoric acid gobbles up carbonate ions, coaxing stubborn calcium carbonate chalk to melt happily into the water.

q: What is the process that best describes the transfer of electrons from one atom to another through electrostatic attraction?
e: In ionic bonding, one generous atom gifts an electron to another, and their opposite charges snap together like best friends hugging!

q: What is the formula for iron II phosphate?
e: To balance their electrical charges, three plus-two iron friends team up with two minus-three phosphate buddies to build Fe3(PO4)2.

q: Which of the following is an example of an A+1 isotope?
e: Nitrogen has a slightly heavier twin with an extra neutron, making it a classic A-plus-one isotope.

q: Which of the following is an assumption of the ideal gas law?
a: The volume of individual molecules is negligible compared to the volume of the container
All molecules travel at the same velocity
Molecules only interact through dipole [DYE-pole]-dipole forces
Molecules do not collide with each other
e: Scientists imagine ideal gas particles as tiny specks so minuscule that their own bodies take up practically zero room.

q: For which of the following gas-phase reactions are the equilibrium constants Kc and Kp equivalent to one another?
a: Ozone is produced from diatomic oxygen
Carbon dioxide and hydrogen are produced from carbon monoxide and steam
Ammonia is produced from hydrogen and nitrogen
Gaseous methanol is produced from carbon monoxide and hydrogen
e: Because two gas molecules start the dance and two finish it, the molecular crowd stays equal, balancing both constants.

q: Which of the following is the strongest spectral line in the visible region of the hydrogen spectrum:
e: Hydrogen's red Balmer line shines the brightest because jumping electrons love making that cheerful hop most of all!

q: Which of the following describes the phenomenon of light emission by fireflies?
e: Fireflies mix special body chemicals to brew up glowing chemiluminescence, lighting the dark without making any heat at all!

q: Which of the following is NOT an example of a weak base:
e: Ammonium clutches an extra proton tight and gives it away, which makes it a weak acid instead of a base.

q: Scientists at Argonne National Lab are using lanthanum-containing perovskites to catalyze the oxygen evolution reaction. They found that by doping the lanthanum with another metal, they introduced holes in the valence band and thereby increased the catalytic activity. Which of the following metals did they use for this purpose?
e: Scientists invited strontium into the crystal to borrow some electrons, creating handy empty pockets that speed up the reaction.

q: Which of the following is the best estimate of the percent of electricity produced in the United States using petroleum in 2014?
e: Because petroleum is saved for roaring car engines, it powered just a tiny one percent slice of our electric grid.

q: The rare earth elements are primarily composed of elements from which groups of the periodic table?
e: These rare earth cousins hide along the bottom rows of the elemental neighborhood, mostly belonging to the lanthanide and actinide families.

q: Which of the following is true for an adiabatic process?
a: Net heat transfer to the surroundings is zero
Work done on the surroundings is zero
e: In an adiabatic adventure, a gas wraps up so snugly that absolutely no heat can slip in or sneak away.

q: Which of the following best describes the difference between the Leclanche cell and the commercial alkaline battery?
a: The alkaline battery has a carbon anode, while the Leclanche cell does not
The alkaline battery has a carbon cathode, while the Leclanche cell does not
e: Both batteries work hard, but alkaline cells use a different chemical liquid inside to keep the electric juice flowing.

q: D orbitals can overlap to form sigma, pi, or delta bonds. Which of these types of d-d bonds is strongest?
e: Sigma bonds meet head-on like an unbreakable high-five, gripping far more tightly than sideways bonds ever could.

q: An aqueous solution contains silver ions, barium ions, iron (III) ions, and nitrate ions. Upon addition of sodium chloride, which of the following will precipitate out of the solution first?
e: Silver and chloride rush together so eagerly to make an insoluble pair that they tumble out of the water first!

q: Which of the following best describes the difference between gas diffusion and gas effusion?
a: Diffusion occurs at constant temperature while effusion occurs at variable temperatures
Diffusion can occur with any gas while effusion occurs only with certain gases
Diffusion involves gas molecules at the same total pressure while effusion involves gases moving from high pressure to low pressure
Diffusion is mass dependent while effusion is mass independent
e: Diffusion lets cozy gas friends mingle at the same pressure, while effusion is gas squeezing eagerly from high pressure into low pressure!

q: Which of the following ionic compounds would have the highest melting point:
e: Magnesium and oxygen carry double electric charges and hug super tightly, needing huge blast-furnace heat to melt apart.

q: Which of the following sulfate salts is the most soluble in water?
e: While other heavy sulfates stubbornly clump together, friendly zinc sulfate happily lets water molecules break it apart and dissolve.

q: What are the primary mobile charge carriers in the sulfonated fluoropolymer [floor-oh-PAWL-ih-mur] ion-exchange membranes used in commercial fuel cells?
e: Tiny, energetic protons zip right through the special plastic pathways like little runners carrying electricity across the finish line!

q: Which of the following is the molarity of a 3.0 liter solution that contains 21 grams of methane?
e: Twenty-one grams of methane makes about 1.3 moles of gas. Spread through three liters of space, that gives a molarity of 0.44.

q: Which of the following elements has the largest first ionization energy?
e: Argon is so completely full and satisfied with its electrons that it holds tight, needing the biggest energy push to let one go.

q: Which of the following statements about a valid wave function is true?
a: A wave function must be single-valued
A wave function must approach infinity as r approaches zero
The spatial integral of wave functions for different orbitals in an atom must be one
The integral of the wave function times its own complex conjugate must equal zero
e: A particle cannot be in two different realities at once, so a proper wave function gives just one single value everywhere.

q: In order to enhance the activity of the catalyst, a textural or chemical promoter may be used in ammonia synthesis. Which of the following is an example of a chemical promoter?
e: Potassium oxide generously donates electrons to help the catalyst work faster, chemically cheering on the whole ammonia-making team!

q: Which of the following graphs would produce a straight line if plotted for a zero- order irreversible reaction?
e: In this reaction, chemicals vanish at one steady pace like sand in an hourglass, drawing a straight line when graphing concentration against time.

q: Making biodiesels is a transesterification reaction. Which of the following represents the product(s) of this reaction?
e: Oils swap partners with alcohol, creating fatty acid esters to power engines and leaving behind sweet, syrupy glycerol.

q: Silicon can be doped with which of the following to produce a p-type semiconductor?
e: Aluminum has one less outer electron than silicon, creating welcoming empty spots called holes that make a positive p-type semiconductor!

q: Which of the following nucleotides [NOO-klee-uh-tyds] is not derived from pyrimidine [py-RIM-i-deen]?
e: Guanine is built with two chemical rings instead of one, making it a purine rather than a smaller pyrimidine cousin.

q: Which of the following is NOT a step in balancing a redox reaction in an acidic solution?
a: Write the unbalanced net ionic equation
Determine which atoms are oxidized and which atoms are reduced
Balance each half-reaction for O by adding hydroxide (OH-) to the side with less oxygen
Balance each half-reaction for H by adding H+ to the side with less H
e: In an acid bath, oxygen is balanced using water molecules, not hydroxide ions, which only show up at basic pool parties.

q: Scientists at SLAC National Lab have developed a way to use diamond anvils to drive chemical reactions using which of the following?
e: Super-hard diamond tips squeeze molecules together with immense crushing pressure, gently nudging stubborn atoms into brand-new friendships.

q: Which of the following types of battery is most commonly used in automobiles?
e: Trusty lead-acid batteries sit under car hoods, providing a mighty jolt of electricity to wake up the engine each morning.

q: Which of the following statements about Fischer projections is false?
a: The structure may be rotated by 90 degrees or 180 degrees
Four bonds to a chiral [KY-ruhl] carbon make a cross with the carbon at the intersection of horizontal and vertical lines
Two horizontal bonds are directed toward the viewer
Two vertical bonds are directed behind the stereogenic carbon
e: Spinning these drawings by ninety degrees accidentally flips chemical bonds inside-out, turning the molecule into its mirror image instead.

q: Which of the following is NOT true of uranium:
a: uranium is sometimes used in counterweights in yacht keels
there are only 3 isotopes of uranium
e: Uranium is actually a big family with over a dozen known isotopes, making the claim of only three completely false.

q: Drift and diffusion both describe the movement of particles. Which of the following is an example of drift?
a: Atoms moving from areas of high concentration to areas of low concentration
e: Instead of wandering randomly, electrons feeling an electric field march in neat unison straight toward the positive anode.

q: An alkyne[AL-kine] is added to a reaction vessel containing pressurized hydrogen gas and a catalyst consisting of palladium [pah-LAID-ee-um] poisoned by traces of lead(II) ions and quinoline [KWIN-oh- lin]. Which of the following is the major product of this reaction?
e: The tired-out catalyst adds hydrogen friends to the exact same side of the chemical chain, neatly shaping a happy cis-alkene.

q: Colloids formed by the dispersal of a gas in a liquid are called:
e: When bubbly pockets of gas get trapped dancing inside a liquid, they create fluffy, airy foam like whipped cream or soap suds.

q: Copper (II) hydroxide is insoluble in water. However, upon the addition of excess ammonia, it dissolves and changes to a deep blue color. Which of the following statements best explains this observation?
a: The rise in pH solubilized the copper hydroxide
The drop in pH solubilized the copper hydroxide
The copper reacted with ammonia, forming a soluble species
The ammonia neutralized the hydroxide, releasing soluble copper (II)
e: Shy copper was hiding as solid sludge, until friendly ammonia invited it to dance into a gorgeous, dissolved blue party!

q: Which of the following statements is true of first-order reactions?
a: The change in concentration of reactant is constant over time
The percentage change in concentration of reactant is constant over time
The half-life changes depending on the concentration of reactant
The half-life changes depending on the concentration of product
e: Like a magical pie that loses half its slice every hour, this reaction always gobbles up the exact same percentage over time!

q: Hydrogen peroxide is:
a: Less dense than water and boils at a lower temperature
Less dense than water and boils at a higher temperature
More dense than water and boils at a lower temperature
More dense than water and boils at a higher temperature
e: Packed with an extra oxygen atom, bubbly hydrogen peroxide is heavier than water and takes way more heat before it finally boils.

q: A lightning bolt strikes a power station, transmitting a current of 30,000 amps for 100 microseconds into it, which is currently charging a 2,000-milliampere-hour battery. Assuming that the charge from the lightning bolt is perfectly transmitted into the battery, which of the following percentages is closest to the percentage of the battery that it would charge?
e: That giant flash vanishes in a blink, delivering so little electric juice that it charges less than one tiny percent!

q: Which of the following bonds has the shortest bond length?
e: Tiny fluorine hugs hydrogen closer than any of its bigger cousins, making their little bond the shortest of all.

q: Which of the following is NOT a colligative property:
e: While crowds of particles change boiling and pressure, a solution picks its own pretty color based on who is inside, not how many!

q: Which of the following sets of values best approximates an average micrite limestone in a ternary diagram with end members (1) allochemical grains, (2) chemical cement, (3) microcrystalline matrix?
e: This ancient sea mud rock is mostly a cozy blanket of tiny crystals, with three-quarters matrix and zero chemical cement holding it together.

q: Doping a silicon crystal with which of the following elements would produce an n-type semiconductor?
e: Heavy bismuth brings an extra negative electron to the silicon party, creating an n-type crystal ready to conduct current!

q: Which of the following period 3 elements has the smallest atomic radius?
e: With lots of positive pull in its center, chlorine tugs its electron cloud in tight, making it the smallest atom in the row.

q: Which one of these factors is NOT used for determining what chemicals are blended to make gasoline?
e: Fuel blends change for chilly seasons, cost, and clean air, but moving gasoline around does not change the recipe inside the tank.

q: Which of the following is NOT a state function?
e: Heat depends entirely on the journey you take to get warm, so it cannot be a fixed state function like volume or pressure.

q: Which of the following would you expect to have an electron affinity of zero:
e: Content little helium already has a perfectly full shell, so it has zero interest in grabbing another electron!

q: Which of the following is an example of an ionic compound?
e: Calcium gladly gives its electrons to sulfur, locking this metal and nonmetal together in a super-strong ionic hug.

q: Which of the following statements is TRUE of dynamic equilibrium in chemistry?
a: Forward and backward rate constants are equal to zero
Forward and backward rate constants are equal in value
Forward and backward rates are equal to zero
Forward and backward rates are equal in value
e: It is a busy two-way street where molecules rush forward and backward at the exact same speed, keeping everything in balance!

q: The bond angle in NH3 is closest to which of the following degree values?
e: A pushy lone pair of electrons nudges ammonia's hydrogen arms slightly closer together, settling right near one hundred and ten degrees.

q: Which of the following metals exhibits a strong inert-pair effect?
e: Heavy thallium has a sleepy pair of electrons that loves to stay put instead of bonding, showing off the inert-pair effect!

q: Which is the chemical name of H2O?
e: Dihydrogen monoxide just means two hydrogens sharing a hug with one oxygen atom, creating the splashy water we drink every day.

q: Consider the following equilibrium reaction, FeO(solid) + CO(gas) Fe(solid) + CO2(gas), where H (read as: delta H) equals -10 kilojoules. Which of the following would have a similar effect on the equilibrium position as lowering the temperature:
e: Taking away carbon dioxide coaxes the reaction to rush forward to replace it, just like cooling down does!

q: When considering the total U.S. energy resources and reserves, coal represents 2.3% of the energy base. What approximate percentage does geothermal represent?
e: Deep beneath our feet, Earth's fiery belly holds an astonishing thirty-nine percent of all our energy treasure!

q: Which of the following is NOT true about amino acids:
a: amino acids exist primarily as zwitterions
an amino acid becomes neutral at its isoelectric point
tryptophan and cysteine contain sulfur atoms in their side chains
e: While cysteine carries a spark of sulfur, tryptophan prefers nitrogen in its ring, so they do not both share sulfur!

q: Which of the following BEST describes the process of coal liquefaction?
a: It converts coal into synthetic fuels
It reduces carbon dioxide emissions in coal plants
It removes sulfur from coal in coal plants
It converts coal into an easily transportable form
e: Imagine turning lumpy black rocks into bubbly liquid fuel for cars! Coal liquefaction works that chemical magic, converting solid coal into usable synthetic fuels.

q: Which of the following explains why extremely high energy is needed for fusion to work?
a: To break the nuclei into two parts
To bind the protons and electrons
To overcome the electrical repulsion between two positively charged nuclei
To create the necessary supercold environment
e: Like two stubborn magnets pushing apart, positive nuclei hate touching. It takes tons of energy to shove past that electrical repulsion so they can fuse!

q: What color can hexa-aqua-iron (III) appear to be in aqueous solution?
e: Iron ions swimming with water molecules show off a warm, sunny yellow glow in their solution!

q: Which of the following does NOT have the electron configuration of argon:
e: While the other busy atoms gather eighteen electrons to dress up like argon, tiny oxygen only grabs ten, matching cozy neon instead.

q: Which of the following organic functionalities is considered the most oxidized carbon atom?
e: A carboxylic acid carbon loves oxygen so much it shares three whole bonds with it, making it the most oxidized of the bunch.

q: What happens when metal freezes and forms a solid?
a: The metal gets high electrical conductivity
e: As molten metal cools, its restless atoms settle down and lock hands in neat, orderly rows called crystals.

q: Assuming that none of the following molecules contain any rings, which one contains exactly one carbon-carbon or carbon-oxygen double bond?
e: With eight hydrogens for four carbons, C4H8O has just enough missing pieces to form exactly one snug double bond.

q: A scientist thinks she has found a sample of rock 10 billion years old, a leftover fragment from the formation of an early solar system. Which of the following parent isotope's concentrations would be most useful in confirming this?
e: Potassium-40 ticks like an ancient clock with a half-life of over a billion years, making it perfect for dating rock from our solar system's birth.

q: Which of the following has a melting point of 185C and readily dissolves in water at room temperature, but is NOT an electrolyte:
e: Table sugar, or sucrose, happily melts into water without breaking into ions, so it sweetly dissolves without carrying any electric current.

q: Which of the following functional groups can be found in sucrose?
e: Sucrose is covered in friendly alcohol groups, which love bonding with water and give sugar its wonderfully sweet personality.

q: Which of the following statements is TRUE regarding calorimetry and heating curves?
a: Bomb calorimeters directly measure the change in enthalpy of a reaction
A heating curve plots pressure versus temperature and is divided into three regions
Regions depicting a phase change are flat on a heating curve
The steeper the slope of a heating curve, the higher the heat capacity of that phase
e: During a phase change, temperature pauses while heat works on breaking bonds, making the heating curve flat like a resting step!

q: Which of the following molecules exhibits intermolecular attractions commonly referred to as hydrogen bonding?
e: Formic acid, or HCOOH, has hydrogen bonded straight to oxygen, letting it link arms with neighbors through super-sticky hydrogen bonds.

q: Which of the following best explains why nickel-cadmium batteries are being replaced by other types of batteries?
a: Cadmium is a heavy metal pollutant
They do not have a consistent terminal voltage
They rapidly lose the ability to store charge
e: Cadmium is a toxic heavy metal that can poison nature, so cleaner batteries are stepping in to keep our planet safe.

q: Which of the following elements will react most vigorously with water to form hydrogen gas as a by-product?
e: Potassium is so eager to lose an electron that tossing it into water sparks a wild, sizzling burst of hydrogen gas!

q: If the atomic mass of carbon-12 is exactly 12 atomic mass units, why is the atomic mass of carbon not exactly 12 when listed on the Periodic Table:
a: neutrons are not the same mass as protons
it adds the mass of the electrons
the presence in nature of about 1.1% carbon-13
e: Nature mixes in a pinch of heavier carbon-13 atoms, nudging the average weight slightly above twelve on the periodic table.

q: Melissa is attempting to dissolve a solid in water to form a solution. After vigorous agitation, she can no longer visibly see particles of solid. Which of the following steps should she take next to determine if the solid has completely dissolved?
a: If she sees no visible particles, the solid has dissolved completely
She should shine a beam of light through the sample
She should determine if the freezing point of the sample has changed
She should measure the vapor pressure of the sample
e: Shining a beam of light reveals hidden floating specks that scatter light, proving whether the solid truly dissolved into a solution.

q: Natural gas is often stored and transported as a liquid because:
a: It is less flammable as a liquid
It takes up less space as a liquid
Liquid natural gas does not smell as bad
e: Chilling natural gas into a liquid squeezes it down to fit in much smaller tanks, making it far easier to travel!

q: Which of the following accurately depicts the hybridization [HY-bri-dy-zay-shuhn] of each atom in the molecule krypton difluoride?
e: Krypton juggles five electron pairs to become sp3d, while each fluorine happily arranges four pairs into neat sp3 shapes.

q: Which of the following anhydrous compounds has the lowest melting point?
e: Aluminum chloride shares its electrons more like a molecule than a tough ionic crystal, so it melts at a much lower temperature.

q: Which of the following is typically TRUE of organic compounds:
a: the simplest carboxylic acid is ethanoic acid
ketones have no hydrogen atoms directly attached to the carbonyl group
e: In a ketone, the central carbon is snuggled between two other carbons, leaving no room for any hydrogen to attach directly.

q: Ceramic materials have all but which of the following properties?
e: Ceramics love staying stiff, so they snap instead of stretching like silly putty. That means high ductility is one trick they just cannot do!

q: In the Haber process, one mole of nitrogen gas reacts with three moles of hydrogen gas to produce two moles of ammonia. The process is exothermic. If a particular Haber synthesis is at equilibrium [ee-kwuh-LIB-ree-uhm], which of the following changes to the reaction's conditions are predicted by Le Chatelier's principle to INCREASE the yield of ammonia?
a: Increasing the pressure of the reaction mixture
Increasing the volume of the reaction vessel
e: Squeezing all those crowded gas molecules together pushes them into fewer, tidier spaces, happily creating more ammonia!

q: A supersaturated solution of sodium nitrate was prepared at 80 degrees Celsius but cooled to room temperature. Which of the following statements describes the addition of a seed crystal?
a: Delta H is negative and Delta S is negative
Delta H is positive and Delta S is negative
Delta H is negative and Delta S is positive
Delta H is positive and Delta S is positive
e: Tiny crystals snap into neat, orderly rows while releasing a warm sigh of heat, so both enthalpy and entropy go down!

q: Nanotechnologists are creating butterfly scale patterns on paper money to foil counterfeiters using which of the following substances?
e: Clever scientists use shiny aluminum oxide like microscopic paint to copy butterfly wings, making money sparkle too brightly for copycats to fake!

q: Assuming a temperature where the net magnetic moment is nonzero, which of the following types of magnetism will have the weakest external field?
e: In antiferromagnetism, tiny magnetic neighbors point in opposite directions, stubbornly canceling each other out until almost no magnetic pull escapes outside.

q: In preparing to perform a flame test on a sample, a high molar solution of which of the following chemicals would be best to use to clean your nichrome wire?
e: Strong hydrochloric acid is the ultimate tidy scrubber, dissolving every leftover crumb so your wire burns clean and shows its true colors.

q: A student obtained a low value when he attempted to measure the number of waters of hydration in a sample of calcium sulfate. Which of the following mistakes could lead to the erroneous result?
a: The sample was not heated enough
The sample was heated too much
A balance that gave uniformly high readings was used
A balance that gave uniformly low readings was used
e: If the sample is not heated enough, stubborn water droplets stay trapped inside, making your final water count too low.

q: Which of the following is NOT a constitutional isomer of the organic compound whose molecular formula is C4H8:
e: With five carbons tucked inside, 2-methyl-1-butene brought an extra friend to the party, so it cannot fit the four-carbon recipe!

q: Which of the following sets of elements are commonly referred to as d block elements?
e: Transition metals live right in the bustling middle neighborhood of the periodic table, where chemists call them the d-block elements.

q: Which of the following acids is diprotic?
e: Generous oxalic acid comes with two hydrogen friends to give away, making it diprotic!

q: Which of the following compounds has the smallest bond angle?
e: Phosphane has a giant, pushy electron cloud that shoves its little hydrogen legs super close together, making the tiniest angle!

q: Scientists at Ames Lab have developed solvent-free techniques to synthesize alkali metal hydrides. Which of the following techniques do they use to unambiguously determine that the hydrogen atoms have bound to the metal?
e: Solid-state NMR uses gentle magnetic waves to listen in and confirm where tiny hydrogen atoms snuggle into the metal.

q: Consider a gas-phase reaction where delta-H is less than delta-U. If the reaction is at equilibrium, which of the following changes will ALWAYS shift the reaction mixture to the right?
e: When you squeeze the container smaller, the crowded gases scurry toward the side with fewer molecules, happily shifting to the right!

q: When the change of enthalpy of a reaction is negative and the change of entropy of the same reaction is positive, the reaction is which of the following?
a: Spontaneous only under high temperature conditions
Spontaneous only under low temperature conditions
e: When a reaction releases heat and makes a joyful mess, nature loves both so much that it is always spontaneous!

q: Identify which of the following types of copolymer [koh-POL- uh-mer] would be represented by a molecule with the linkage pattern FGGFFFGFG?
e: The building blocks mingle in a playful, random shuffle without neat patterns or giant blocks, making this chain statistical.

q: Nitrogen monoxide is an example of which of the following?
