q: Which of the following is considered a monoprotic acid:
e: With just a single acidic hydrogen proton to give away, hypochlorous acid is a proud, one-shot monoprotic donor.

q: Which of the following is the least geographically-restricted form of grid-scale energy storage?
e: While giant water dams need big mountains, cheerful batteries can be set up almost anywhere you can place a box!

q: Nick has an unknown compound that he has determined to be soluble in water and produces a solution that is not electrically conductive. Which of the following might the compound be?
e: Sweet sucrose melts invisibly into water as whole neutral molecules, leaving no charged ions to carry an electric spark.

q: What is the major product in the ethoxide-promoted [beta]- elimination of 1-chloro-1-methylcyclohexane [1-chloro-1-meth-uhl-sy-kluh-HEK-sayn]?
e: Nature loves stability, so the reaction builds its sturdy double bond inside the ring, happily forming 1-methyl-1-cyclohexene.

q: Which of the following is a term used to describe the electronic geometry around a central atom that has 5 regions of high electron density:
e: Five electron clouds pushing apart spread into a flat three-cornered triangle with two poles, creating a neat trigonal bipyramidal shape.

q: Which of the following transition metal 2+ ions is most commonly found in a square planar geometry?
e: Nickel two-plus has eight outer electrons that love lounging flat in four corners, forming a tidy square planar shape.

q: Which of the following molecules is most likely to have a zero dipole moment based on its molecular shape:
e: Standing in a perfectly straight line, two fluoride buddies pull in exact opposite directions, canceling out the molecule's electric pull.

q: Which of the following gases has the highest effusion rate through a pinhole opening from one compartment to another and at room temperature:
e: Featherweight helium atoms zip around faster than the heavier gases, slipping through tiny pinholes in the blink of an eye!

q: Which of the following oxygen- containing compounds has the highest mass percentage of oxygen?
e: Al2O3 packs three eager oxygen atoms onto two light aluminum helpers, making oxygen the heavyweight champ of this little family.

q: Which of the following is never considered evidence of a chemical change?
e: Melting ice is still just water wearing a different outfit, so a phase change never means a brand-new substance was born.

q: Which of the following is NOT true about enzymes?
a: They catalyze most of the chemical changes that occur in a cell
They are unchanged by the reaction they catalyze
They do not change the normal equilibrium position of a chemical system
They change the amount of product that is produced
e: Enzymes are speedy little helpers that hurry a reaction along, but they never change how much stuff gets made in the end.

q: Which of the following both have very similar chemical compositions but exhibit different colors:
e: Ruby and sapphire are twin mineral sisters made of the exact same crystal, just wearing different colorful mineral jackets!

q: Which of the following quantities increases with the addition of a catalyst?
e: A catalyst acts like a cheerful shortcut, helping molecules find each other faster so the reaction rate speeds right up!

q: Which of the following molecules has a tetrahedral molecular geometry?
e: Carbon tetrafluoride looks like a tiny pyramid tent, with four fluorine friends pushing apart evenly around their central carbon buddy.

q: Which of the following polyprotic [polly-PRO-tic] acids has only two pKa values?
e: Friendly ascorbic acid has only two hydrogen gifts to share, giving it just two special give-away steps called pKa values.

q: Which of the following ions has the LARGEST radius?
e: Arsenic three minus stuffs three extra electrons into its shell, puffing up like a giant balloon because its center holds them loosely.

q: Which of the following is not true of oxalic acid?
a: It can be oxidized to carbon dioxide
It contains three oxygen atoms per molecule
It contains two carbon atoms per molecule
e: Oxalic acid actually holds four oxygen atoms in its cozy frame, so saying it only has three is a tiny mistake!

q: Which of the following best describes the elementary kinetic step where a proton is transferred directly between an ammonium ion and water?
e: It takes two partner molecules bumping together for this proton dance, which scientists call bimolecular teamwork.

q: Identify the statement that does NOT describe a prostaglandin [pros-tuh-LAN-din] lipid function.
a: Prostaglandins are involved in the inflammatory response process
Prostaglandins play a role in blood clot formation but not clot reduction
Prostaglandins can help to increase kidney blood flow
e: Helpful prostaglandins are busy multitaskers that both build and break down blood clots, keeping your bloodstream perfectly balanced.

q: In a phase diagram, the solid-liquid line has a negative slope for which of the following pure substances:
e: Water is wonderfully weird because its ice floats, making its solid-liquid line tilt backward unlike almost anything else!

q: Which of the following statements concerning crystal structure is NOT true?
a: HCP lattices are more space-filling than FCC lattices
Cesium [SEEZ-ee-um] chloride lattices form when anions [AN-eye-ons] and cations [CAT-eye-onz] are of roughly equal size
The crystal structure of a metal is dependent on pressure and temperature
e: HCP and FCC crystals are equally brilliant at packing their atomic marbles tightly, so one never out-packs the other!

q: Which of the following elements, in its gaseous state, has the greatest electron affinity?
e: Tiny fluorine pulls fiercely on wandering electrons because its compact heart loves snatching up negative charges.

q: Which of the following titrations would have an equivalence point with a pH closest to 9?
a: Titration of sodium hydroxide with hydrochloric acid
Titration of hydrochloric acid with ammonia
Titration of acetic acid with sodium hydroxide
Titration of barium hydroxide with sulfuric acid
e: Mixing weak acetic acid with mighty sodium hydroxide leaves behind basic salt buddies that sweetly push the pH near nine!

q: Given that the standard enthalpy [EN-thal-pee] of formation for solid calcium carbonate is -1200 kilojoules per mole, for solid calcium oxide is -600 kilojoules per mole, and for gaseous carbon dioxide is -400 kilojoules per mole, which of the following is the standard enthalpy change in kilojoules per mole for the reaction: CaCO3 (s) [yields] CaO (s) + CO2 (g)?
e: The products together hold minus one thousand, and subtracting the starting energy leaves a sunny positive two hundred kilojoules behind.

q: If two solutions that are separated by a semipermeable membrane have the same osmotic pressure, they are said to be:
e: When two watery worlds push across a fence with equal strength, they live in peaceful, balanced isotonic harmony.

q: With regard to crystalline solids, which of the following most aptly describes a covalent network?
a: Low melting point, soft, excellent thermal conductor
Low to high melting point, hard, moderate electrical conductor
High melting point, soft, poor electrical conductor
High melting point, hard, poor thermal conductor
e: Giant covalent networks link atoms in super-strong handshakes, making them tough, high-melting fortresses that keep heat from traveling easily.

q: Which of the following functional groups is most likely to be formed when dodecane [doh-DECK-ane] undergoes "cracking?"
e: Snapping a long oil chain in half forces some broken pieces to form double-bonded alkene handshakes to stay happy.

q: Which of the following is a metallic element, composes about 5% of the Earth's crust, oxidizes very easily, and when pure is a dark, silver-grey metal:
e: Iron makes up five percent of Earth's crust and loves rusting into reddish dust when it touches air.

q: Which of the following is NOT a component of a phospholipid [fos-foh-LIP-id]?
e: A phospholipid has greasy tails and a cozy head, but water is just a splashy neighbor outside, not a building block!

q: Which of the following is an example of effusion?
a: The formation of snowflakes in the upper atmosphere
The evaporation of water from a lake
A bike tire losing air after running over a nail
e: Tiny air molecules sneak out through a pinprick hole in a punctured tire, playing the ultimate game of hide-and-seek called effusion.

q: Which of the following metals could NOT successfully be used to galvanize iron?
e: To protect iron, a bodyguard metal must sacrifice itself, but nickel is too stubborn to give up its electrons first.

q: Which of the following molecular geometries can exhibit meridional isomerism?
e: Like six dancers holding hands around a globe, an octahedral shape can line three friends up along its equator for meridional isomerism.

q: In comparison to a gallon of gasoline, how much energy is contained in a gallon of ethanol?
e: A gallon of ethanol packs a gentle punch, carrying only about 70 percent of the fiery get-up-and-go energy found in gasoline!

q: According to VSEPR theory, which of the following could NOT be the molecular geometry of a compound with a trigonal bipyramidal electron-pair geometry?
e: Trigonal pyramidal shapes belong to tetrahedral families, so a five-legged electron cloud can never fold into one.

q: O2 and O3 are considered what type of molecules?
e: Oxygen atoms can hold hands as twins or triplets, making these different forms of the same element true allotropes!

q: Which of the following energy sources produces the least carbon dioxide per unit of energy?
e: Nuclear power splits tiny atoms instead of burning fuel, releasing giant bursts of clean energy without puffing out carbon dioxide.

q: When iron becomes the ion Fe2+, it
e: Iron sheds its two outermost 4s electrons first, happily tossing them aside like an old winter coat to become Fe2+!

q: During fission in a nuclear reactor, non-fission neutron capture by uranium yields heavy elements like americium and plutonium. What are these elements called?
e: These heavy radioactive cousins all live together on that special bottom row of the periodic table, proudly called the actinides.

q: What substance was the primary fuel source for NASA space shuttles?
e: Chilled until it turned into a freezing sea, liquid hydrogen gave rockets the super-lightweight punch needed to reach the stars!

q: A reaction is carried out in a constant pressure calorimeter. Appropriate measurements are taken and the energy for the change is calculated. The quantity of heat exchanged under these conditions leads to the calculation of which of the following state functions?
e: When pressure stays totally still, heat on the move is measured as enthalpy, happily wearing the letter H!

q: Which of the following ions is most similar in ionic radius to the cation Na+?
e: Calcium loses two electrons and shrinks down to almost the exact same cuddly size as a sodium ion.

q: Which of the following does not describe how atoms in a CH2 group can vibrate?
e: Carbon and hydrogen love to rock, stretch, and twist together, but they never do a silly see-saw dance.

q: Which of the following diatomic molecules will exhibit paramagnetism:
e: Boron twins share electrons but leave two spinning alone, acting like tiny magnets that love to feel magnetic fields!

q: Di-iodine gas can dissociate into two atoms of iodine gas. At 1200 kelvins, the forward reaction has an equilibrium constant of approximately 10. In kilojoules [KILL-oh- jools] per mole, which of the following is closest to the standard change in Gibbs free energy of this reaction?
e: Because the reaction rolls forward with an equilibrium constant of ten, its free energy drops downhill to around minus twenty kilojoules.

q: If an endothermic reaction is at equilibrium [ee-kwuh-LIB-ree- uhm], how will the equilibrium shift if the temperature is raised?
a: Toward both the reactants and the products
It will not shift in either direction
e: Heat feeds an endothermic reaction like warm soup, happily nudging it forward to make even more products!

q: Which of the following pairs of fundamental forces are the most important for modeling the behavior of nucleons in a carbon-12 nucleus?
e: The strong force glues the nucleus together like magic tape, while electromagnetic forces push the sunny positive protons apart.

q: Which of the following sectors in the U.S. uses the most petroleum?
e: Zooming cars, rumbling trucks, and soaring airplanes make transportation the thirstiest machine for petroleum of them all!

q: Which of the following species is NOT considered an electrolyte?
e: Diethyl ether holds its molecules tightly together without making ions, so electric currents cannot hitch a ride through it.

q: Which of the following liquids is least viscous? Assume temperature is 25°C.
e: Acetone is super runny and thin, racing and splashing along much faster than thick water or heavy mercury!

q: Which of the following chemical bonds is not important in polymer formation?
e: Building giant polymer chains takes super-strong covalent handshakes, so gentle hydrogen bonds are just too weak to hold the main backbone together.

q: Tollens' test can detect aldehyde [AL-deh-hide]-containing compounds. To perform Tollens' test, an organic compound is mixed with a solution of silver ions. Which of the following indicates that the compound of interest contains an aldehyde?
a: Insoluble silver oxide precipitates from solution
The aldehyde is reduced to an alcohol
e: When aldehydes meet silver ions, they gift them electrons, turning the glass into a shiny, sparkling silver mirror!

q: Which of the following best explains why a beam of light is scattered when it shines through milk but not through water?
a: Milk is a colloid, while water is not
Milk forms weaker hydrogen bonds than water
Milk has a higher vapor pressure than water
e: Milk is a colloid packed with tiny floating bits that bump light beams around like pinballs, while plain water lets light zip right through.

q: How would you classify a reaction in which solid potassium and chlorine gas react to form the ionic compound potassium chloride?
e: Potassium and chlorine joyfully combine into one brand-new compound, which makes this a synthesis reaction because they built something together.

q: What kind of isomers are mannose and glucose?
e: These two sweet sugars are diastereoisomers because their atoms bend slightly differently without being perfect mirror reflections of each other.

q: Which of the following is a triprotic [try-PRO-tic] acid?
e: Phosphoric acid is triprotic because it happily carries three hydrogen protons, ready to give all three away one by one.

q: If you were to use hydrogen fuel cells in spacecraft, what kind of fuel cell type would you most likely prefer?
e: Astronauts love alkaline cells because they run super efficiently on pure rocket gases and even brew fresh drinking water for the crew!

q: The oxidation number of oxygen is -1 in:
e: In peroxides, oxygen atoms hold hands in pairs, sharing electrons so each one only takes on a minus-one charge.

q: Which of the following is an alternative name for 1,3-xylene?
e: Meta means leaving a one-spot gap on the carbon ring, which matches 1,3-xylene perfectly as its friendly groups skip a seat.

q: For the reaction N2 + 3H2 in equilibrium with 2NH3, with a negative change in enthalpy, which of the following events is least likely to occur when the temperature of the reaction is increased?
a: The gas particles will speed up
The reaction will produce more ammonia
The entropy of the system will increase
e: This cozy reaction already releases heat, so adding extra warmth actually pushes it backward, making it produce less ammonia instead of more.

q: Which of the following would least likely be used for biomass energy production?
a: Urban wood waste and biodegradable garbage
Car parts from a salvage yard
e: Biomass energy comes from living things like plants and trees, but old metal car parts never grew from the sunny earth.

q: Which of the following chemicals is least likely to hydrogen bond with water?
e: Water loves polar friends, but oily benzene is nonpolar and lacks the oxygen or nitrogen hooks needed for hydrogen bonds.

q: Which of the following is closest to the pKa of an acid whose Ka = 5.0 10-4:
e: Using the negative log turns that tiny power of minus-four into a neat, friendly acidity score of about 3.3.

q: J.J. Thomson invented a prototype mass spectrometer that enabled him to measure what property of the electron?
e: Thomson watched electric and magnetic forces bend zooming electrons, cleverly figuring out their mass-to-charge ratio from how much they curved.

q: Which of the following is a weak electrolyte:
e: Ammonia is a weak electrolyte because only a tiny handful of its molecules split into charged ions when swimming in water.

q: Which of the following silver salts with the given Ksp values has the greatest molar solubility?
e: A bigger Ksp means it dissolves much easier, and silver chloride has the largest number here, making it the most soluble.

q: Which of the following is the general formula for a noncyclic alkene (read carefully as: al-KEEN) with n number of carbon atoms:
e: Because alkenes share a special double bond, they hold exactly twice as many hydrogens as carbons, making CnH2n the perfect recipe.

q: Which of the following is generally NOT considered to be an appropriate SN2 electrophile?
e: In vinyl bromide, the carbon is locked in a flat double bond, totally blocking the backside attack needed for an SN2 reaction.

q: Which of the following electron configurations is correct for neutral copper?
e: Copper cleverly borrows one electron from the 4s level to fill its 3d shell completely, because filled shells are super stable.

q: The dissolving ability of water is related to which of the following?
a: The attraction between the water molecule's positive and negative charges and charges on other atoms
Its ability to form hydrogen bonds with other molecules
Its ability to transmit energy from water molecule to water molecule
e: Tiny water molecules act like playful magnets, using their plus and minus ends to hug and tug other atoms apart.

q: Which of the following strong acids, all at 0.1 molar concentration, will have the LOWEST pH value:
e: Sulfuric acid carries two acid protons to share instead of just one, packing twice the punch to make the lowest pH!

q: Converting a power generating plant from coal to natural gas will reduce sulfur emissions by approximately which of the following percentages?
e: Switching over clears the air by cutting those smelly sulfur clouds right in half, leaving fifty percent less behind.

q: Plutonium Uranium Redox Extraction, or PUREX, is a standard worldwide method for doing which of the following?
e: PUREX acts like a clever recycling machine, washing and saving leftover nuclear fuel so it can make power again.

q: Which of the following ions does NOT have a noble gas electron configuration in ionic compounds:
e: Sodium loves giving away an electron to look like noble neon, so grabbing an extra one leaves its shell unmatching.

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true of polyunsaturated fatty acids?
a: They are highly concentrated in cell membranes of the nervous system
They are the most prevalent fatty acid found in the human body
They contain two or more double bonds
They play a crucial role in brain function
e: While these bendy fats are superstars in your brain, other common fats actually outnumber them inside our bodies.

q: The most accurate Lewis structure of phosphoric acid had one hydrogen atom bonded directly to the central phosphorous atom and two bonded to oxygen atoms. Given this information, which of the following terms best describes how phosphoric acid actually behaves in water?
e: Only the two hydrogens holding hands with oxygen can easily leap into the water, making this acid diprotic!

q: Which of the following catabolic pathways liberates carbon dioxide?
e: The citric acid cycle spins like a busy little wheel, breaking down food and puffing out carbon dioxide.

q: Ozonolysis [oh-zuh-NOL-uh-sis] cleaves which of the following?
e: Ozone swoops in like tiny scissors, neatly snipping the double bonds holding two carbon buddies together.

q: Which of the following atoms has an atomic radius closest to the atomic radius of sodium?
e: Calcium’s fluffy cloud of electrons spreads out to nearly the exact same size as sodium’s.

q: Which of the following is a substance whose molecular and empirical formulas are NOT the same:
e: Benzene is made of six carbons and six hydrogens, but its simplest recipe shrinks down to one of each.

q: The price of which of the following fuels has the greatest impact on the cost of electricity?
e: Natural gas is the go-to fuel that powers extra generators quickly, so its price tag steers your electric bill.

q: Which of the following energy resources is the most energy efficient, meaning very little of the energy created is transferred to the surroundings unused?
e: Hydrogen fuel cells turn clean fuel straight into electricity without burning, hardly wasting any energy at all.

q: Which of the following are elements in the Periodic Table whose outer shell electrons are on two principal energy levels:
e: Transition elements are busy multitaskers, happily juggling their outermost electrons across two different energy shells at once!

q: Consider the reaction of two moles of hydrogen gas and one mole of oxygen gas to generate two moles of steam. Which of the following statements is TRUE?
a: Delta H is greater than delta U
Delta H is less than delta U
Delta H is equal to delta U
Delta H is greater than delta U at high temperatures, but less at low temperatures
e: Three dancing gas molecules squeeze down into just two, so delta H ends up lower than delta U.

q: Which of the following represents the electron-pair geometry of the central oxygen atom of ozone?
e: Three electron groups push apart around the middle oxygen, spreading flat like a three-pointed star called trigonal planar.

q: Which of the following lattices is an example of cubic closest packing?
e: Nestling atoms tightly into corners and the middle of every square face packs them as close together as marbles in a box!

q: Which of the following compounds would be insoluble in an aqueous [AY-kwee-uhs] solution?
e: Calcium carbonate holds onto its partners so tightly that water cannot break them apart, keeping it solid chalk!

q: A sample of an ideal gas has a volume of 1 cubic meter at standard temperature and pressure. Which of the following is closest to the number of molecules in the sample?
e: That big box holds about forty-four moles of gas, multiplying into 2.7 times 10 to the 25th buzzing particles.

q: Which of the following molecules has the highest bond enthalpy, or energy it would take to break apart the bond:
e: Carbon and oxygen share a mighty triple bond, hugging so tightly that it takes massive energy to pull them apart!

q: Diesel fuel does not need a spark to ignite like gasoline does. Diesel can rely on compression to heat the fuel for which of the following reasons?
a: It has a lower molecular weight than gasoline
It has a lower flash point than gasoline
It has a lower auto ignition temperature than gasoline
It has a lower spark point than gasoline
e: Diesel gets so excited when squeezed that it catches fire all on its own at a lower temperature than gasoline.

q: In a nuclear power plant, the fission reaction directly yields all but which of the following?
e: Splitting atoms makes lots of heat and tiny flying bits, but spinning generators have to turn that heat into electricity later.

q: Which of the following pieces of glassware will most accurately transfer 10 milliliters of a solution?
e: A burette is like a skinny glass wand that lets you tap out liquid drop by tiny drop with super precise control.

q: Which of the following best describes the ground state electron configuration of chromium?
a: A fully-filled 4s orbital and five half-filled 3d orbitals
A half-filled 4s orbital and five fully-filled 3d orbitals
A half-filled 4s orbital and five half-filled 3d orbitals
An empty 4s orbital and five fully-filled 3d orbitals
e: Chromium loves fairness, so its six outer electrons share nicely, leaving both the 4s room and five 3d rooms half full.

q: Which of the following is NOT true about aqueous solutions:
a: diluting a buffer with water can change the pH of the water
metal cations can act as weak acids in water solutions
an acid whose Ka = 6 10-10 is weaker than an acid whose Ka = 5.8 10-4
an acid whose pKa is 3.0 is stronger than an acid whose pKa is 7.0
e: Buffers are stubborn little peacekeepers that hold their ground, refusing to let added water change their balanced pH level.

q: Which of the following types of mixtures displays the Tyndall effect and also separates when filtered?
e: In a suspension, floating bits are big enough to scatter beams of light and get caught in a paper filter trap.

q: Which of the following functional groups has the weakest carbon- oxygen bond?
e: Alcohol holds its oxygen partner with just a single bond, which is much easier to snap than sturdy double bonds.

q: What is the term for the ease of distortion of an electron cloud by an external entity?
e: Polarizability is just how squishy an atom's electron cloud is when another charged friend comes along and nudges it.

q: Which of the following best describes the kinetics of radioactive decay?
a: It is a zeroth order process
It is a first order process
It is a second order process
It is a third order process
e: In this first-order countdown, the speed depends only on how many lonely atoms are waiting their turn to decay.

q: The measured bond angle in ammonia is 107.3, whereas the bond angles in phosphine [FOS-feen] are 93.7. Which of the following facts correctly identifies the atomic property that makes the two angles different?
a: Ammonia and phosphine have different expected VSEPR geometries
Nitrogen is more electronegative than phosphorus
The bonding orbitals of phosphine have more s and less p character than those of ammonia
The phosphorus atom is much larger than the nitrogen atom
e: Phosphorus is much larger than nitrogen, so its roomy size lets its bonded arms squeeze closer together into smaller angles.

q: Which of the following atoms is commonly found in a +3 oxidation state?
e: Iron loves to give away three of its electrons, happily settling into a plus-three state when making reddish rust.

q: Consider the gas phase exothermic reaction of phosphorous trichloride [try-KLOOR-ide] with chlorine to yield phosphorous pentachloride. Under which of the following conditions is the equilibrium constant greater than one?
a: It is never greater than one
e: Because this reaction releases warmth, keeping things chilly encourages the chemicals to cuddle together and make even more product.

q: The reaction Ca(OH)2 + 2HCl 2H2O + CaCl2, is an example of what class of chemical reaction:
e: Like dancers swapping partners mid-song, the calcium and hydrogen trade places to form two brand-new pairs.

q: Solvent-based techniques best capture carbon dioxide under which of the following relative conditions?
e: Chilly temperatures and heavy pressure squeeze gas molecules together, helping liquids capture carbon dioxide like a cozy sponge.

q: Which of the following pairs does NOT correctly match the element and its oxidation number?
e: In hydrogen peroxide, the two oxygen friends share electrons equally, giving each an oxidation number of minus-one instead.

q: An atom is sp3 [S-P-3] hybridized. Which of the following is NOT a possible molecular geometry about this atom?
e: An sp3 atom only has four hybrid rooms to share, so it can never stretch into a five-cornered trigonal bipyramid.

q: Acid rain is unusually acidic precipitation containing elevated levels of hydrogen ions. Which of the following emissions is NOT an emission from a power plant that would contribute to acid rain?
e: Hydroxide is a base rather than an acid, so it neutralizes sourness instead of pouring down as acid rain.

q: Which of the following does not perform a chemical reaction during operation?
e: A wind turbine simply dances with the breeze, using pure mechanical motion instead of chemical reactions to make power.

q: Which of the following techniques employs a moving phase and a stationary phase to separate components of a mixture:
e: Chromatography works like a race where some chemicals zoom forward while others cling to the stationary track.

q: Which of the following is NOT true of halogens:
a: iodine is the least reactive of the stable halogens
elemental halogens exist as diatomic molecules containing single covalent bonds
their outermost electron configuration is represented by ns2np6
halides of typical metals are ionic
e: Halogens are always one electron short of a full set of eight, so their outer shell ends in five, not six.

q: How many protons are in an oxygen atom?
e: Every breath of oxygen you take is powered by atoms that hold exactly eight cheerful protons in their centers.

q: Which of the following molecules has a double covalent bond:
e: Two friendly oxygen atoms hold hands with two shared bonds instead of one, teaming up tight to make breathable oxygen gas!

q: Which of the following terms best describes the relationship between 1-butanol [one-BYOO-tan-all] and 4-butanol?
e: It is the very same molecule just flipped around, like looking at your favorite pencil from the eraser end instead of the tip!

q: Which of the following elements has the lowest freezing point?
e: Oxygen shivers down to colder temperatures than the others before freezing solid, needing extreme cold to finally sit still.

q: Which of the following molecules has T-shaped molecular geometry?
e: Two sneaky electron pairs shove the three fluorine atoms down, bending chlorine trifluoride into the shape of a capital T!

q: In a pressure-volume diagram of an isothermal expansion, what is represented by the area underneath the curve?
e: As the warm gas happily stretches out, it pushes outward against its container, and that shaded area measures the work it did!

q: Which of the following scientists is credited with discovering electrons and calculating their mass to charge ratio?
e: J.J. Thomson discovered tiny negative electrons zooming inside atoms, and clever math helped him weigh them against their electrical charge.

q: Dr. Ecniecs, the evil genius, has released multiple dangerous weather balloons into the atmosphere, filled with his new concoction - Boomgas! If the density of Boomgas drops below one third of its density at room temperature, it will explode with the force of 1/10th of an atomic bomb. Which of the following disposal methods would force the balloons to explode?
a: Throwing weighted balloons into the sea
Cryogenically storing the balloons in liquid nitrogen
e: In empty space, with no air pressing in, the balloon swells so huge that its gas thins out and kaboom!

q: What gas is produced by bacterial decay in landfills?
e: Trillions of busy little bacteria feast on buried trash in the dark and burp out methane gas as they digest!

q: Which of the following substances has the most spontaneous reduction half-reaction?
e: Fluorine is the greediest element around, eagerly snatching up new electrons faster and more easily than anyone else!

q: In what unit is the atomic radius often measured?
e: Atoms are so wonderfully tiny that regular rulers fail, so scientists measure them in picometers, which are trillionths of a meter.

q: Which of the following statements is true about alkenes [AL- keens] and alkynes [AL-kyns]?
a: Both can undergo hydrogenation to lose hydrogens
Both can undergo oxygenation to lose oxygens
e: Because they share extra bonds between carbons, both molecules still have room to welcome more hydrogen friends, making them unsaturated!

q: How would you classify a bacterium that derives its energy from inorganic sources such as hydrogen sulphide?
e: These clever microbes do not need sunlight to cook up dinner; they turn simple chemicals into food all by themselves!

q: Which of the following is NOT true in the titration of a weak monoprotic acid with a strong base?
a: The starting pH will be lower than 7
The final pH will be higher than 7
Methyl red would be a good indicator to use
Phenolphthalein [fee-knol-THAY-leen] would be a good indicator to use
e: This reaction finishes in basic territory, but methyl red changes color way too early while things are still acidic.

q: An aqueous solution of sodium sulfate is electrolyzed using platinum electrodes. If phenolphthalein [fee-nawlf-THAY-leen] indicator is added to the solution, which of the following will be observed?
a: The solution is colorless everywhere except at the cathode, where it is pink
The solution is colorless everywhere except at the anode, where it is pink
The solution is pink everywhere except at the cathode, where it is colorless
The solution is pink everywhere except at the anode, where it is colorless
e: Water turns into basic hydroxide ions right at the cathode, making the indicator blush a bright, cheerful pink only there!

q: Which of the following is the atomic sublevel with the next highest energy after the 4p sublevel:
e: Electrons love an easy climb, and the 5s room takes slightly less energy to move into than the 4d room next door.

q: Denatured alcohol contains which of the following toxic substances added to ethanol?
e: Poisonous methanol is sneakily mixed into ethanol so people cannot drink it, keeping the bottle strictly for cleaning and science!

q: Which of the following is NOT true for the reaction between silver nitrate and sodium chloride in solution?
a: Nitrate ion is not included in the net ionic equation
Silver ion is a spectator ion
One mole of sodium nitrate is produced per mole of silver nitrate reacted
e: Silver is definitely not just watching from the sidelines; it actively hugs chloride to form a brand-new solid crystal!

q: A carboxylic [CAR-box-IHL-ik] acid is stirred in a large excess of ethanol in the presence of a sulfuric acid catalyst. What functional group will this reaction form?
e: When the acid and alcohol link hands with a little chemical help, they create a sweet-smelling ester!

q: What is the electronic pair geometry and the molecular geometry typical of the molecule with the general formula AB4U, where A represents the central atom, B represent the bonded atoms, and U represent the unbonded electron pair:
e: Five electron clouds spread into a trigonal bipyramid, but that one lonely pair tilts the atoms like a playground seesaw!

q: What are the products of the complete combustion of cyclohexane [sy-kluh-HEK-sayn]?
a: Carbon monoxide, carbon trioxide and water
e: When this fuel burns up completely in plenty of oxygen, it magically transforms into carbon dioxide and puffy clouds of water!

q: Steam cracking is one process used in the manufacture of lighter olefins. Which of the following is NOT true of steam cracking?
a: Increasing temperature shifts cracking to the ends of molecules
Short residence times cause more olefin formation
The reaction is favored by high pressure
To minimize coke formation, steam may be added
e: Breaking big molecules into smaller pieces creates a crowd, so squeeze-happy high pressure actually slows the reaction down.

q: When hydrogen reacts with 2-butanone, which of the following is the primary product?
e: Friendly hydrogen snaps onto the middle carbon, turning that ketone into a secondary alcohol hugged by carbon neighbors on both sides.

q: Recycling code 2 indicates which of the following types of plastic?
e: Stamped inside that little number two triangle is high-density polyethylene, the sturdy, trusty plastic that keeps your milk jugs safe!

q: Which choice represents the electron configuration for the magnesium 2+ ion?
e: Magnesium cheerfully tosses away its two outermost electrons, leaving a neat, cozy full house of 1s2 2s2 2p6.

q: Which of the following pairs does NOT correctly match the raw material and feedstock with its primary petrochemical?
e: Propane prefers stretching into flat propylene rather than curling itself up into a tight little ring called cyclopropane.

q: Natural gas systems are the greatest source of U.S. anthropogenic [an-thruh-puh-JEN-ik] methane emissions. What metabolic process, occurring in the rumens of domesticated animals, results in the second-greatest source of methane emissions?
e: Tiny microbes inside a cow's stomach feast on grass through fermentation, happily bubbling up burps full of methane.

q: Consider the covalent bonding in the molecule acetylene [ah-SET-ihl-een], and assume that the carbon-carbon axis is the x-axis. What two orbitals on each carbon atom participate in pi bonding?
e: With the main bond hugging the x-axis, the sideways pi bonds reach out like playful dancing arms using 2py and 2pz.

q: Which of the following molecules is most polar?
e: Sneaky nitrogen pulls electron blankets to its side of the ring, giving pyridine a strong electrical tug that makes it polar.

q: Which of the following molecules is used as a standard for determining the octane rating of gasoline?
e: 2,2,4-trimethylpentane burns so smoothly without angry engine knocking that scientists crowned it the perfect top score for gasoline!

q: A beaker of concentrated aqueous ammonia is placed next to a beaker of concentrated aqueous hydrochloric acid at room temperature. After a short while, a white cloud forms between the beakers. This is a demonstration of:
e: Curious gas particles wander through the open air by diffusion, drifting toward each other until they meet in a smoky high-five.

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the seven crystal lattice systems?
e: Nature loves building crystal boxes with neat tiles, but octagonal shapes leave awkward gaps and simply cannot fit together.

q: Which of the following is the term used to describe the resistance to flow of a liquid:
e: Viscosity is a liquid's sleepy stubbornness, deciding whether it flows like water or creeps slowly like chilled honey.

q: Which of the following statements portrays waxes inaccurately?
a: Waxes help plants eliminate excess water
Paraffin waxes do not contain ester functional groups
Ear wax contains both phospholipids and esters of cholesterol
e: Leafy waxes act like tiny raincoats to trap precious water inside, rather than tossing it away!

q: Silver iodide, or AgI, is LEAST soluble in which of the following aqueous solutions:
e: Because KI is already packed with iodide friends, there is no room left for silver iodide to dissolve and join in.

q: The reaction of hypochlorite and chloride ions in the presence of sulfuric acid generates gaseous chlorine endothermically in a closed vessel. Increasing which of the following would shift the reaction to the left?
e: Raising the pH washes away the sour acid, starving the reaction and politely nudging everything back to the starting side.

q: Which of the following qualitative organic tests is NOT matched correctly to a functional group for which it predominantly tests?
e: Tollens' reagent loves painting a shiny silver mirror for aldehydes, leaving grumpy carboxylic acids completely out of the fun.

q: Which of the following statements best explains why chloroacetic [kloro-ah-SEE-tik] acid is a stronger acid than acetic [ah-SEE-tik] acid?
a: Resonance delocalization of the conjugate base chloroacetate
Withdrawal of electron density by chlorine
Donation of electron density by chlorine
Greater electronegativity of chlorine than oxygen
e: Greedy chlorine pulls electron charge toward itself, steadying the molecule so it can easily set its hydrogen free.

q: Which of the following is least likely to improve the rate of an endothermic reaction involving two gas species reacting on the wall of a vessel?
a: Coating the wall with a catalyst
e: Giving the gases a giant room spreads them far apart, making it much harder for them to bump into the walls.

q: What is the empirical formula for C6H12O6?
e: Dividing each ingredient by six shrinks sugar's big recipe down to its simplest, tidiest building block: CH2O!

q: What is the change in the parent atom atomic number upon alpha particle emission?
e: When an atom tosses out a tiny alpha particle, it loses two protons, making its atomic number drop by two!

q: Which of the following is the formula for n-Octadecanoic acid?
e: This fatty chain needs eighteen carbons in all, so seventeen link up right next to one acid group to make C17H35COOH.

q: The electromotive force is defined as:
a: The maximum electric potential energy stored within a battery
The maximum potential difference between the terminals of a battery
The force that accelerates electrons through a wire when a battery is connected to it
The maximum capacitance between the terminals of a battery
e: Think of it as a battery's total eager push, measured as the biggest possible voltage difference waiting between its two ends.

q: Which of the following compounds is an additive to natural gas that serves as an odorant?
e: Natural gas sneakily has no smell, so we add super smelly tert-butylthiol to warn our noses if anything leaks!

q: You are asked to investigate a gaseous sample that is composed of a variety of different atmospheric gases. Which of the following gas laws could provide information about the relative composition of the gases?
e: Dalton's law shows that every gas pushes with its own pressure, revealing exactly how much of each gas is mingling inside.

q: Kate is performing an experiment where she has a chamber containing an inert gas. The chamber is at a fixed temperature and she varies the pressure of the chamber. She generates a curve by plotting pressure on the x-axis and PV over RT on the y-axis. At which of the following fixed chamber temperatures, in kelvins, would this curve be the MOST linear?
e: At a scorching 1500 Kelvins, gas particles zip by so fast they hardly notice each other, making the line wonderfully straight.

q: Trans fats necessarily contain what functional group?
e: Every trans fat has a bendy double bond between carbon buddies, which makes it an alkene!

q: According to predictions by the Department of Energy, which of the following is closest to the percentage of U.S. gasoline and diesel use that could be replaced using biofuels from agricultural and forestry waste?
e: Leftover farm crops and forest scraps pack enough green power to replace thirty percent of the fuel we use!

q: According to MO [M-oh] theory, which of the following orbitals is the LUMO [LOO-mo] acceptor orbital for the major cycloaddition reaction between butadiene [byoo-tah-DYE-een] and ethylene?
e: Ethylene opens up its empty pi-star room to warmly welcome the incoming electrons during their chemical dance.

q: Based on their bond-dissociation energies, which of the following bonds is strongest?
e: Two nitrogen atoms hug with a mighty triple bond that grips so tightly it takes the most energy to break!

q: One 42-gallon barrel of crude oil produces approximately how many US gallons of gasoline?
e: When refineries cook up a big barrel of dark crude oil, about twenty fresh gallons become gasoline for our cars.

q: An object of mass m sits on a flat table. The Earth pulls on the object with force mg. Which of the following is the corresponding reaction force?
a: The table pushing down on the floor with force mg
The object pushing down on the table with force mg
The object pulling upward on the Earth with force mg
The table pushing up on the object with force mg
e: Gravity is a two-way street, so if Earth pulls down on the object, the object pulls right back up on Earth!

q: Which of the following is the best example of determinate error?
e: A systematic error always sneaks in the same direction with a real cause you can track down and fix.

q: What law states that equal volumes of gases at the same temperature and pressure contain the same number of particles?
e: Avogadro showed that matching balloons at the same warmth and squeeze will always hold the exact same crowd of particles!

q: Which of the following elements CANNOT be a source of fuel in nuclear fusion?
e: Stars easily fuse lighter atoms, but stubborn iron steals energy instead of giving it away, halting the nuclear party cold.

q: Cathode rays are most similar to what type of radiation?
e: Both cathode rays and beta radiation are just lively streams of tiny electrons zooming through space together!

q: Which of the following best describes the Bayer process?
a: Electrolysis of bauxite to produce aluminum
Production of sulfuric acid from hydrogen sulfide
Smelting of copper from copper oxide
e: The Bayer process takes messy red bauxite ore and tidies it up to pull out sparkling pure alumina.

q: Which of the following bonds should have the longest length?
a: C-C (read as: C single bond C)
C=C (read as: C double bond C)
C-H (read as: C single bond H)
CC (read as: C triple bond C)
e: Holding hands with just one single bond lets two carbon atoms stretch farthest apart, making C-C the longest of all!

q: Based on trends in the periodic table, which of the following elements is the least electronegative?
e: Sitting far to the left on the table, gentle beryllium is the least greedy when pulling on shared electrons.

q: To check the accuracy of a graduated cylinder, a student repeatedly filled the cylinder to the 25-milliliter mark using water delivered from a buret and then read the volume delivered. The results of the trials in milliliters were as follows: 1) 26.54, 2) 26.51, 3) 26.60, 4) 26.49, and 5) 26.57. What type of error do these results primarily demonstrate?
e: Since every single measurement landed too high by the exact same amount, a sneaky systematic error was tilting the results.

q: Which of the following compounds is the product of the ozonolysis [oh-zohn-AW-lih-sis] of ethylene followed by a reductive workup?
e: Ozone chops the tiny ethylene molecule right in half, neatly turning both pieces into formaldehyde!

q: Which of the following statements concerning amino acids is NOT true?
a: Glycine is an achiral amino acid
Phenylalanine has a nonpolar side chain
All amino acids are net neutral at a pH of 7
e: Not all amino acid buddies stay neutral in plain water; some carry zippy positive or negative electrical charges!

q: Which of the following statements concerning hydrogen bonding is NOT true?
a: Amines [ah-MEENS] can act as hydrogen bond donors and acceptors
Ethers can form hydrogen bonds with each other
The salicylate [sah-LIH-sil-ate] anion [AN-eye-on] is stabilized by intramolecular hydrogen bonding
Hydrogen sulfide cannot engage in hydrogen bonding
e: Ethers love to mingle, but they cannot hold hands with each other because they lack the special hydrogen hooks needed.

q: A spring consists of a coil of conducting wire, and is initially at equilibrium. A battery is then connected to the spring so that a constant current runs through its wire. Which of the following best describes the resulting behavior of the spring?
e: When electricity zooms through the coils side by side, they attract like tiny magnets and squeeze the spring tight!

q: What is the major potential benefit of electric propulsion systems for the NASA space program?
a: They are lighter than traditional fuels
They are less toxic than traditional fuels
They contribute to an artificial gravity environment
They require less research and development
e: Electric thrusters pack super light, using far less heavy fuel so spacecraft can drift through the stars without extra baggage!

q: Which of the following is NOT an endothermic process:
e: When steamy gas snuggles into cozy liquid drops, it happily gives away warmth instead of soaking it in.

q: Which of the following experimental batteries is able to charge in less than a minute?
e: Aluminum ion batteries are speedy little wonders, gulping down a full charge in under a minute!

q: Sodium azide and potassium nitrate react to inflate an airbag during a car crash primarily by producing which of the following gases?
e: Chemicals instantly release a huge rush of nitrogen gas, puffing the cushion up like a giant balloon to protect you!

q: The titration of a weak base, 0.100 molar NaCN, with a strong acid, 0.100 molar HCl, results in a solution at the equivalence point having a pH of:
e: When the strong acid finishes wrestling the weak base, leftover acidic parts keep the final mix gently sour, between four and seven.

q: Which of the following compounds is INSOLUBLE in water?
e: While other salts love swimming, copper(I) chloride hugs itself tightly and stubbornly refuses to dissolve in water.

q: Which of the following solutions or substances will have the highest vapor pressure at room temperature?
a: Water with 0.1 mole fraction sodium chloride
e: Ethanol molecules are restless little jumpers, easily escaping into the air to create the highest vapor pressure of all!

q: According to a study at Argonne National Laboratories, what is the net energy gain or loss, expressed as a ratio, from producing a gallon of ethanol from corn?
e: Corn gives back more than it takes, handing us 1.3 times the energy it took to grow and brew!

q: Which of the following metals will not readily react with cold water to generate hydrogen gas and the corresponding metal hydroxide due to the existence of a nonreactive metal oxide layer coating the metal?
e: Aluminum wears an invisible oxide coat of armor, which shields it from reacting with chilly water.

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true about gasoline?
a: The octane rating of gasoline tells you how much the fuel can be compressed before it spontaneously ignites
When gasoline is burned under ideal conditions, its products are carbon dioxide, water, and heat
The overall efficiency of an automotive gasoline engine is about 80%
e: Car engines lose so much heat to the air that reaching eighty percent efficiency is far beyond what they can actually do.

q: Which of the following elements has the largest second ionization energy:
e: Once lithium gives away one electron, it hugs its tiny inner shell so tightly that stealing another takes enormous energy!

q: A student wishes to convert an aldehyde to a secondary alcohol. Which of the following reagents would be most useful?
e: A Grignard reagent brings a new carbon friend to join the aldehyde, cleverly building it up into a secondary alcohol!

q: Which of the following molecules has a permanent dipole moment?
e: Hydrogen sulfide is bent and lopsided, pulling its electric charges unevenly to create a permanent dipole tug-of-war.

q: Which of the following is used to measure the decay time for an unstable isotope?
e: A half-life is the trusty timer showing how long it takes for half of those restless atoms to quietly transform.

q: With respect to magnesium and oxygen, respectively, how do the radii of the constituent ions compare to the corresponding neutral atoms?
e: Magnesium shrinks when it tosses out electrons, while oxygen puffs up bigger like an inflated balloon after grabbing extras.

q: The standard heat of formation of hydrogen gas in the form H2 is:
a: Determined by checking a table of the Standard Heats of Formation
e: Hydrogen gas is already resting in its favorite natural form, so it takes zero extra energy to build it from scratch!

q: What is the name for a chemical bond that involves sharing the electrons between two non-metals?
e: Like two best friends sharing a warm scarf on a chilly day, atoms in a covalent bond share their electrons to stick together.

q: Which of the following is the strongest reducing agent yielding the most ATP per molecule during oxidative phosphorylation?
e: Tiny NADH acts like a supercharged delivery truck packed with energy, dropping off electrons to build the most ATP power.

q: You take an IR [I-R] spectrum that has a long, broad peak just below 3000 inverse centimeters. Which of the following is the likely identification of the molecule?

q: Which of the following is the name of the compound HClO4?

q: Which of the following BEST describes the Balmer series:
a: a series of quantum numbers indicating certain energy levels
a sequence of elements that are produced chronologically in supernovae
the energy spectrum of the early universe
e: Whenever a hydrogen atom gets excited and hops down energy levels, it sings out a glowing rainbow called the Balmer series.

q: Which of the following is an element that is very important to human life, is contained in vitamin B-12, belongs to a group of transition metals, and has magnetic properties like iron:
e: Cobalt is a busy little metal that loves magnets and sits proudly at the very heart of vitamin B-12 to keep you healthy!

q: Which of the following is NOT a real element?
e: Vitrainium sounds like an awesome superpower metal, but someone completely made it up, so you will never find it in the real universe.

q: What are the products for the complete combustion of methane?
e: When methane burns completely, it dances with oxygen to turn into friendly puffs of carbon dioxide and water vapor.

q: Which of the following is NOT a method to separate two liquids?
e: Sonication just tickles liquids with sound waves to shake them up, which mixes them instead of pulling them apart!

q: Which of the following is NOT an aliphatic hydrocarbon?
e: Benzene is an aromatic ring with its own special electron circle, making it far too fancy to be called aliphatic.

q: Which of the following statements is the best explanation for why the atomic radius decreases across a period to the right?
a: Increase in ionization [eye-on-ih-ZAY-shun] energy at the valence [VAY-lence] shell
Increase in effective nuclear charge at the valence shell
Increase in atomic polarizability [POH-lah-rize-ah-BIL-itee] at the valence shell
Increase in electron affinity at the valence [VAY-lence] shell
e: As the nucleus gains more protons, it hugs its outer electrons with stronger positive power, pulling them in closer.

q: Steven plots temperature versus time as he heats water while adding energy at a constant rate. Which of the following statements best explains why the heating curve reaches a plateau at 100 degrees Celsius?
a: Energy is required to decrease the entropy [EN-troh-pee] of the water
Energy is required to decrease the enthalpy [EN-thul-pee] of the water
Energy is required to break the hydrogen-oxygen bonds in water
Energy is required to break the hydrogen bonds between water molecules
e: Water pauses at boiling because all that heat is busy breaking the sticky hydrogen bonds holding the molecules together.

q: Which of the following organic functional groups does NOT exhibit sp2 [s-p-2] hybridization?

q: An organic compound with the formula C6H14 is an:
e: With fourteen hydrogens snugly hugging six carbons, this happy molecule matches the CnH2n+2 recipe for an alkane.

q: What signs for enthalpy and entropy changes, respectively, guarantee a spontaneous reaction at all temperatures?
e: Negative enthalpy releases heat while positive entropy creates messy disorder, guaranteeing a reaction happens anytime!

q: Pyrex glassware contains silicon dioxide, which has acidic properties and should not be used to store which of the following?

q: Scientists at Pacific Northwest National Lab are developing sodium-ion batteries. Which of the following best explains why graphite is not used as the anode in these batteries?
a: Graphite is used as the cathode
Graphite is dissolved by the electrolytes used in these batteries
Graphite has significant reactivity to sodium ions
Graphite cannot store appreciable amounts of sodium ions

q: Which of the following would be LEAST applicable for determining the end point in a titration experiment:

q: Which of the following best describes the role of ammonia in the gas-phase reaction of ammonia with boron trichloride?
e: Generous ammonia shares its spare pair of electrons with hungry boron, making it a classic Lewis base.

q: Maple tree sap has a density of 1.010 grams per centimeter cubed and is approximately 3.0% sucrose by mass in water. What is the molarity of sucrose in sap?
e: In every liter of sweet sap, thirty grams of sugar are hiding, which works out to just 0.089 moles of sweetness!

q: If an astronomer photographed a massive cloud of ionized hydrogen in space that was emitting all of the Balmer wavelengths, what color would it typically appear to us:
e: When glowing hydrogen mixes bright red light with a dash of blue, it paints these dreamy space clouds a cozy shade of pink.

q: The molal (read as: moe-lahl) is a concentration unit that is most appropriately used in experimental designs that determine:
e: Molality measures weight instead of volume, so temperature changes cannot fool it while watching chilly liquids freeze solid.

q: A student is holding two balloons, one containing one mole of hydrogen gas and the other containing one mole of helium gas. What is the ratio of the volume of the helium balloon to that of the hydrogen balloon?
e: Any gas with the same number of bustling little molecules puffs out its balloon to the exact same size, giving a ratio of one.

q: A protein chemist isolates a new enzyme. Which of the following techniques, when performed alone, would be most useful for determining its size?
e: MALDI-TOF gently launches the whole enzyme into the air, clocking its flight time to weigh exactly how big it is.

q: Which of the following chlorides is least soluble?
e: While other chlorides happily dissolve into water, stubborn lead chloride clings together tightly and refuses to break apart.

q: What are the two conditions that distinguish bioluminescence from chemiluminescence (read as: keh-mee-luh-mi-NEH-sehns)?
a: Bioluminescence occurs in living organisms and has hydrogen as a common reactant
Bioluminescence occurs in living organisms and requires an enzyme catalyst
Bioluminescence occurs in living organisms and involves the emission of light at a lower energy than chemiluminescence (read as: keh-mee-luh-mi-NEH-sehns)
Bioluminescence occurs uniquely in living organisms and has oxygen as a common reactant
e: Bioluminescence happens inside living creatures using special helper enzymes to craft their magical glow, unlike simple glow sticks.

q: Which of the following are the units of the rate constant for a 2nd order reaction given that concentration is measured in molarity and time in seconds:
e: With two molecules crashing together each second, the speed formula balances out neatly to give units of M-1s-1.

q: Macrophages use NADPH oxidase to generate what chemical, which is then used to destroy invading bacteria?
e: Defender cells whip up super-charged superoxide ions like tiny shields to zap away pesky invading bacteria.

q: What additional piece of information can be used in conjunction with an elemental analysis to determine the chemical formula of an unknown pure substance?
a: The chemical formula can be directly calculated from the elemental analysis
The retention time on a chromatography column
e: Elemental analysis gives the recipe's ingredients, but mass spectrometry weighs the whole package to reveal the true chemical formula.

q: Ames Lab researchers are studying quantum phase transitions in materials where the magnetic moments of each molecule point in the opposite direction as each of their neighbors'. Which of the following terms describes this type of magnetism?
e: In antiferromagnetism, neighboring magnetic particles politely take turns pointing in opposite directions, like dancers facing away from each other.

q: Department of Energy and Argonne National Lab researchers have recently found that termolecular [ter-mo-lecular] reactions may play a significant role in a number of processes. Why had chemists previously considered termolecular reactions to be insignificant?
a: Termolecular reactions have high changes in entropy
Termolecular reactions are forbidden by the Woodward-Hoffmann rules
Termolecular reactions are statistically unlikely to occur
e: It is statistically so unlikely for three wandering molecules to crash together at the exact same instant that chemists ignored them.

q: Which of the following conditions is NOT required to form coal?
a: A stagnant and stable water level
Heat and pressure over a long period of time
An equal supply of both vegetation and sediment
A plant accumulation rate equaling land subsidence rate
e: Coal needs heaps of ancient buried swamp plants, not a half-and-half mix of plants and mud, to bake into fuel.

q: Boyle's gas law concerns which of the following two variables:
e: Boyle's law shows that squishing a gas into a smaller volume makes its pressure push back even harder.

q: In which of the following scattering angles is Rayleigh [RAY- lee] scattering from unpolarized light the most intense?
e: At a ninety-degree angle, light beams scatter off particles sideways at the sweet spot where their glow shines brightest.

q: An aqueous solution in which the concentration of OH- ions is greater than that of H+ ions is:
e: When hydroxide ions outnumber hydrogen ions in the pool, the whole solution happily turns basic.

q: M2+ is a metal ion with a ground state electron configuration of [Ar]3d84s0 [argon-3-d-8-4-s-0]. What is the identity of M?
e: Giving this metal ion back its two lost electrons brings its total to twenty-eight, revealing it was nickel all along.

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true regarding alkaline earth metals?
a: Calcium burns brick-red in a flame test
Magnesium has no naturally occurring radioisotopes
Radium is found in all uranium-bearing ores
e: Radium is always busily buzzing with radioactivity, meaning it has zero stable isotopes instead of three.

q: Which of the following compounds has the lowest solubility product constant at pH 7?
e: Among these salts, iron two chloride clings together most stubbornly in water, giving it the lowest solubility product constant.

q: Which of the following statements is true regarding a gas-phase reaction at chemical equilibrium?
a: The forward and reverse reactions stop at equilibrium
Adding reactant will increase the concentration of product
Adding reactant will increase the equilibrium constant
The reverse reaction only begins at equilibrium
e: Tossing extra reactants into the mix nudges the balanced system forward to craft even more product.

q: Which of the following statements concerning chemical kinetics is NOT true?
a: Catalysts of a reaction can appear in the reaction's rate law
The reciprocal of concentration versus time will be linear for a first order reaction
For a reaction, the equilibrium constant is the forward rate constant over the reverse rate constant
The half-life of a zero-th order reaction is proportional to initial concentration of the reactant
e: Plotting one over concentration only draws a straight line for second-order reactions, not first-order ones, making that statement false.

q: One proposed solution for carbon capture is to use the reaction of calcium oxide with carbon dioxide to form calcium carbonate. Which of the following is true regarding this process?
a: This reaction requires large quantities of thermal energy to proceed
Increasing the amount of carbon dioxide while holding the calcium oxide amount constant will always increase the amount of calcium carbonate produced
This reaction is spontaneous at low temperatures
e: When things chill out at cool temperatures, these friendly molecules gladly snuggle together all on their own without needing heat.

q: Which of the following molecules contains carbon-carbon bonds with the most s-character?
e: Ethyne holds its carbon atoms in a tight triple hug, packing in the most round, bouncy s-shaped energy.

q: Which of the following statements is true regarding the energetics of electrochemical cells?
a: For a voltaic cell, E-cell is positive and delta G is positive
For a voltaic cell, E-cell is positive and delta G is negative
For an electrolytic cell, E-cell is negative and delta G is negative
For an electrolytic cell, E-cell is positive and delta G is negative
e: Like an eager little battery, this cell naturally flows forward, creating positive voltage while happily spending its free energy.

q: Which of the following assumptions is not valid under the kinetic theory of gases?
a: Molecules move with the same speed at a given temperature
Outside of collisions, molecules do not exert forces on each other
e: Gas particles are like bouncy bumper cars, zooming at all sorts of different speeds instead of sharing just one pace.

q: FutureGen 2.0 power plants will reduce carbon dioxide production by burning coal in which of the following ways?
a: With a mixture of oxygen and carbon dioxide instead of air to produce concentrated carbon dioxide
With an enhanced concentration of oxygen instead of air to produce less carbon dioxide per ton of coal burned
In a catalytic chamber that scrubs the carbon dioxide out of the emissions
Using carbon dioxide reduced coal in an 80% nitrogen and 18% oxygen mixture
e: By burning fuel with pure oxygen and carbon dioxide, the plant neatly captures thick, concentrated fumes instead of messy air.

q: Which of the following molecules is NOT matched correctly to its central atom hybridization?
e: Phosphorus pentachloride only holds five chlorine pals, meaning it needs five blended atomic rooms, not the six in d2sp3.

q: Polycatenane [pol-ee-KAT-n-ayn] and polyrotaxane [pol-ee- ro-TUH-ksayn] are examples of what type of unconventional polymer?
e: Like magicians interlocking solid rings without glue, these supramolecular wonders hold together through clever mechanical teamwork.

q: Which of the following solutions, when mixed one-to-one, will exhibit the smallest deviation from Raoult's [rah-oolt's] law?
e: Pentane and hexane are so alike they mix like twin raindrops, following Raoult's law almost perfectly.

q: Nanticoke Generating Station, located in southern Ontario, Canada, is one of the world's largest coal-burning power plants. However, the Canadian Ministry of Energy announced in 2010 that Nanticoke would convert some of their generators to use which of the following types of fuel instead of coal?
e: The giant plant traded dusty, heavy coal for cleaner natural gas, giving the Canadian skies a much fresher breath.

q: You are studying a material that has started to undergo thermal fatigue. Which of the following would be a good action to take to reduce this fatigue?
e: When changing heat pushes metal to its breaking point, designing away the heavy strain keeps it happy and whole.

q: Researchers at Lawrence Berkeley National Lab are currently working on optimizing plants to produce less lignin. For which of the following are these genetically modified plants likely to be used?
e: Tough plant walls act like stubborn wooden armor, so softening that lignin lets us easily brew sweet ethanol fuel.

q: Group 1 cations and group 7 anions combine to form:
e: When energetic alkali metals hug salty halogen friends, they snap together into sparkling alkali halide crystals.

q: A nitrogen atom present in the backbone of a polypeptide [pol-ee-PEP-tyd] is part of which of the following functional groups?
e: Inside a protein chain, nitrogen holds hands with a carbon right beside an oxygen, building a sturdy amide link.

q: Researchers at the Joint Genome [JEE-nome] Institute have been using new types of fungi [fun-ji] to produce biofuels from plant material. Where are these fungi naturally found?
e: These hungry little fungi live cozy inside animal tummies, happily helping creatures digest tough plant grass into fuel.

q: Atom A possesses atomic orbitals that are slightly lower in energy than those of atom B. Which of the following is true of a bond between atoms A and B?
e: Because atom A pulls tighter with its lower energy, the shared electrons lean over, creating a polar covalent bond.

q: Which of the following best describes why Neptune is blue?

Absorption of light by methane in its atmosphere
