a: Coal is formed when dead plant matter is converted to peat, then lignite
China produces the most coal worldwide
Natural gas releases more carbon dioxide per kilowatt-hour than coal
Anthracite can be converted to graphite under high pressure and temperature
e: Natural gas is actually cleaner, puffing out way less carbon dioxide than coal when making the same power.

q: The intensity of absorption maxima in a visible spectrum depends upon which of the following characteristics?
a: Electron configuration of the metal center
e: When quantum rules allow jumping electrons to make their big leap, light is soaked up with dazzling, bold intensity.

q: Which of the following is a type of colloid that is classified as a sol at room temperature:
e: Gelatin loves swimming as tiny solid bits floating freely inside water, making it a classic liquid sol.

q: Fats and oils contain what functional group?
e: Fats and oils are built using cozy chemical bridges called ester groups, linking their long tails together.

q: Which of the following statements regarding reaction intermediates is true?
a: There is precisely one reaction intermediate in a one step reaction
Reaction intermediates are local minima on the reaction coordinate scheme
Reaction intermediates are synonymous with activated complexes
The concentrations of reaction intermediates cannot influence reaction rate
e: Like a tired hiker resting in a valley, an intermediate pauses at a cozy low dip on the energy map.

q: Consider a reaction that has a negative enthalpy of reaction, and a positive change in entropy. Under what conditions will the reaction occur spontaneously?
e: Releasing heat while creating joyful chaos gives this reaction a green light to happen at any temperature!

q: Iron minerals can be subdivided into different categories based on their gangue [GANG] content. Into which of the following categories would you place a mineral that is made up primarily of aluminum oxide?
e: Aluminum oxide acts like a tangy acid gangue, needing basic rocks to help wash it away.

q: Plug-in hybrid electric vehicles are:
a: Powered by electricity until batteries are discharged and then powered by gasoline
e: These clever cars zip quietly on battery power first, then wake their gas engine once the battery gets sleepy.

q: Which of the following is considered a weak acid:
e: Formic acid is shy and clings tightly to its hydrogens, only letting a tiny few wander off into water.

q: Which of the following is the most plausible first step in the solvolysis [sawl-VAWL- eh-sis] of tert-butyl [turt-BYU-til] iodide in water?
a: Attack of water to form a pentavalent [penta-VAY-lent] intermediate
e: The iodide buddy pops right off first, leaving behind an eager, positively charged carbon friend ready to meet water.

q: The polymerization of a 1,3 diene [DY-een] will produce a material that can be used to make which of the following polymers?
e: When these bouncy molecules link hands, they create stretchy rubber that loves to flex and snap right back!

q: Which of the following bonds is the longest in length?
e: Big, chubby iodine atoms take up lots of space, so holding hands makes the longest bond of all!

q: The functional groups forming a peptide bond do NOT contain which of the following atoms?
e: Peptide bonds link carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, and hydrogen, leaving phosphorus completely out of their cozy little club.

q: Which of the following indicators would be most useful for a strong base-strong acid titration [tie-TRAY-shun]?
e: Strong acids and bases balance out right near neutral seven, exactly where phenol red magically switches its color!

q: In the equation for the Gibbs free energy change, if H (read as: delta H) is positive and S (read as: delta S) is positive, then the reactions are:
e: This reaction needs lots of heat energy so its wild, messy entropy can finally win the day.

q: Which of the following factors does NOT affect the solubility of a solid in a liquid?
e: Squeezing down with extra pressure does not bother solids, since they are already packed together super tightly.

q: Which of the following is the molecular orbital theory prediction for the bond order of the dioxygenyl radical cation, whose chemical formula is O2+?
e: Losing one troublesome electron actually tightens their hug, giving these two oxygen atoms a stronger bond order of 2.5!

q: New computer simulations at Princeton Plasma Physics Lab have shown that adding a porous layer around a reservoir of liquid lithium could aid in heat absorption and transfer in a nuclear fusion reactor. This system could potentially be deployed in what toroidal [tore-OY-dul] device?
e: A tokamak is a giant magnetic donut that traps blazing starfire, making it the perfect home for liquid lithium.

q: Which of the following does NOT have an index of hydrogen deficiency of 3?
e: Spiropentane is just two joined rings with no double bonds, giving it a missing hydrogen count of only two.

q: Which of the following gases is NOT one of the major causes of the greenhouse effect?
e: Carbon monoxide does not trap heat directly like its famous cousin carbon dioxide, so it is not a major greenhouse gas.

q: The further advancement of rechargeable batteries is currently hindered by unavoidable growth of what during battery cell recharge?
e: Tiny spikes called lithium dendrites sprout like mischievous weeds inside recharging batteries, poking parts they shouldn't.

q: Which of the following is NOT true of glucose:
a: when glucose joins with galactose, fructose is formed
cellulose is a polymer of glucose molecules
e: When glucose buddies up with galactose, they actually make milky lactose, not fructose!

q: The degree of unsaturation of a hydrocarbon containing two rings is equivalent to the degree of unsaturation of a hydrocarbon containing an:
e: Tying two molecular rings together locks away two pairs of hydrogens, just like the strong triple bond of an alkyne!

q: Which of the following statements is true of the compression of a system?
a: Work is done on the system, and dV and dw are greater than 0
Work is done on the system, dV is less than 0, and dw is greater than 0
Work is done by the system, dV is greater than 0, and dw is less than 0
Work is done by the system, and dV and dw are less than 0
e: Squishing a gas puts work into it, so work is positive while the shrinking space is negative.

q: Three metals, A, B, and C, have reduction potentials of their +2 cations such that A has the greatest reduction potential and C has the least. Which of the following is true?
e: Metal C gives away its electrons easiest, happily passing them over to reduce B's ions!

q: What biological carbon sequestration method uses iron and requires a better understanding of iron cycling in marine systems to determine its long-term impacts?
e: Iron fertilization feeds hungry ocean algae tiny iron snacks so they grow big and trap carbon.

q: Which of the following ligands induces the largest electronic d orbital splitting in a transition metal complex?
e: The mighty cyano group pushes hardest on a metal's electron cloud, splitting its energy levels the widest.

q: Which of the following is a substance that is very reactive with the oxygen in air and must be stored under water or some other substance to keep it from becoming incendiary:
e: White phosphorus gets so excited around oxygen that it bursts into flame, so it hides safely underwater!

q: The rate-limiting step for a reaction involving Reactant X is X + X yields Y, where Y is a product. Which of the following quantities plotted against time would produce a straight line?
a: Natural log of the molarity of X
e: Because two X molecules collide, graphing one over the amount of X draws a beautifully straight line.

q: Given R = 1.097 107 inverse meters, which of the following represents the wavelength of the longest wavelength Lyman line of the hydrogen spectrum in meters and the region of the electromagnetic spectrum in which it lies?
e: Hydrogen drops down, shooting out an ultraviolet light beam measuring 1.22 times ten to the minus seven meters.

q: At the DOE's Advanced Photon Source, researchers are studying industrial catalysts used in petrochemical processing. Which of the following correctly describes most of these catalysts?
e: These solid mineral helpers work without dissolving into the liquids, making them heterogeneous inorganic catalysts.

q: What is the process by which nuclear fission produces energy?
a: Combining lighter nuclei into heavier nuclei
Increasing the number of protons a nucleus contains
Changing an electron's spin state following excitation
Splitting heavier nuclei into lighter nuclei
e: Nuclear fission cracks a heavy atom's center into smaller pieces, releasing an enormous pop of energy!

q: Of the following 1.0 molar solutions, which will have the highest pH?
e: Hydrocyanic acid is the gentlest, weakest acid of the bunch, so it keeps the highest pH.

q: Some compounds feature two-atom covalent [koh-VAY-lent] bonds in which both electrons forming the bond are donated by one of the atoms, also known as a dative bond. Which of the following bonds is most likely to be a dative bond?
e: Generous nitrogen shares both of its own electrons with hungry boron to form a friendly dative bond.

q: 10 milliliters of a 0.1 molar solution of which of the following substances added to 10 milliliters of a 0.1 molar acetic acid solution will form a buffer solution?
e: Acetic acid pairs with potassium acetate, its special partner, to make a buffer that tames acids.

q: The precipitation reaction caused by the addition of potassium chloride to aqueous [AY-kwee-us] silver nitrate is an example of which of the following types of reactions?
e: Potassium and silver politely swap dance partners, making a metathesis reaction that leaves a solid behind.

q: Which of the following best describes the catalyst in the destruction of ozone by chlorofluorocarbons:
e: The chlorine catalyst and ozone float together as gases in the air, making the reaction homogeneous!

q: According to VSEPR bonding theory, if 2 of the bonded atoms in an octahedral molecule are replaced by 2 electron pairs, the molecule will assume what geometric shape, such as in XeF4:
e: Two electron pairs push to opposite sides, flattening the other four atoms into a square planar shape.

q: Transition metal elements have atoms or ions with which of the following orbitals partially filled?
e: Transition metals are special because their energetic d orbitals are only partially filled with electrons.

q: The Michaelis-Menten assumptions are integral to understanding the kinetics of enzyme-based reactions. Which of the following is NOT one of these assumptions?
a: Substrate is present in slightly greater quantities than the enzyme
In a steady state, the concentration of the intermediate is always constant
Rate is highest when enzyme catalytic sites are saturated with substrate
The reaction between the substrate and the enzyme is reversible
e: Enzymes need a giant flood of molecules, not just slightly more, so that assumption is wrong!

q: If an electron in a hydrogen atom decays to emit a photon, which of the following transitions emits the longest wavelength photon?
a: First excited state to ground state
Second excited state to ground state
Second excited state to first excited state
Third excited state to first excited state
e: Taking a tiny hop from the third step down to the second releases the gentlest energy, creating light with the longest, laziest wave.

q: Scientists at Lawrence Berkeley National Lab are studying how plant leaves emit a single-carbon alcohol. What is the name of this alcohol?
e: In chemistry, the prefix 'meth' always means a single carbon atom, making methanol the little alcohol leaves whisper into the air.

q: Which of the following is false regarding the reaction A(g) + B(s) C(s)? (READ IS: A gaseous plus B solid yields C solid)
a: As pressure decreases, reaction rate decreases
As temperature increases, reaction rate increases
As surface area increases, reaction rate decreases
When a catalyst is added, reaction rate increases
e: Spreading a solid out gives it more room to bump and react, which actually speeds things up instead of slowing them down!

q: Which of the following is the strongest acid?
e: Giant iodine holds its little hydrogen so loosely that hydroiodic acid lets it go quickest, making it the strongest acid around.

q: Which of the following is true about the alpha particle?
a: It was discovered by J.J. Thomson
It was used by Ernest Rutherford in experiments relating to the nucleus of the atom
e: Rutherford shot these energetic particles at thin gold foil and was amazed to discover the atom's dense little nucleus at the center!

q: A former Russian service officer died in November 2006 after being diagnosed with acute radiation syndrome. During the investigation into his death, authorities were able to trace his activities, in part, because his body had excreted trace amounts of which of the following radioactive isotopes, which he had recently ingested?
a: Polonium-210 with a half-life of 138 days
Bismuth-213 with a half-life of 45 minutes
Technetium-99 with a half-life of 6 hours
Uranium-238 with half-life of 4.5 billion years
e: Dangerous polonium-210 decays steadily over months, leaving behind a glowing trail of tiny clues that investigators could easily track down.

q: Which of the following neutral ground state atoms has the lowest ionization energy?
e: Boron has just one lone electron in its outer shell, so it lets go of it with the least amount of energy.

q: Which of the following matches the molecular formula of a cyclic alkane [AL-kayn]?
e: To hold hands in a closed ring, five carbons must let go of two hydrogens, leaving exactly ten loyal hydrogen friends.

q: Which of the following is NOT true when writing electron configurations?
a: Atomic orbitals can accommodate two electrons
Electrons pair in degenerate orbitals when possible
Electrons will populate orbitals to maximize spin
Noble gas cores are often used to truncate longer configurations
e: Like grumpy siblings, electrons prefer having their own empty rooms first and never pair up until every open space is filled!

q: At a given temperature, which of the following molecules will have the greatest route mean square speed?
e: Being the lightest featherweight of the group, nitrogen zips and zooms across the room faster than its heavier gas friends.

q: Which of the following salt solutions, all at 1.0 molar concentration, will have a pH value less than 7:
e: Born from a strong acid and a gentle base, ammonium chloride leaves water slightly sour, tipping the pH balance below seven.

q: When performing distillation, which of the following substances would be expected to be collected last based on boiling point?
e: Pentanoic acid clings to its neighbors with extra-strong bonds, stubbornly refusing to boil until all the other liquids have floated away.

q: Which of the following stellar reactions releases the most energy?
e: Squishing tiny hydrogen atoms into shiny new helium releases the most dazzling, powerful burst of energy in a star's furnace!

q: When assigning electrons to subshells, which of the following subshells will be filled first?
e: The 5s orbital requires the least climbing energy, so eager electrons happily move into that cozy room first.

q: Which of the following ions has the smallest radius?
e: With thirteen mighty protons pulling on ten electrons, aluminum hugs its cloud the tightest, shrinking into the smallest size of all!

q: If an acid is added to an unbuffered, neutral aqueous solution, which of the following is true?
a: The concentrations of the hydronium and hydroxide ion concentrations remain unchanged
e: When fresh acid rushes in, it eagerly snaps up hydroxide ions, leaving far fewer of them floating around in the water.

q: Which of the following is not one of the characteristics of indirect coulometry [koo-LOM-i-tree]?
a: Utilizes a constant current source and both indicating and generating electrodes
Requires the use of standards even if the current efficiency is known
e: Because this clever method directly counts moving electrical charges, scientists never need outside reference standards to measure their samples.

q: In which of the following sets of elements would all members be expected to have very similar chemical properties?
e: Living in the very same family column, magnesium, calcium, and barium act like friendly siblings with matching chemical personalities!

q: Which of the following would be the resulting pH from the reaction of equal amounts of a strong acid with a strong base?
a: The reaction is independent of the pH
e: When equally strong acids and bases clash, they completely cancel each other out, leaving peaceful neutral water sitting right at seven.

q: Which of the following is the theoretical end of a titration:
e: The equivalence point is that perfectly balanced, ideal moment where the acid and base have matched up in exact chemical harmony.

q: A pure element when mixed with an ionic compound is most likely to undergo which of the following kinds of reactions?
e: Like a bold dancer cutting in on a happy pair, the lone element steps in and swaps places in a single replacement!

q: Which of the following would be most likely to undergo an SN1, reaction?
e: Tert-butyl chloride has three carbon friends crowding around, keeping it cozy and stable so it can easily do an SN1 reaction!

q: Department of Energy-supported scientists are using DNA as a molecular wire to transport electrons between organic molecules. What specific moieties [MOY-eh-teez] in the DNA exchange the electrons in these reactions?
e: Nucleobases stack together like flat stepping stones in a twisted ladder, letting tiny electrons skip happily from step to step!

q: For the molecular orbital diagram of H2, in which of the following locations are the electrons located?
a: One electron in each hydrogen's 1s atomic orbital
Both electrons in the sigma 1s orbital
Both electrons in the sigma* [sigma-star] 1s orbital
Both electrons in the pi 1s orbital
e: When two hydrogen atoms hug, both of their electrons snuggle happily into the low-energy sigma 1s bonding orbital together!

q: Which of the following is NOT an aromatic amino acid:
e: While the other amino acids wear fancy circular chemical rings like little hula hoops, friendly glutamine doesn't have one!

q: In a proton NMR spectrum, a proton associated with which of the following carbon atoms would be predicted to have the largest chemical shift?
e: The greedy oxygen on a carbonyl pulls electron blankets away, leaving its neighbor proton bare and showing off the biggest chemical shift!

q: The oxidation of elemental lithium with which of the following is a redox reaction that is MOST favorable?
e: Lithium loves giving away electrons, and greedy fluorine gas snatches them up faster and stronger than anyone else!

q: In order to calculate the heat of fusion for a piece of ice placed in warm water, you must know:
a: The energy released by the warm water and the mass of the water
The energy released by the warm water and the mass of the ice
The energy released by the ice and the mass of the warm water
The energy released by the ice and the mass of ice
e: You must see how much energy the warm water gives away and weigh the ice that soaks it up to melt!

q: Which of the following do NOT have liquid crystals as a possible component?
e: Stalactites are just solid rocky icicles hanging in dark caves, with no flowing liquid crystals inside them at all!

q: What is the most likely type of interaction between the side chains of the amino acids leucine [LOO-seen] and phenylalanine [Fennel-AL-ah-neen]?
e: Both of these amino acids are shy around water, so they huddle together in a cozy hydrophobic hug!

q: What is the difference between heat and temperature?
a: Temperature is a form of heat, while heat is a measurement
Temperature is a measurement of molecular kinetic energy, while heat is a form of energy
Heat and temperature have different wavelengths
Heat and temperature have similar wavelengths but different amplitudes
e: Heat is the actual energy on the move, while temperature is just a thermometer measuring how fast tiny molecules wiggle!

q: Which of the following carboxylic [CAR-box-IHL-ik] acid derivatives would be most reactive with a nucleophile [NU-klee-oh-file]?
e: Acid chlorides have a chloride friend ready to leave in a flash, making them react faster than all the rest!

q: What element on the periodic table has 92 electrons?
e: Mighty uranium is a true giant, surrounded by a swirling cloud of ninety-two busy electrons buzzing around its core.

q: Consider the dissociation of weak hydrofluoric acid into fluoride and hydronium ions, and a solution in which this reaction is at equilibrium [ee-kwuh-LIB-ree- uhm]. Which of the following additions would shift the equilibrium to the right?
e: Ammonia acts like a hungry guest eating up acid ions, pulling the reaction to the right to make more!

q: A chemist adds ethylenediamine [eh-thil-een-DYE-ah-meen], methylamine, and EDTA to an aqueous [AY-kwee-us] solution of cadmium (II). Which of the following ligands [LIH-gundz] will form the most stable complex in this solution?
e: EDTA wraps around cadmium like an octopus with six grippy arms, locking it into the most stable hug possible!

q: According to Boyle's Law, the volume of a gas is linearly related to what quantity?
e: As you squeeze a gas, volume shrinks, making it line up straight and neat with one over pressure!

q: Which of the following is true concerning a chemical system at a state of dynamic equilibrium?
a: Forward and reverse rate constants are both equal to one
Change in enthalpy for the reaction at standard state is zero
Change in Gibbs free energy is zero
Molar entropy of products minus molar entropy of reactants is zero
e: Forward and backward reactions balance out like a perfect seesaw, so the change in Gibbs free energy settles at zero!

q: Which of the following alkali metals has the most negative standard reduction potential?
e: Cesium has a giant, fluffy electron cloud that gives away its electron so easily that it resists reduction the most!

q: Which of the following electrons would be most effective at shielding the nuclear charge seen by a 3s electron in an aluminum atom?
e: 1s electrons hug closest to the center, blocking the positive nuclear pull like a sturdy front-row shield!

q: Lithium dialkylcuprates [dy-AL-kuh-KUHP-rayts] can be used in carbon-carbon bond-forming reactions and are usually known as what named reagent?
e: Chemists nickname these clever copper helpers Gilman reagents after the scientist who showed how they glue carbons together!

q: Sherry is performing elemental analysis on a compound she knows is composed of only hydrogen and oxygen. She finds that the compound is 5.9% hydrogen by mass. Which of the following might be the identity of the compound?
e: With two heavy oxygen buddies outweighing two tiny hydrogens, hydrogen peroxide leaves hydrogen holding just under six percent of the team's weight.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the kinetic molecular theory of ideal gases is TRUE:
a: the average kinetic energy of gaseous molecules is directly proportional to the absolute temperature of the sample
the volume occupied by the atoms and/or molecules in a gas is large
collisions between gas particles are both elastic and inelastic
between collisions, molecules exert both attractive and repulsive forces on each other
e: When gas particles warm up, they zoom and dance much faster, because higher temperature directly boosts their average movement energy!

q: Two solutions are made with equal molarity: one contains sucrose dissolved in water, while the other contains an unknown salt dissolved in water. The freezing point of the sucrose solution is found to be -0.75 Celsius, and the freezing point of the unknown salt solution is -2.2 Celsius. Which of the following is the most likely chemical formula of the salt?
e: Calcium chloride splits into three busy little ions, dropping the freezing point three times as much as lonely, unbroken sugar!

q: If an organo-magnesium compound is reacted with formaldehyde [foor-MAL-dih-hide], which of the following will be formed?
e: Formaldehyde has only one carbon with room on the end, so this friendly reaction builds a neat primary alcohol!

q: Which of the following expresses a challenge or challenges facing the use of hydrogen technology in vehicles?
a: The technology required to carry thousands of gallons of water is not practical
There are high costs for fuel cells and hydrogen production technologies
The well to wheel efficiency for hydrogen is less than 1%
e: Building fancy fuel cells and making clean hydrogen takes so much pricey equipment that high costs still slow these cars down.

q: Which of the following methods would be most accurate when determining the molecular weight of a polymer?
e: Giant polymer chains make tiny freezing changes hard to see, but osmometry easily measures their push against water to weigh them!

q: Which of the following transition metals has the smallest atomic radius?
e: Nickel has extra protons that hug its buzzing electron cloud tightly inward, pulling it into the smallest size of the bunch!

q: Ca(OH)2, NaOH, and Ba(OH)2, are all:
e: These strong bases jump into water and eagerly split completely into free ions, without leaving any unbroken molecules behind!

q: Which of the following is true regarding resistors connected in parallel to a battery?
a: Each resistor has the same current through it
Each resistor has the same voltage across it
There will be a short circuit unless the resistances are equal
e: Parallel paths give each resistor its very own direct connection to the battery, so they all share the exact same voltage!

q: As you turn on your flashlight, its lithium-ion battery begins to discharge. What happens to the electrons and ions inside the battery?
a: Both the electrons and the lithium ions move towards the cathode
Both the electrons and the lithium ions move towards the anode
The electrons move towards the cathode while the lithium ions move towards the anode
The electrons move towards the anode while the lithium ions move towards the cathode
e: When your flashlight shines, both the tiny electrons and lithium ions race together toward the cozy cathode to power your light!

q: An increase in which of the following conditions would NOT lead to an increase in pressure of a gas in a piston:
a: increased average kinetic energy of gas particles
e: Giving gas particles more room to roam lets them spread out peacefully, which lowers their bumping pressure instead of raising it.

q: Which of the following statements best explains why triethylamine [try-ethil-ah-MEEN] is more basic than ammonia?
a: Alkyl groups elevate the energy of nitrogen's nonbonding HOMO
Alkyl groups lower the energy of nitrogen's nonbonding HOMO
Alkyl groups elevate the energy of nitrogen's nonbonding LUMO
Alkyl groups lower the energy of nitrogen's nonbonding LUMO
e: Triethylamine's extra carbon branches happily push electron energy higher in nitrogen's top orbital, making it much more eager to grab protons!

q: Which of the following mixtures of solvents would have a negative deviation from Raoult's [rah-OOLZ] law?
e: Water and acetone love hugging each other through hydrogen bonds, keeping them from evaporating easily and causing a negative deviation!

q: A catalyst speeds up a chemical reaction by:
e: A catalyst shows chemical friends an easier alternate pathway to travel, helping them finish their reaction much faster!

q: A 100 gram sample of a pure compound is found to contain 3.22 moles of carbon, 16.1 moles of hydrogen, and 3.22 moles of nitrogen by elemental analysis. Which of the following statements must be true?
a: The chemical formula of the sample is C2H10N2
The empirical formula of the sample is CH5N
The chemical formula of the sample is CH5N
The empirical formula of the sample is C2H10N2
e: Dividing by the smallest amount reveals the simplest recipe, giving an empirical formula with one carbon, five hydrogens, and one nitrogen.

q: Which of the following is TRUE concerning the hydroxide ion and its sulfur-containing counterpart, hydrosulfide?
a: Hydrosulfide is more polarizable and more basic than hydroxide
Hydrosulfide is more polarizable and less basic than hydroxide
Hydrosulfide is less polarizable and less basic than hydroxide
Hydrosulfide is less polarizable and more basic than hydroxide
e: Sulfur is bigger and squishier, making hydrosulfide more polarizable, yet it holds protons more loosely, so it is less basic!

q: Which of the following functional groups is created by the addition of an alkyne [AL-kine] to Lindlar's catalyst and hydrogen gas?
e: Lindlar's gentle catalyst adds hydrogen to just one side of the triple bond, steering the molecule into a bent cis-alkene!

q: Which of the following acids is stronger than hydrofluoric acid?
e: Iodic acid lets go of its proton much more easily than hydrofluoric acid, making it the strongest acid of the group!

q: How many orbitals can have a principal quantum number of four and angular momentum quantum number of two?
e: When an electron dances with an angular number of two, it discovers five cozy orbital rooms where it can live!

q: Which of the following molecules is nonpolar?
e: Four chlorine atoms pull outward equally in all directions, keeping this balanced molecule without any positive or negative side.

q: The enthalpy in the reaction 3Q + 2R + 300 kilojoules (read as: yields) 6Y + Z is +150 kilojoules per mole of:
e: Two friendly R partners split the 300 energy snacks, giving each one an exact share of 150 kilojoules!

q: Which of the following is NOT an accurate representation of a limitation on the production and use of bioplastics?
a: Using crops to produce plastic diverts plants from the food supply
Bioplastics are unlikely to disintegrate in a landfill
Bioplastics produce a variety of pollutants when burned
Individuals at home would find it difficult to compost bioplastics
e: Plant plastics actually burn quite cleanly, so worrying about them puffing out lots of nasty pollutants isn't true.

q: What property of hydrogen makes water a good neutron moderator?
a: It has a small neutron scattering cross section
It has a large neutron scattering cross section
e: Hydrogen acts like a giant catcher's mitt with its huge scattering cross section, happily bumping speeding neutrons to slow them down!

q: Which of the following is NOT a buffering agent?
e: Rubidium hydroxide is a bully of a strong base, so it wildly swings the balance instead of buffering it steady.

q: According to molecular orbital theory, which of the following diatomic molecules is paramagnetic?
e: Two unpaired electrons hide inside oxygen, giving it a secret magnetic charm that pulls it toward magnets.

q: Which of the following uses stored electricity and is required to get a gasoline-powered car's engine going?
e: Like a tiny morning alarm, the starter motor uses battery power to crank the big engine awake!

q: Which of the following molecules is not iso-electronic with carbon monoxide?
e: Carbon monoxide and its friends share fourteen electrons, but oxygen brings sixteen, making it the odd one out.

q: Adding ethyl-magnesium bromide to which of the following would produce a tertiary [TUR-shee-ary] alcohol?
e: Ketones already hold two carbon buddies, so welcoming one more makes a proud tertiary alcohol with three!

q: Which of the following is an example of a molecular solid?
e: Unlike giant atomic webs, purple iodine crystals are built of tidy, separate little molecule pairs snuggled together.

q: Which of the following best explains the difference between real gases and ideal gases?
a: At low pressure, intermolecular attractions become significant
At high pressure, intermolecular attractions become significant
As pressure decreases, the volume of the gas itself also decreases
As pressure increases, the volume of the gas itself also increases
e: Squeezed tight under high pressure, gas particles get so close that their friendly attractions suddenly matter!

q: Which of the following instruments would most likely be used in a lab to measure the concentration of a species in aqueous [AK-wee-uhs] solutions?
e: A spectrophotometer shines friendly beams of light through a liquid to see how much colorful stuff is swimming inside.

q: Consider the first-order decomposition of N2O5 into nitrogen dioxide and oxygen. In order to get a linear fit, which of the following parameters should be graphed against time?
a: Natural log of the concentration of N2O5
One over the concentration of N2O5
e: For a first-order decay, graphing the natural log of the amount straightens out the bouncy curve into a neat line.

q: Which of the following ions has the largest polarizability?
e: Big, fluffy iodide has a huge electron cloud that squishes and wobbles far more easily than its smaller cousins!

q: Pacific Northwest National Lab scientists are depolymerizing lignin. In order to prevent the newly-cleaved lignin monomers from repolymerizing, they scavenge them with what type of molecule?
e: Friendly alcohol molecules swoop in like soft bumpers, capping the broken pieces so they cannot glue back together.

q: Which of the following is the final product of purine metabolism excreted in the urine?
e: When your body finishes recycling its old purine building blocks, it packs them up as uric acid to wash away in urine.

q: Which of the following is true of spontaneous processes at constant temperature, volume, and pressure?
a: Gibbs and Helmholtz free energies increase
Gibbs free energy increases; Helmholtz free energy decreases
Gibbs and Helmholtz free energies decrease
Gibbs free energy decreases; Helmholtz free energy increases
e: Nature loves rolling downhill, so spontaneous changes always cause both Gibbs and Helmholtz energies to tumble lower and lower.

q: Which of the following compounds is produced by the Haber process?
e: The famous Haber process hugs nitrogen and hydrogen together to build helpful ammonia molecules for plants to eat!

q: A buffered aqueous system contains 0.02 molar ammonia and 0.2 molar ammonium. Which of the following is closest to the pH of this system?
e: Having ten times more acidic ammonium pulls the normal balance down to a cozy pH of 8.3.

q: Which of the following statements best describes how chlorine adds to an alkene [al-KEEN]?
a: Both chlorine atoms add to the same carbon atom
Chlorine atoms add with syn-stereoselectivity [sin-stereo-see-lek-TIV-ih-tee] to adjacent carbon atoms
Chlorine atoms add with anti-stereoselectivity to adjacent carbon atoms
Only one chlorine atom adds to the carbon atoms
e: The two chlorine atoms sneak onto neighbor carbons from opposite sides, pulling off a clever anti-addition move!

q: Adding which of the following solutes to hexane would form a solution that most closely obeys Raoult's [rah-OOLZ] law?
e: Pentane looks and acts so much like hexane that they mingle seamlessly, following Raoult's law like identical best friends.

q: Good nucleophiles [noo-klee-uh-FYLS], which promote substitution instead of elimination reactions, tend to be which of the following?
e: Weak bases make friendly traders, gently swapping atomic spots rather than acting like bossy bullies who rip things apart.

q: Where is most of the uranium used in the United States mined?
e: Most of this special rock is dug right out of America's own backyard, keeping the fuel close to home.

q: A Buchner (read as: BYOU-kh-ner) funnel is a piece of laboratory glassware often used in chemistry labs for which of the following procedures:
e: This clever little funnel traps soggy bits on paper while letting pure liquid swoosh right through during filtration.

q: Which of the following compounds is both a hydrogen bond donor and a hydrogen bond acceptor?
e: Ammonia is the ultimate friend, happily giving away a hydrogen hug with one hand while grabbing another with its spare pair!

q: Which of the following statements is TRUE about boiling points?
a: The presence of a non-volatile solute decreases the boiling point of a liquid
A liquid in a vacuum has a higher boiling point than at atmospheric pressure
A boiling point can be reduced below the triple point
The boiling point cannot be increased above the critical point
e: Past the critical point, liquid and gas merge into one mystery soup, so water can never boil again.

q: Soapy water is better at cleaning surfaces than plain water is because the soap changes what property of the water?
e: Soap gently relaxes water's tight skin, called surface tension, letting the water spread out flat and wash away dirt.

q: A consortium of Department of Energy labs is working to create carbon-free hydrogen fuel cells for heavy-duty vehicles. These fuel cells produce what chemical byproduct as exhaust?
e: When clean hydrogen powers these mighty engines, the only little puff left behind in the exhaust pipe is pure water!

q: The solubility of a gaseous solute in a liquid solvent is typically expressed in units of concentration. Which of the following factors does NOT affect the solubility of a gas in a liquid?
a: Polarity of solvent and solute molecules
e: A giant bucket holds more water, but it cannot change how easily gas molecules dissolve into each tiny drop.

q: The PH3 molecule has what type of molecular geometry?
e: With three little legs tucked underneath and a cloud sitting on top, this molecule balances like a tiny three-sided pyramid!

q: Which of the following molecules has an electron pair geometry that matches its molecular geometry:
e: Because all five chlorine friends hold hands with phosphorus and leave no lonely pairs behind, its two shapes match perfectly.

q: In titration, which of the following is most commonly used as an acid-base indicator in the pH 8 to pH 10 range?
e: Phenolphthalein is a magical color-changer that wakes up and turns bright pink right between pH eight and ten.

q: Which of the following is NOT generally true of reaction equilibria:
a: if the temperature of an exothermic reaction is raised, the equilibrium shifts to the left
the equilibrium constants for forward and reverse reactions are the reciprocals of each other
pure liquids appear in the equilibrium expression but pure solids do not
an equilibrium constant greater than 1 means that the reaction favors products at equilibrium
e: Pure liquids stay so packed and steady that chemists leave them completely out of balance equations, just like pure solids.

q: According to the kinetic theory of ideal gases, the molecules of an ideal gas in a container do which of the following?
a: Collide with the wall of the container and bounce back
Collide with the container wall and stick to it
Undergo collision among themselves and with the container wall, until their speed reduces to zero
Remain fixed until the container is opened
e: Gas particles are like tireless bouncy balls, zipping around and bouncing right off the walls without ever slowing down!

q: Analysis of which of the following isotopes is most commonly used because it gives the BEST indication of historical temperatures at different latitudes worldwide:
e: Tiny oxygen atoms trap chilly ancient secrets in old ice, showing us just how warm or frosty Earth was long ago.

q: Which of the following one-to-one solutions of liquids would be expected to show the most deviation from Raoult's Law's prediction of vapor pressure?
a: A mixture of water and ethanol
A mixture of pentane and hexane
A mixture of water and cyclohexanol
A mixture of acetone and chloroform
e: Water and ethanol love to tangle and pull in surprising ways, breaking the usual rules and dodging normal pressure predictions.

q: Hydraulic fracturing is used to obtain which of the following resources?
e: Blasting water deep underground cracks ancient rocks open, freeing hidden natural gas so it can rush up to the surface.

q: What is the coordination number of a body-centered cubic lattice?
e: Imagine a tiny dancer in the center of a box, holding hands with eight corner friends all at once.

q: Which of the following percentages is closest to the level of engine efficiency in a modern gasoline-burning automobile?
e: Most energy escapes as noisy heat, leaving just a helpful quarter of each drop to actually turn your car's wheels.

q: What type of interaction dominates between polar molecules?
e: Polar molecules act like cheerful little magnets, using dipole-dipole hugs where their plus and minus ends stick happily together.

q: An organic compound is considered an alcohol if it has what functional group?
e: An alcohol gets its bubbly personality from a hydroxyl group, where oxygen and hydrogen hold hands like best friends.

q: The lines in the visible region of the hydrogen spectrum are known as the:
e: When excited hydrogen glows with colorful light our eyes can see, it lights up the magical Balmer series!

q: Which of the following statements concerning pressure-temperature phase diagrams is NOT TRUE?
a: The slope of the liquid-solid coexistence curve is positive if the solid floats on the liquid
Fluids at a pressure above the critical pressure cannot be boiled
Gases are found in the low-pressure, high-temperature regime
It is not possible for four phases of the same substance to be in equilibrium
e: If an ice cube floats, its melting line tilts backward with a negative slope, not a positive one.

q: If molten sodium is burned in a pure oxygen atmosphere, a salt is formed. Which of the following is the likely identity of this salt?
e: When melted sodium meets plenty of pure oxygen, they throw a fiery party to create sodium peroxide, Na2O2.

q: Which of the following methods is LEAST helpful in identifying chiral [KYE-ruhl] isomers?
e: Mirror-twin molecules weigh the exact same, so a quadrupole mass spectrometer cannot tell them apart just by weighing them.

q: Which of the following will generally cause the kinetics of a reaction to increase?
e: Heating things up makes molecules dance faster and bump into each other, speeding up the whole reaction.

q: Which of the following molecules exhibits a dipole moment:
e: Because H2S is bent like a tiny boomerang, its electrical charges stay uneven, giving it a dipole moment.

q: Which of the following represents a chemical property of sodium?
a: It is less dense than water
It has a melting point of 98.7 degrees Celsius
It reacts with water to release hydrogen gas
When cut with a knife, it has a shiny surface with a metallic luster
e: Fizzing in water to create hydrogen gas is a chemical property because sodium transforms into completely new things.

q: Which of the following is a molecule with a square pyramidal molecular geometry around its central atom:
e: With five fluorine friends and one hidden electron pair, ClF5 builds a neat square pyramid.

q: The International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor, commonly called ITER [eat-er] has been designed to produce 500 million watts of output power and is currently scheduled to begin plasma experiments in 2020. What type of nuclear fusion method will ITER utilize, once completed?
e: ITER uses invisible magnetic confinement to bottle up super-hot plasma like a tiny, captured star.

q: Which of the following molecules can ionize in water?
e: In water, friendly acetic acid gladly gives away a proton, breaking apart to form charged ions.

q: Which of the following is a product from a hydrogen fuel reaction?
e: When hydrogen fuel burns cleanly with oxygen, the only sweet thing left behind is pure water!

q: Which of the following statements is NOT true regarding colligative [koh-LIG-ah-tiv] properties?
a: They do not depend on the identity of the solute
Sodium chloride has a van't Hoff factor less than one
The osmotic pressure of a solution increases with increasing solute concentration
The freezing point of a solution decreases with increasing solute concentration
e: Salt splits into two swimming ions in water, so its van't Hoff number is around two, never under one.

q: If l = 3, what are the minimum and maximum allowed values of the magnetic quantum number (ml) [M-L], respectively?
e: When quantum number l is three, its magnetic buddy ml can roam all the way from minus three to three.

q: Consider the following reaction: 5H2O(l)+ S2O32- + 4Cl2 (aq) [yields] 8Cl-(aq) + 2SO42-(aq) + 10H+. What is the oxidizing agent in this reaction?
e: Chlorine gas eagerly steals electrons to become chloride, making it the busy oxidizing agent in this reaction.

q: What is the local VSEPR geometry of a fully substituted carbonyl carbon?
e: A carbonyl carbon spreads its three connected atoms out flat like a triangle, making it trigonal planar.

q: Which of the following countries was NOT a major petroleum exporter to the United States in 2015?
e: Due to strict trade rules, Iran was not sending oil shipments to power American cars in 2015.

q: Which of the following is an isotope that has attracted recent interest in terms of developing a new generation of cleaner, proliferation-resistant nuclear power?
e: Thorium-232 is an exciting fuel for future power plants because it makes clean energy without dangerous bomb materials.

q: Which of the following is TRUE about the solubility of a gas in water?
a: It increases as both temperature and partial pressure of the gas rise
It increases as temperature rises but decreases as partial pressure of the gas rises
It decreases as temperature rises but increases as partial pressure of the gas rises
It decreases as both temperature and partial pressure of the gas rise
e: Pressing down on a gas pushes it into water, but warmth gives bubbles energy to break free and escape.

q: Lithium aluminum hydride would likely be used by a synthetic chemist for what type of reaction?
e: Lithium aluminum hydride is a generous giver of electrons, making it perfect for powering a reduction reaction.

q: Which of the following types of fuel cell is most commonly used in vehicles?
e: Cars love polymer electrolyte membrane fuel cells because they wake up fast and stay nice and cool.

q: Which of the following species has an unpaired electron, according to the VSEPR [ves-per] model?
e: With forty-three total valence electrons, this busy molecule has an odd count, leaving one lonely electron without a dance partner!

q: Which of the following statements does NOT describe a molecule in an octahedral arrangement?
a: Two-fold, three-fold, and four-fold rotation axes can all be found
Two different types of improper rotations can be found
Exactly eight different mirror planes can be found
e: This super-symmetric shape loves mirrors so much that it actually hides nine reflective planes inside, not just eight.

q: As a multiple of the gas constant, which of the following represents the change in entropy for the reversible isothermal expansion of a mole of ideal gas doubling in volume?
e: When gas doubles its playground, its messy freedom grows by the natural log of two multiplied by the gas constant.

q: Which of the following materials is a common catalyst in commercial polymer electrolyte membrane fuel cells?
e: Shiny platinum acts like an eager helper, speeding up chemical reactions inside the fuel cell without ever wearing out.

q: Which of the following is a nonpolar molecule:
e: Carbon dioxide sits in a straight line, so its oxygen atoms pull electrons equally in opposite directions, balancing out completely.

q: Which of the following is the correct definition of molality?
a: Kilograms of solute per liter of solvent
Moles of solute per liter of solution
Moles of solute per liter of solvent
Moles of solute per kilogram of solvent
e: Molality measures how many tiny packets of dissolved stuff are packed into each kilogram of pure liquid solvent.

q: The molar heat of vaporization for water at its boiling point and in kilojoules per mole is:
e: Each mole of bubbling water needs forty point seven kilojoules of heat energy to break free and become steam.

q: Which of the following is the most common linkage between successive monomers in cellulose?
e: Sugar building blocks hold hands in sturdy beta-one, four bonds, creating tough, straight fibers that help tall plants stand proud.

q: Consider the closed equilibrium [ee-kwuh-LIB-ree-uhm] system of calcium carbonate, carbon dioxide, and water, which yields calcium ions and bicarbonate ions. Adding sodium bicarbonate to the solution will make which of the following true in the reaction?
a: Q will be greater than K
Q will be less than K
Q will be equal to K
e: Dumping extra product into the mix tips the balance, making the reaction quotient Q bigger than the calm equilibrium constant K.

q: Which of the following is one of the factors that determine the bonding between atoms in a solid?
a: Magnitude of the electronegativities of the atoms
e: How greedily each atom tugs on shared electrons decides whether they share nicely or steal, shaping the solid's bonds.

q: Which of the following is the full list of products produced by the mild heating of sodium bicarbonate at temperatures of about 80 degrees Celsius?
a: Sodium carbonate, water, and carbon dioxide
e: Gentle heat coaxes baking soda to split into powdery sodium carbonate, steamy water, and bubbling carbon dioxide gas.

q: Which of the following is a molecule having a nonpolar covalent bond:
e: Two identical bromine twins tug on their shared electrons with equal strength, creating a perfectly balanced bond.

q: Charles law is particularly useful in explaining which of the following:
a: dry air is more dense than humid air
CO2 escapes from a bottle of soda when opened
the change in enthalpy when nitrogen and oxygen react to form nitrogen dioxide
a hot-air balloon rises when the air in the balloon is heated
e: Warming up the trapped air makes it puff out and expand, helping a majestic balloon float up toward the clouds!

q: Which of the following is a polar, aprotic solvent?
e: Dimethyl sulfoxide has friendly positive and negative sides, but keeps all its hydrogen atoms tucked safely away.

q: Which of the following is NOT true:
a: any foreign substance added to water will cause a freezing point drop
a nonvolatile solute raises the boiling point of a solvent
methane has a higher boiling point than ethane
freezing point depression is a colligative property
e: Tiny methane has weaker attractions than heavier ethane, so it actually boils and drifts away at a much colder temperature.

q: The convex meniscus of mercury in a capillary tube indicates which of the following?
a: Mercury is highly attracted to glass
Mercury's cohesion is greater than its adhesion
e: Shiny mercury droplets love hugging each other far more than touching the glass, so they curve inward like a little dome.

q: At which of the following pH values is zinc hydroxide likely to be most soluble?
e: Zinc hydroxide dissolves best at a strong, acidic pH of two, where hungry acid quickly gobbles up its hydroxide parts.

q: A student isolates a natural product from a tropical frog and takes a proton NMR in deuterated chloroform. They notice that there is a sharp peak at 10.5 parts per million in the compound. This suggests the presence of what functional group?
e: That bright signal at ten point five ppm is the cheerful calling card of an aldehyde proton saying hello.

q: Consider an arbitrary acid HA [H- A], where A can be any group. Which of the following facts would allow one to directly infer that it is a stronger acid than acetic acid?
a: H-A has the ability to protonate water in high yield
Acetic acid has the ability to protonate H-A in high yield
H-A has the ability to protonate acetate in high yield
Acetic acid has the ability to protonate A- in high yield
e: If an acid easily gifts its proton to acetate, it proves it is stronger and more generous than acetic acid.

q: Which of the following compounds is NOT named CORRECTLY?
e: Because iron here carries a plus-two charge instead of plus-three, its true old-fashioned name is ferrous oxide, not ferric.

q: Scientists at SLAC National Accelerator Lab are shooting femtosecond electron pulses at samples and measuring their diffraction signals with time resolution. Which of the following phenomena is best probed by this type of experiment?
e: Taking super-fast snapshots lets scientists watch atoms dance as reactions happen, catching chemical kinetics right in the middle of all the action!

q: Which of the following elements has the valence electron configuration of 3s23p3?
e: Phosphorus has five busy outer electrons twirling in its third shell, matching that 3s2 3p3 pattern perfectly.

q: Lipstick is known to be a suspension of high molecular weight hydrocarbons, waxes, and other ingredients. Which of the following choices does NOT describe lipstick composition?
a: Castor oil may be a dispersing agent
Beeswax is sometimes used as a stiffening agent
Metal ions such as Nickel(II) [nickel two] are the basis for lipstick dyes
Carbon soot is typically used as a coloring agent
e: Nobody wants dirty chimney soot on their lips! Makeup makers use pretty, colorful ingredients instead of messy carbon soot.

q: In order to find the heat of reaction, or delta H naught, for a reaction using standard enthalpies of formation, the working formula is:
a: delta H products minus delta H reactants
delta H reactants minus delta H products
delta H reactants plus delta H products
delta H products plus delta H reactants
e: To see heat changes, you just take the final products and subtract the starting reactants, like checking your score at the finish line.

q: Dalton's gas law applies primarily to:
e: When different gases throw a party together in one balloon, Dalton's law adds up each gas mixture's pushy little pressure.

q: Fuel cells operating on methanol and air produce heat, electricity, and which of the following?
e: While making electricity, this clever engine breathes out harmless water and carbon dioxide, like two quiet puffs of exhaust.

q: Which of the following is not a Lewis acid?
e: Ammonia carries an extra pair of electrons it loves to share, making it a friendly giver instead of a Lewis acid taker!

q: What is the process by which lithium enters electrodes in a lithium-ion battery?
e: Tiny lithium ions neatly slide between layers like books onto a shelf, a cozy process called intercalation.

q: In a breath analyzer, what color change occurs in a potassium dichromate solution in the presence of alcohol?
e: Touching alcohol makes the liquid trade its sunny orange-yellow glow for a bold green to show what it caught!

q: Which of the following is considered a strong acid?
e: Nitric acid is a champion that breaks apart completely in water, tossing all its protons into the pool without holding back!

q: Which of the following adjectives describes the reaction of a strong base with a strong acid?
e: When an acid and a base clash, they cancel each other out into harmless water and salt in a friendly neutralization.

q: Which of the following statements is usually TRUE about an unsaturated fatty acid?
a: It is from vegetable sources and is solid at room temperature
It is from vegetable sources and is liquid at room temperature
It is from animal sources and is solid at room temperature
It is from animal sources and is liquid at room temperature
e: Unsaturated oils from plants have bendy shapes that stop them from freezing solid, so they stay runny liquids at room temperature.

q: Which of the following compounds contains bonds with the most ionic character?
e: Lithium gladly hands its electron over to greedy chlorine, making lithium chloride lock together with super strong ionic bonds.

q: One hundred millimoles of each of the following compounds is dissolved in a liter of water. Which of them will produce the solution of lowest ionic resistance ?
e: Hydrochloric acid splits completely into swimming ions, letting electricity zoom right through with the lowest resistance!

q: Which of the following substances could be a precipitate in a double replacement reaction in an aqueous solution?
e: Silver chloride refuses to dissolve in water, clumping together like tiny white snowflakes that sink straight to the bottom.

q: Which of the following molecules is classified as an arene [AIR-een]?
e: Benzene is a famous arene that holds hands in a flat, super-stable ring of six carbon atoms sharing their electrons.

q: What component is required for a gasoline combustion engine but is unnecessary for a diesel engine?
e: Gasoline engines rely on a spark plug to start the fire, but diesel squeezes its air until it bursts into flame all alone.

q: Hydrogen gas effuses through a pinhole opening from one compartment to another about how many times as fast as nitrogen gas:
e: Feathery light hydrogen sneaks through a tiny pinhole about 3.7 times as fast as heavier, slower nitrogen gas!

q: When plotting the temperature dependence of volume for a sample of an ideal gas on a graph, the slope of the line is most dependent on what aspect of the sample?
e: The amount of gas determines the slope, because packing in more particles means the gas expands way more as it warms.

q: Which of the following is a tertiary alcohol:
e: In 2-methyl-2-propanol, the alcohol group attaches to a central carbon that is surrounded by three other carbon buddies.

q: Which of the following molecules contains the most electron-rich carbon center?
e: In methane, friendly hydrogen buddies gladly share their electrons with carbon, making it the richest little atom on the playground.

q: What is the oxidation state of nitrogen in nitric acid?
e: Three hungry oxygens hog so many shared electrons in nitric acid that poor nitrogen is left with a bright plus five charge.

q: Powerful X-ray technology developed at DOE national laboratories is revealing new insights into diseases ranging from Alzheimer's to swine flu. This X-ray crystallography [kris-tl-OG-ruh-fee] has been used for all EXCEPT which of the following?
a: Revealing the structures of diseased and disease-causing molecules
Creating three-dimensional maps of mutated enzymes
Producing scattered, low intensity X-ray beams to surround the surface of the molecules
Allowing medical researchers to develop drugs to prevent mutated enzymes from triggering cancer cells
e: Scientists need brilliant, super-strong X-rays to snap clear portraits of tiny molecules, not weak, scattered beams that merely wander around the outside!

q: What element has the highest ionization energy?
e: Tiny helium hugs its two electrons so close to its heart that pulling one away takes more energy than any other atom!

q: Which of the following best describes the incident and exit beams in attenuated total reflectance spectroscopy?
a: Incident beam is photons and exit beam is electrons
Incident and exit beams are ions
Incident and exit beams are photons
Incident and exit beams are electrons
e: This clever trick shines a beam of light in and catches it coming out, and light is made entirely of bouncing photons.

q: Under aqueous conditions, which of the following reactions would generate a precipitate?
a: Ammonium chloride mixed with potassium hydroxide
Calcium chloride mixed with potassium nitrate
Calcium carbonate mixed with hydrochloric acid
Barium chloride mixed with potassium sulfate
e: When barium meets sulfate, they lock hands so tightly they fall out of the water like solid white snowflakes.

q: Which of the following benzene derivatives contains an amino group?
e: Picture a benzene ring putting on a cozy little amino group backpack—that stylish molecule is called aniline!

q: Which of the following elements possesses the largest first ionization energy?
e: With its cozy shell completely full, neon clings to its electrons tighter than any of its neighbors, stubbornly refusing to let go.

q: Determine the solubility product constant (or Ksp) of silver bromide, given that its molar solubility is 5.71 10-7 moles per liter.
e: When silver bromide splits up, multiplying its dissolved partner ions together gives that teeny-tiny number: 3.26 times ten to the negative thirteen.

q: Which of the following devices stores electrical energy in chemical form in order to release it slowly through a circuit?
e: A battery packs electrical energy into cozy chemical jars, ready to wake up and gently power your flashlight on demand.

q: Which of the following compounds is generally considered soluble in water?
e: Sodium nitrate loves water so much that its friendly ions happily scatter into the pool, dissolving without leaving a single trace!

q: According to Lewis theory, which of the following conditions would most accelerate an acid-base reaction?
a: An elevated HOMO [HO-mo] and a depressed LUMO [LOO-mo]
An elevated HOMO and an elevated LUMO
A depressed HOMO and an elevated LUMO
A depressed HOMO and a depressed LUMO
e: Reactions zoom fastest when the giver holds electrons high up and the receiver sits down low, creating an easy downhill slide.

q: Which of the following sets are all strong electrolytes?
a: Hydrogen chloride, phosphoric acid, acetic acid
Hydrogen chloride, sodium hydroxide, phosphoric acid, potassium hydroxide
Hydrogen iodide, hydrogen bromide, lithium hydroxide, nitric acid
Ammonia, potassium hydroxide, sodium hydroxide, lithium hydroxide
e: Every champion in this group completely breaks apart into eager ions in water, letting electricity zoom right through without stopping.

q: Which of the following statements regarding geometric or cis-trans isomers is NOT true:
a: they have the same molecular formula
they have the same order of attachment of atoms
they have the same orientation around a double bond
they have the same functional groups
e: These molecular twins share the same parts, but they point in totally different directions across that stiff double bond.

q: In atomic orbital overlap, which of the following is true of destructive interference?
a: It gives a bonding orbital and no nodes
It gives an antibonding orbital and a node parallel to the internuclear axis
It gives an antibonding orbital and a node perpendicular to the internuclear axis
It gives an antibonding orbital and no nodes
e: When atomic waves cancel each other out, they create an unhappy antibonding zone with a dividing wall right between the atoms.

q: Of which of the following acid-base titrations would the pH be less than 7 at the equivalence point?
e: A mighty strong acid easily overpowers a gentle weak base, leaving the final mixture slightly sour with a pH below seven.

q: What stress applied to an equilibrium [ee-kwuh-LIB-ree- uhm] causes the equilibrium to shift to the side with fewer moles of gas?
e: When you squeeze a gas with extra pressure, the crowded molecules pack onto the side with fewer gas particles to save space.

q: The following gases are all at standard temperature and pressure. Which of the following gases will have the fastest root mean square speed?
e: Because helium is the lightest featherweight of the bunch, it zips across the room faster than all its heavier gas friends!

q: In addition to the "sniff test", which of the following is a standard laboratory test for a sulfide, such as hydrogen sulfide gas:
a: the gas passed over a filter paper soaked in colorless lead nitrate turns the paper brown
when inserted into a flame, a glowing wooden splint bursts into flames
a flame test gives off a deep purple color
e: Stinky sulfide gas loves meeting lead on paper, quickly painting it brown to reveal the hidden smelly visitor!

q: What is the primary advantage of using cellulosic feedstocks over crops like corn to produce ethanol?
a: The enzymes that produce cellulosic ethanol are cheap and plentiful
There are more cellulosic ethanol plants than corn ethanol plants
Waste products can be used as cellulosic feedstocks
Cellulosic ethanol production does not require government subsidies to be economically competitive
e: Instead of using up food like corn, we can magically turn leftover plant stalks and trash into clean, useful fuel.

q: Fluid pressure is caused by which of the following?
a: Gravitational interactions among atoms and molecules of the fluid
Collisions of fast moving atoms and molecules of the fluid
e: Tiny, bouncy molecules zoom around like bumper cars, and their energetic bumping creates fluid pressure against the walls!

q: Which of the following is an insoluble base?
e: While friendly bases happily dissolve in water, stubborn magnesium hydroxide refuses to break apart and stays solid.

q: Effective nuclear charge is BEST described by which of the following?
a: It is the charge on the nucleus experienced by an electron when accounting for the shielding effect of other electrons
It is the amount of energy required to remove an electron from the valence shell when the atom is in a gaseous state
It is the energy released when a proton is added to the nucleus
It is the number of electrons that penetrate the nucleus
e: Effective nuclear charge is the pull an outer electron actually feels when pushy inner electrons block the center's hug.

q: Which of the following is the purpose of a fuel cell stack in a fuel cell vehicle?
a: Store hydrogen gas compressed at extremely high pressure to increase driving range
Store energy generated from regenerative braking
Convert hydrogen and oxygen gas into electricity to power the electric motor
e: The fuel cell stack acts like a little power plant, teaming up hydrogen and oxygen to make electricity that drives the car!

q: Which of the following best explains why propane is stored in liquid form rather than as a gas?
a: It is less flammable as a liquid
It takes up much less space as a liquid
It is easier to burn as a liquid
It is a liquid at room temperature
e: Squishing propane gas into a liquid lets us pack way more fuel into a tank, because liquids take up much less room!

q: What is the formula of the ionic compound composed of the zinc cation [CAT-eye-on] and sulfite anion [AN-eye-on]?
e: Zinc brings a positive two charge while sulfite brings a negative two charge, neatly balancing out into ZnSO3.

q: What is the typical co-electrolyte in Vanadium [vah-NAY-dee-um] redox [REE-dox] flow batteries?
e: Sulfuric acid acts like a helpful river inside the battery, letting vanadium ions swim along to deliver their electric power.

q: With regard to the Rosenmund reduction, which of the following functional group pairs corresponds to the reactant and product, respectively?
e: In this clever chemical makeover, an acyl chloride molecule gets trimmed down to become a brand new aldehyde!

q: Which of the following most accurately describes an advantage of a nuclear fusion reactor over a nuclear fission reactor?
a: A failure of control systems shuts down the fusion reactor
Fusion based nuclear plants are much less expensive than fission plants
Fusion reactors operate at a lower temperature than fission reactors
The fuel rods in the fusion reactor can be reused
e: Fusion is like a finicky campfire. If the controls ever fail, it instantly cools down and safely turns itself off!

q: A student is using mass spectrometry to identify an unknown sample of rock. Which of the following does mass spectrometry not directly quantify?
a: Mass to charge ratio of ions
e: A mass spectrometer acts like a super-sensitive scale for weighing particles, so it cannot tell you about a material's polarity.
